After Chaco's decline people drew together into large, tightly packed towns, many of them tucked into canyon alcoves - the cliff dwellings of Mesa Verde and Canyon de Chelly belong to this time. Defensive placement, towers and reservoirs suggest competition for land and water. By about 1300 the Four Corners country was emptied entirely, its inhabitants moving south and east in one of the great migrations of North American history.
Pueblo III (United States, AD 1150–AD 13.source: Colorado prehistory : a context for the Southern Colorado River Basin

Basketmaker II (United States, 999 BC–AD.label: Basketmaker II
Basketmaker II (United States, 999 BC–AD.prose:
[Southwestern Colorado / San Juan Basin, 999 BC–AD 500] Basketmaker II. Period definition from Colorado prehistory : a context for the Southern Colorado River Basin — 1999.

Early farming communities of the Colorado Plateau, growing maize and squash while still hunting with the atlatl and gathering wild plants. They stored grain in slab-lined cists, lived in shallow pithouses and rockshelters, and produced the superb coiled baskets and sandals — preserved in dry caves — that give the period its name. Pottery and the bow had not yet arrived.
Basketmaker II (United States, 999 BC–AD.source: Colorado prehistory : a context for the Southern Colorado River Basin

Basketmaker III (United States, AD 500–A.label: Basketmaker III
Basketmaker III (United States, AD 500–A.prose:
[Southwestern Colorado / San Juan Basin, AD 500–AD 750] Basketmaker III. Period definition from Colorado prehistory : a context for the Southern Colorado River Basin — 1999.

Pottery arrives in quantity, the bow and arrow replaces the atlatl, and beans join maize in the diet, allowing bigger and more permanent settlements. People lived in deep pithouses clustered into hamlets, often with an oversized structure for communal use that foreshadows the later kiva. These villages are the direct foundation of the Pueblo world that followed.
Basketmaker III (United States, AD 500–A.source: Colorado prehistory : a context for the Southern Colorado River Basin

Pueblo II (United States, AD 900–AD 1150.label: Pueblo II
Pueblo II (United States, AD 900–AD 1150.prose:
[Southwestern Colorado / San Juan Basin, AD 900–AD 1150] Pueblo II. Period definition from Colorado prehistory : a context for the Southern Colorado River Basin — 1999.

The era of Chaco Canyon, when massive multi-storey great houses, great kivas and a network of engineered roads linked communities across tens of thousands of square miles. Small farmsteads spread over almost every arable pocket of the Colorado Plateau, tied to regional centres by shared architecture and ritual. Trade brought turquoise, macaws and copper bells from as far as Mesoamerica.
Pueblo II (United States, AD 900–AD 1150.source: Colorado prehistory : a context for the Southern Colorado River Basin

Pueblo I (United States, AD 750–AD 900).label: Pueblo I
Pueblo I (United States, AD 750–AD 900).prose:
[Southwestern Colorado / San Juan Basin, AD 750–AD 900] Pueblo I. Period definition from Colorado prehistory : a context for the Southern Colorado River Basin — 1999.

Farming families across the Colorado Plateau moved out of scattered pithouses into rows of aboveground rooms built of jacal and stone, clustered into the first true villages. Populations grew fast, some settlements reaching hundreds of people, and pottery, turkey-keeping and bean cultivation spread. Many of these villages were short-lived, breaking up and reforming elsewhere - a pattern of movement that would define Puebloan history.
Pueblo I (United States, AD 750–AD 900).source: Colorado prehistory : a context for the Southern Colorado River Basin

Etruscan (Italy, 615 BC–508 BC).label: Etruscan
Etruscan (Italy, 615 BC–508 BC).prose:
[pre-Roman Italy, 615 BC–508 BC] Etruscan. "Etruscans" entry. Period definition from The Oxford classical dictionary. — 2003.

The years of Etruscan dominance over Rome, when the city was ruled by kings of the Tarquin line and transformed from a cluster of hill villages into a genuine urban centre with drained marshland, a paved Forum and a great temple on the Capitol. Etruscan craftsmen, engineers and religious practices, from divination by entrails to the alphabet itself, shaped Roman institutions permanently. Tradition ends the era with the expulsion of Tarquinius Superbus and the founding of the Republic.

Aksumite (Ethiopia, AD 300–AD 700).label: Aksumite
Aksumite (Ethiopia, AD 300–AD 700).prose:
[Ethiopia and Eritrea, AD 300–AD 700] Aksumite. Spatial coverage: Eritrea, Ethiopia. Derived from Cerulli 1968. Period definition from Beta maṣāḥǝft: Manuscripts of Ethiopia and Eritrea — Alessandro Bausi, 2017.

From a highland capital in northern Ethiopia, Aksum controlled the Red Sea trade in ivory, gold and incense, minted its own gold, silver and bronze coinage, and traded with Rome, Arabia and India. King Ezana adopted Christianity in the fourth century, making Aksum one of the earliest Christian states and founding the church that still shapes Ethiopian life. The giant carved stelae over royal tombs, some over thirty metres tall, remain the most striking monuments of the kingdom, which later lost ground as Islamic powers took over Red Sea commerce.
Aksumite (Ethiopia, AD 300–AD 700).source: Beta maṣāḥǝft: Manuscripts of Ethiopia and Eritrea

Postaksumite I (Ethiopia, AD 1200–AD 143.label: Postaksumite I
Postaksumite I (Ethiopia, AD 1200–AD 143.prose:
[Ethiopia and Eritrea, AD 1200–AD 1433] Postaksumite I. Spatial coverage: Eritrea, Ethiopia. Derived from Cerulli 1968. Period definition from Beta maṣāḥǝft: Manuscripts of Ethiopia and Eritrea — Alessandro Bausi, 2017.

Centuries after Aksum's decline, the Christian highland state re-formed further south: the Zagwe kings cut the rock-hewn churches of Lalibela out of living stone, and from 1270 the Solomonic dynasty claimed descent from Solomon and Sheba to legitimise its rule. Kings such as Amda Seyon campaigned against neighbouring Muslim sultanates over the trade routes to the Red Sea, and the court moved with the army rather than sitting in a fixed capital. Monasteries became the main producers of manuscripts, painting and the chronicles on which Ethiopian history is built.
Postaksumite I (Ethiopia, AD 1200–AD 143.source: Beta maṣāḥǝft: Manuscripts of Ethiopia and Eritrea

Postaksumite II (Ethiopia, AD 1434–AD 16.label: Postaksumite II
Postaksumite II (Ethiopia, AD 1434–AD 16.prose:
[Ethiopia and Eritrea, AD 1434–AD 1632] Postaksumite II. Spatial coverage: Eritrea, Ethiopia. Derived from Cerulli 1968. Period definition from Beta maṣāḥǝft: Manuscripts of Ethiopia and Eritrea — Alessandro Bausi, 2017.

Power in the Ethiopian highlands rested with the Solomonic kings, who ruled from mobile tented camps rather than fixed capitals, while monasteries and rock-cut and built churches anchored Christian life in the countryside. The period was torn open by the invasion of Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Ghazi in the 1520s-40s, which destroyed churches and treasuries across the plateau and drew in Portuguese musketeers on the emperors' side. Jesuit missionaries followed, until their expulsion and the restoration of the Orthodox faith closed the era just before Gondar was founded as a permanent royal city.
Postaksumite II (Ethiopia, AD 1434–AD 16.source: Beta maṣāḥǝft: Manuscripts of Ethiopia and Eritrea

Zamana Masāfǝnt (Ethiopia, AD 1769–AD 18.label: Zamana Masāfǝnt
Zamana Masāfǝnt (Ethiopia, AD 1769–AD 18.prose:
[Ethiopia and Eritrea, AD 1769–AD 1855] Zamana Masāfǝnt. Spatial coverage: Eritrea, Ethiopia. Derived from Cerulli 1968. Period definition from Beta maṣāḥǝft: Manuscripts of Ethiopia and Eritrea — Alessandro Bausi, 2017.

Ethiopian emperors at Gondar were reduced to figureheads while regional warlords, above all the Yejju Oromo rulers of Begemder, fought each other for the position of ras and controlled the throne. Provinces went their own way, trade routes were disrupted and the church split over doctrinal disputes. The fragmentation ended when Tewodros II defeated the great lords and reunified the empire by force.
Zamana Masāfǝnt (Ethiopia, AD 1769–AD 18.source: Beta maṣāḥǝft: Manuscripts of Ethiopia and Eritrea

Modern Period (Ethiopia, AD 1855–AD 1974.label: Modern Period
Modern Period (Ethiopia, AD 1855–AD 1974.prose:
[Ethiopia and Eritrea, AD 1855–AD 1974] Modern Period. Spatial coverage: Eritrea, Ethiopia. Derived from Cerulli 1968. Period definition from Beta maṣāḥǝft: Manuscripts of Ethiopia and Eritrea — Alessandro Bausi, 2017.

Crete entered the century in political limbo, an autonomous state under great-power supervision, and was formally joined to Greece in 1913. German paratroopers seized the island in the fierce battle of 1941, and the brutal occupation and mountain resistance that followed are still central to local memory. Since the 1960s mass tourism and intensive olive and greenhouse agriculture have reshaped the coast, while excavation at Knossos, Phaistos and elsewhere turned the Minoan past into a national and international symbol.
Modern Period (Ethiopia, AD 1855–AD 1974.source: Beta maṣāḥǝft: Manuscripts of Ethiopia and Eritrea

Gondarine (Ethiopia, AD 1632–AD 1769).label: Gondarine
Gondarine (Ethiopia, AD 1632–AD 1769).prose:
[Ethiopia and Eritrea, AD 1632–AD 1769] Gondarine. Spatial coverage: Eritrea, Ethiopia. Derived from Cerulli 1968. Period definition from Beta maṣāḥǝft: Manuscripts of Ethiopia and Eritrea — Alessandro Bausi, 2017.

For the first time in centuries Ethiopian emperors stopped moving with a mobile camp and built a permanent capital, ringing Fasil Ghebbi with stone castles, churches and baths. The court sponsored a brilliant school of manuscript illumination and church wall painting, hosted Jesuit-influenced architecture and fierce theological disputes over the nature of Christ, and drew trade from the Red Sea. Royal power then drained away to regional warlords, opening the long era of princes.
Gondarine (Ethiopia, AD 1632–AD 1769).source: Beta maṣāḥǝft: Manuscripts of Ethiopia and Eritrea

South-Arabian, Pre-Aksumite and Proto-Ak.label: South-Arabian, Pre-Aksumite and Proto-Aksumite
South-Arabian, Pre-Aksumite and Proto-Ak.prose:
[Ethiopia and Eritrea, 999 BC–AD 1] South-Arabian, Pre-Aksumite and Proto-Aksumite. Spatial coverage: Eritrea, Ethiopia. This definition was not derived from Cerulli 1968, but provided directly by Bausi. Period definition from Beta maṣāḥǝft: Manuscripts of Ethiopia and Eritrea — Alessandro Bausi, 2017.

Highland Ethiopia and Eritrea drew close to the Sabaean world across the Red Sea, producing the polity known as D'MT with monumental stone temples at Yeha, South Arabian script and inscriptions, and altars to the moon god Almaqah. Local traditions persisted alongside imported forms, and after D'MT's decline smaller chiefdoms coalesced. Out of them grew Aksum, whose kings would dominate the region and its Red Sea trade.
South-Arabian, Pre-Aksumite and Proto-Ak.source: Beta maṣāḥǝft: Manuscripts of Ethiopia and Eritrea

Early Aksumite (Ethiopia, AD 1–AD 300).label: Early Aksumite
Early Aksumite (Ethiopia, AD 1–AD 300).prose:
[Ethiopia and Eritrea, AD 1–AD 300] Early Aksumite. Spatial coverage: Eritrea, Ethiopia. This definition was not derived from Cerulli 1968, but provided directly by Bausi. Period definition from Beta maṣāḥǝft: Manuscripts of Ethiopia and Eritrea — Alessandro Bausi, 2017.

A highland kingdom in northern Ethiopia grew rich by funnelling ivory, gold and slaves to the Red Sea port of Adulis and on to Roman Egypt, India and Arabia. Aksum built monumental stone palaces and raised carved granite stelae over elite tombs, developed the Ge'ez script, and by the late third century was striking its own gold coinage — one of only a handful of states in the world to do so. It set the stage for Ezana's conversion to Christianity and Aksum's imperial reach across the sea into Yemen.
Early Aksumite (Ethiopia, AD 1–AD 300).source: Beta maṣāḥǝft: Manuscripts of Ethiopia and Eritrea

Early Iron Age (Pompeii, 849 BC–699 BC).label: Early Iron Age
Early Iron Age (Pompeii, 849 BC–699 BC).prose:
[Pompeii, 849 BC–699 BC] Early Iron Age. Period definition from The complete Pompeii — Berry, Joanne, 1971-, 2007.

Iron working replaced bronze as the everyday metal, and communities in the western Balkans built fortified hilltop settlements and buried their dead beneath earthen tumuli with weapons and ornaments. Distinctive bronze jewellery and imported goods show links to the Adriatic and the Aegean world. These groups form the archaeological background to the Dardanians known from later Greek and Roman writers.

Khirokitia Culture (Cyprus, 6050 BC–4550.label: Khirokitia Culture
Khirokitia Culture (Cyprus, 6050 BC–4550.prose:
[Cyprus, 6050 BC–4550 BC] Khirokitia Culture. Compiled from several sources, including Bolger (2003: 214)[1]; Hood (personal communication 2004); Peltenberg (2003b: 99)[2]; and Peltenburg et al. Cyprus's aceramic Neolithic villagers built clusters of round stone-and-mud houses, sometimes walled off from the outside, and buried their dead beneath the floors of their homes. They farmed grain, herded sheep, goats and pigs, ground stone into elegant vessels and carved stylised human figures, all without making pottery. Their settlements show an island society that developed largely on its own terms after the first farmers crossed from the mainland.
Khirokitia Culture (Cyprus, 6050 BC–4550.source: The neolithic revolution in the Near East : transforming the human landscape

Sotira Culture (Cyprus, 4150 BC–3050 BC).prose:

Period definition from The neolithic revolution in the Near East : transforming the human landscape — Alan H. Simmons, 2007.

Cyprus's Late Neolithic, named after the hilltop village of Sotira-Teppes, where dozens of round and sub-rectangular houses with plastered floors and hearths crowded inside an enclosure. Potters now made dark burnished bowls decorated with combed and painted patterns, a break from the earlier aceramic villages. Farming, herding and the seasonal use of caves and coastal sites continued until the settlements gave way to the Chalcolithic communities of Erimi.
Sotira Culture (Cyprus, 4150 BC–3050 BC).source: The neolithic revolution in the Near East : transforming the human landscape

Epoca Bronzului (Romania, 3500 BC–1051 B.label: Epoca Bronzului
Epoca Bronzului (Romania, 3500 BC–1051 B.prose:
[Romania, 3500 BC–1051 BC] Epoca Bronzului. Romanian Academy. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Metalworkers in the Carpathian basin turned local copper and imported tin into swords, axes and ornaments of remarkable quality, buried in hoards that still turn up by the hundred. Cultures such as Otomani, Wietenberg and Monteoru built fortified settlements and tells, worked gold on a lavish scale, and traded amber and metal along routes running to the Aegean and central Europe.

Vroeg Romeinse Tijd (Netherlands, 12 BC–.label: Vroeg Romeinse Tijd
Vroeg Romeinse Tijd (Netherlands, 12 BC–.prose:
[Netherlands, 12 BC–AD 69] Vroeg Romeinse Tijd. Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Roman armies pushed to and across the Rhine, turning the river into a supplied and fortified frontier and drawing the local tribes into the empire as taxpayers, allies and above all recruits. Towns, roads and forts appeared, and imported goods spread quickly through the countryside. The period closes with the Batavian revolt of AD 69, when Roman-trained auxiliaries turned on their masters and burned much of the frontier.

Modern (Denmark, AD 1660–AD 2000).label: Modern
Modern (Denmark, AD 1660–AD 2000).prose:
[Denmark, AD 1660–AD 2000] Modern. ARENA1/ADS. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Kosovo passed from the last decades of Ottoman rule - years of Albanian national awakening around the League of Prizren and repeated uprisings - into Serbian and then Yugoslav control after the Balkan Wars of 1912. Land was redistributed and colonists settled, tens of thousands emigrated, and rival Albanian and Serbian national claims hardened into the contest that would define the territory for the next century. The Second World War brought Italian and German occupation, partition, and brutal reprisals before Yugoslav partisans took control.

Jüngere Eisenzeit (Austria, 450 BC–1 BC).label: Jüngere Eisenzeit
Jüngere Eisenzeit (Austria, 450 BC–1 BC).prose:
[Austria, 450 BC–1 BC] Jüngere Eisenzeit. Austrian Academy of Sciences. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The La Tène centuries, when Celtic-speaking communities in the eastern Alps buried warriors with iron swords and imported wine equipment, mined salt at Hallein, and eventually gathered into fortified hilltop towns. Out of these groups grew the kingdom of Noricum, famous for its steel and closely tied to Rome by trade before being absorbed into the empire under Augustus.

Mittel Neolithikum (Austria, 4800 BC–425.label: Mittel Neolithikum
Mittel Neolithikum (Austria, 4800 BC–425.prose:
[Austria, 4800 BC–4251 BC] Mittel Neolithikum. Austrian Academy of Sciences. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Farming communities of the Danube basin in this period built enormous circular ditched enclosures, the Kreisgrabenanlagen, with precisely aligned entrance causeways that are among Europe's oldest monumental architecture. The Lengyel culture's painted pottery, longhouse villages and copper ornaments show settled communities with growing social complexity. Why the enclosures were built, and why they were abandoned within a few centuries, remains debated.

Modern (Iceland, AD 1900–AD 2000).label: Modern
Modern (Iceland, AD 1900–AD 2000).prose:
[Iceland, AD 1900–AD 2000] Modern. ARENA1/ADS. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Kosovo passed from the last decades of Ottoman rule - years of Albanian national awakening around the League of Prizren and repeated uprisings - into Serbian and then Yugoslav control after the Balkan Wars of 1912. Land was redistributed and colonists settled, tens of thousands emigrated, and rival Albanian and Serbian national claims hardened into the contest that would define the territory for the next century. The Second World War brought Italian and German occupation, partition, and brutal reprisals before Yugoslav partisans took control.

železna doba (Slovenia, 750 BC–31 BC).label: železna doba
železna doba (Slovenia, 750 BC–31 BC).prose:
[Slovenia, 750 BC–31 BC] železna doba. ZRC SAZU, Institute of Archaeology. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Iron-using communities in the Slovenian lands built fortified hilltop centres such as Stična and Vače, surrounded by great barrow cemeteries. Their aristocrats commissioned bronze situlae decorated with banquets, processions and boxing matches, some of the finest figural art north of the Adriatic, and traded with Etruria and the Balkans. Celtic Taurisci arrived from the 4th century BC, and the whole region was absorbed by Rome under Augustus.

Nieuwe Tijd Midden (Netherlands, AD 1650.label: Nieuwe Tijd Midden
Nieuwe Tijd Midden (Netherlands, AD 1650.prose:
[Netherlands, AD 1650–AD 1849] Nieuwe Tijd Midden. Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The Republic after its commercial peak: wars with England and France, a slow slide from dominance in trade, and enormous investment in drainage, dykes and country estates. French invasion swept the old order away, producing the Batavian Republic, annexation to Napoleon's empire, and then the unified Kingdom of the Netherlands. Material culture from these centuries is abundant and well dated, from clay pipes and delftware to the timbers of merchant ships.

âge du Bronze ancien (France, 2200 BC–16.node: âge du Bronze ancien (France, 2200 BC–1601 BC)
âge du Bronze ancien (France, 2200 BC–16.label: âge du Bronze ancien
âge du Bronze ancien (France, 2200 BC–16.prose:
[France, 2200 BC–1601 BC] âge du Bronze ancien. INRAP. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Copper-alloy metallurgy took hold across the region, with tin-bronze daggers, axes and pins produced and traded along river and coastal routes. Communities were still small and dispersed, but the demand for tin and copper drew them into long-distance exchange networks reaching Cornwall, the Alps and central Europe. Burials begin to single out individuals with weapons and ornaments, a hint of hardening social hierarchies.

Late Bronze Age (Cyprus, 1650 BC–1051 BC.label: Late Bronze Age
Late Bronze Age (Cyprus, 1650 BC–1051 BC.prose:
[Cyprus, 1650 BC–1051 BC] Late Bronze Age. Jamieson, 2007 (Ian Potter Museum exhibition). Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Farming communities in the Danube, Sava and Morava basins turned to cremation burial in urnfields and produced bronze on a large scale, leaving hoards of swords, axes and ornaments buried in the ground. Fortified settlements on river terraces and along trade routes carrying Baltic amber and Transylvanian metal mark the era. Its groups feed directly into the Iron Age cultures of the central Balkans.

Eneolit (Albania, 3060 BC–2101 BC).label: Eneolit
Eneolit (Albania, 3060 BC–2101 BC).prose: [Albania, 3060 BC–2101 BC] Eneolit. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Hellenistic I (Cyprus, 325 BC–151 BC).label: Hellenistic I
Hellenistic I (Cyprus, 325 BC–151 BC).prose:
[Cyprus, 325 BC–151 BC] Hellenistic I. Jamieson, 2007 (Ian Potter Museum exhibition). Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The island's ancient city-kingdoms were abolished and Cyprus became a Ptolemaic possession governed from Egypt, valued for its copper, timber and shipbuilding. Nea Paphos replaced Salamis as the administrative capital, and Alexandrian styles in sculpture, mosaics and burial architecture reshaped island culture. Greek language and Ptolemaic coinage displaced the old Cypro-syllabic script and local dynasties.

Mittlere Bronzezeit (Germany, 1600 BC–13.label: Mittlere Bronzezeit
Mittlere Bronzezeit (Germany, 1600 BC–13.prose:
[Germany, Switzerland, Czech Republic, Liechtenstein, 1600 BC–1301 BC] Mittlere Bronzezeit. Spatial coverage: Czech Republic, Germany, Liechtenstein, Switzerland. no source provided. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The age of the Tumulus culture, when the dead across much of central Europe were buried under round earthen mounds with bronze daggers, pins and spiral ornaments. Bronzeworking became routine rather than exotic, supplied by long-distance trade in copper from the Alps and tin from further west, and cemeteries show clear differences in wealth between graves. The tradition ends as cremation and urnfield burial spread, remaking funerary practice across the continent.

Trattbägarkulturen (Sweden, 3900 BC–2400.label: Trattbägarkulturen
Trattbägarkulturen (Sweden, 3900 BC–2400.prose:
[Sweden, 3900 BC–2400 BC] Trattbägarkulturen. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Farming reached southern Scandinavia with these people, who cleared forest for wheat, barley and cattle and left behind the distinctive funnel-necked pots that give the culture its name. They built the region's first monuments — dolmens, passage graves and long barrows — and deposited pots of food, amber and flint axes in bogs and lakes. Their megalithic tombs still stand in the Swedish landscape, the oldest surviving architecture in the country.

La Tène C (Germany, 250 BC–121 BC).label: La Tène C
La Tène C (Germany, 250 BC–121 BC).prose:
[Germany, Switzerland, Czech Republic, Liechtenstein, 250 BC–121 BC] La Tène C. Spatial coverage: Czech Republic, Germany, Liechtenstein, Switzerland. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The middle La Tène, when the long slashing sword hung from an iron chain belt becomes the standard warrior's equipment and cremation begins to replace inhumation over much of the region. Large open settlements and craft centres grew, gold and silver coinage struck in imitation of Macedonian and Roman types came into use, and trade with the Mediterranean intensified. The decorated scabbards of this phase, in the so-called Sword Style, are among the finest Celtic metalwork.

Medeltid (Sweden, AD 1050–AD 1520).label: Medeltid
Medeltid (Sweden, AD 1050–AD 1520).prose:
[Sweden, AD 1050–AD 1520] Medeltid. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Sweden took shape as a Christian kingdom in these centuries: stone churches and cathedrals replaced pagan cult sites, towns like Stockholm and Visby grew rich on Baltic trade with the Hanseatic League, and provincial laws were gradually welded into a national code. Danish, Norwegian and Swedish crowns were joined in the Kalmar Union from 1397, an arrangement Swedish nobles resented and repeatedly rebelled against. The Stockholm Bloodbath of 1520 ended it, opening the way to Gustav Vasa and the Reformation.

legújabb kor (Hungary, AD 1867–AD 2000).label: legújabb kor
legújabb kor (Hungary, AD 1867–AD 2000).prose:
[Hungary, AD 1867–AD 2000] legújabb kor. Hungarian National Museum. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The Compromise of 1867 gave the kingdom self-government within Austria-Hungary and set off rapid industrialisation, railway building and the transformation of Budapest into a European capital. Defeat in the First World War and the Treaty of Trianon cut the country to a third of its former territory, a wound that shaped the century. Another war, four decades of communist rule, the crushed uprising of 1956 and the peaceful transition of 1989 followed.

Midden Romeinse Tijd A (Netherlands, AD.label: Midden Romeinse Tijd A
Midden Romeinse Tijd A (Netherlands, AD.prose:
[Netherlands, AD 70–AD 149] Midden Romeinse Tijd A. Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Rebuilding after the Batavian revolt turned the Rhine frontier into a permanent military landscape of stone forts, watchtowers and a metalled road, garrisoned by auxiliary units drawn from across the empire. Towns and markets grew up beside the camps, and native farmsteads adopted Roman pottery, coinage and building styles. Nijmegen gained city rights and the south saw its first villa estates.

Epoca Contemporană (Romania, AD 1878–AD.label: Epoca Contemporană
Epoca Contemporană (Romania, AD 1878–AD.prose:
[Romania, AD 1878–AD 2000] Epoca Contemporană. Romanian Academy. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Independence, won on the battlefield and confirmed at the Congress of Berlin, was followed by a kingdom, oil and grain exports, and the union of 1918 that created Greater Romania. Two world wars, territorial losses, four decades of communist rule culminating in Ceaușescu's austerity, and the violent revolution of 1989 all fall within this span.

Néolithique (France, 6000 BC–2201 BC).label: Néolithique
Néolithique (France, 6000 BC–2201 BC).prose:
[France, 6000 BC–2201 BC] Néolithique. INRAP. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Herding of sheep, goats and cattle, together with pottery and cultivated grain, spread across the Moroccan coast, the Rif and the Atlas, taking hold among populations descended from earlier hunter-gatherers. Cardial-impressed pottery in the north points to contact across the Strait with Iberia, while cave sites and shell middens show a mixed economy of farming, herding, fishing and gathering. Rock engravings and painted shelters of these centuries record the animals people now depended on.

Medieval (Iceland, AD 1100–AD 1599).label: Medieval
Medieval (Iceland, AD 1100–AD 1599).prose: [Iceland, AD 1100–AD 1599] Medieval. ARENA1/ADS. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Moyen Âge (France, AD 500–AD 1491).label: Moyen Âge
Moyen Âge (France, AD 500–AD 1491).prose:
[France, AD 500–AD 1491] Moyen Âge. INRAP. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

A thousand years running from the collapse of Roman authority through Merovingian and Carolingian kingdoms to the age of cathedrals, and on into the plague, the Hundred Years' War and recovery under Charles VII and Louis XI. Latin Christianity, feudal lordship and the manorial countryside gave the era its framework, while towns, guilds and universities gradually grew inside it. By its end a recognisably French kingdom, language and royal state had emerged.

късна желязна епоха (Bulgaria, 500 BC–AD.label: късна желязна епоха
късна желязна епоха (Bulgaria, 500 BC–AD.prose:
[Bulgaria, 500 BC–AD 14] късна желязна епоха. National Institute of Archaeology with Museum, Automated Information System "Archaeological Map of Bulgaria". Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The Odrysian kings and their successors ruled from residences such as Seuthopolis, minted coins and buried their dead in stone and brick tombs with corbelled domes — Kazanlak's painted chamber and the caryatids of Sveshtari among them. Greek craftsmen and Greek taste shaped the treasures of the Thracian elite, while Celtic incursions and a Celtic kingdom at Tylis added another layer. Roman power closed in from the south and the Danube, ending Thracian independence.

доцната антика (Republic of Macedonia, A.label: доцната антика
доцната антика (Republic of Macedonia, A.prose:
[Macedonia, AD 300–AD 599] доцната антика. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Roman provincial towns were rebuilt as Christian centres, with bishops, baptisteries and floor mosaics of extraordinary quality at Stobi, Heraclea Lyncestis and Lychnidos. Earthquakes, Gothic and Hunnic raids and shifting imperial administration repeatedly disrupted urban life, and Justinian's building programme marked a last major investment. By the end of the period the cities were shrinking or abandoned as Slavic groups settled the countryside.

Laat Romeinse Tijd (Netherlands, AD 270–.label: Laat Romeinse Tijd
Laat Romeinse Tijd (Netherlands, AD 270–.prose:
[Netherlands, AD 270–AD 449] Laat Romeinse Tijd. Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Roman control north of the Rhine had already gone, and the frontier itself became porous: forts were abandoned, rebuilt or garrisoned by Germanic troops, and much of the countryside emptied of villas. Coin hoards, late military belt fittings and hand-made Germanic pottery mark the arrival of new populations, above all Franks and Saxons. By the end of it, Roman administration in the region had ceased entirely.

Neolithic (Denmark, 3900 BC–1701 BC).label: Neolithic
Neolithic (Denmark, 3900 BC–1701 BC).prose:
[Denmark, 3900 BC–1701 BC] Neolithic. ARENA1/ADS. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

In the southern Levant this is where farming villages first take hold: wheat, barley, sheep and goats replace foraging, and settlements like Jericho grow to unprecedented size behind stone walls and a tower. Households plastered their floors, kept the skulls of their dead under them and modelled faces onto them in plaster, and at 'Ain Ghazal produced large human statues of lime plaster over reed frames. Pottery arrives only in the later centuries, long after the farming economy itself.

La Tène I (France, 450 BC–261 BC).label: La Tène I
La Tène I (France, 450 BC–261 BC).prose:
[France, 450 BC–261 BC] La Tène I. INRAP. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The first phase of the Celtic Iron Age, when a new curvilinear art style — tendrils, palmettes and stylised faces borrowed from Greek and Etruscan models — appeared on brooches, scabbards and drinking gear. Rich chariot burials in the Marne and Moselle regions replaced the older princely tombs, and warrior equipment became a standard part of graves. This is the era of the great Celtic migrations that carried raiders into Italy and the Balkans.

Mesolithic (Poland, 8200 BC–4501 BC).label: Mesolithic
Mesolithic (Poland, 8200 BC–4501 BC).prose:
[Poland, 8200 BC–4501 BC] Mesolithic. ARENA1/ADS. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

After the ice sheets withdrew, birch and then dense oak forest spread over Britain, and hunter-gatherers followed the red deer, wild pig and fish into it. They worked tiny flint microliths into composite arrows and harpoons, built shelters at places like Star Carr, and burned back woodland to draw game into clearings. For most of these millennia Britain was joined to the continent by the drowned plain of Doggerland, and the sea's final closure around 6000 BC turned the population into islanders.

Ältere Kupferzeit (Germany, 4250 BC–3401.label: Ältere Kupferzeit
Ältere Kupferzeit (Germany, 4250 BC–3401.prose:
[Germany, Switzerland, Czech Republic, Liechtenstein, 4250 BC–3401 BC] Ältere Kupferzeit. Spatial coverage: Czech Republic, Germany, Liechtenstein, Switzerland. no source provided. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Copper objects — flat axes, awls, daggers and ornaments — begin appearing in Central European graves and settlements, evidence of smelting and casting knowledge spreading up from the south-east. Farming communities such as the Michelsberg culture built large ditched enclosures on hilltops and river terraces, while in the north the first megalithic tombs were being raised. Metal was still rare and largely a marker of status rather than a workaday material, but the skills involved would transform the following centuries.

Crusader (Cyprus, AD 1191–AD 1488).label: Crusader
Crusader (Cyprus, AD 1191–AD 1488).prose:
[Cyprus, AD 1191–AD 1488] Crusader. no source provided. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Richard the Lionheart seized the island from its rebel Byzantine governor on his way to the Third Crusade and quickly passed it on; under the Lusignan dynasty it became a Latin kingdom with a French-speaking aristocracy ruling a Greek Orthodox population. After the mainland crusader states fell, Cyprus became the front line and the entrepôt of eastern trade, with Famagusta growing rich enough to fund a skyline of Gothic churches. Genoese and Venetian rivalry hollowed out the monarchy until Venice took the island outright.

ранен eнеолит (Bulgaria, 4900 BC–4601 BC.label: ранен eнеолит
ранен eнеолит (Bulgaria, 4900 BC–4601 BC.prose:
[Bulgaria, 4900 BC–4601 BC] ранен eнеолит. National Institute of Archaeology with Museum, Automated Information System "Archaeological Map of Bulgaria". Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Farming villages on the tells began smelting copper, producing heavy axe-adzes and ornaments and opening ore sources in the Sredna Gora. Fine graphite-painted pottery and elaborate figurines mark the Marica and related cultures, and organised cemeteries outside settlements appear for the first time. These developments led directly to the extraordinary wealth and social ranking of the later Copper Age.

зряло средновековие (Bulgaria, AD 1187–A.label: зряло средновековие
зряло средновековие (Bulgaria, AD 1187–A.prose:
[Bulgaria, AD 1187–AD 1395] зряло средновековие. National Institute of Archaeology with Museum, Automated Information System "Archaeological Map of Bulgaria". Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The uprising of the brothers Asen and Peter broke Byzantine control and created the Second Bulgarian Empire, with its capital on the fortified hill of Tsarevets at Tarnovo. Under Ivan Asen II the state briefly dominated the Balkans, and Tarnovo became a centre of painting, manuscript copying and church building — the frescoes of Boyana date from this world. Repeated Tatar raids, dynastic splits and the division of the realm left it unable to resist the Ottoman advance, which took Tarnovo in 1393.

Hochmittelalter (Austria, AD 976–AD 1249.label: Hochmittelalter
Hochmittelalter (Austria, AD 976–AD 1249.prose:
[Austria, AD 976–AD 1249] Hochmittelalter. Austrian Academy of Sciences. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The Babenberg margraves, granted the eastern march in 976, turned a frontier zone into a duchy with its own law, towns and Danube trade, with Vienna emerging as a residence city. Monasteries such as Melk and Klosterneuburg were founded or rebuilt in stone, hilltop castles multiplied, and forest and marsh were cleared for new villages. The dynasty died out in 1246, opening the succession struggle that would eventually bring the Habsburgs.

късен eнеолит (Bulgaria, 4400 BC–3801 BC.label: късен eнеолит
късен eнеолит (Bulgaria, 4400 BC–3801 BC.prose:
[Bulgaria, 4400 BC–3801 BC] късен eнеолит. National Institute of Archaeology with Museum, Automated Information System "Archaeological Map of Bulgaria". Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Copper-using farming communities reached a peak of wealth on the tells of the Thracian plain and the lower Danube, with two-storey houses, graphite-painted pottery and mining of ore at sites like Ai Bunar. The cemetery at Varna belongs here — the earliest large concentration of worked gold anywhere, buried with sceptres and axes that mark out a ranked society. Around 4000 BC these settlements were abandoned almost everywhere, one of prehistoric Europe's sharpest collapses.

Early Medieval (Poland, AD 375–AD 599).label: Early Medieval
Early Medieval (Poland, AD 375–AD 599).prose:
[Poland, AD 375–AD 599] Early Medieval. ARENA1/ADS. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Avar and Slav raids broke the Byzantine Danube frontier, emptying the old Roman towns and bringing permanent Slavic settlement to the central Balkans. Over the following centuries small Serb principalities emerged in the hills between Byzantine and Bulgarian spheres, and Christian missionaries introduced the Slavonic liturgy and Cyrillic letters. Archaeologically the shift is stark: masonry cities give way to timber villages, cremation cemeteries and simple hand-made pottery.

Alto Romano (Spain, 50 BC–AD 199).label: Alto Romano
Alto Romano (Spain, 50 BC–AD 199).prose:
[Spain, 50 BC–AD 199] Alto Romano. Institute of Heritage Sciences, Spanish National Research Council (CSIC Incipit). Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

With the Cantabrian wars finished, Hispania settled into provincial life under the Empire: new towns with forums and theatres, roads and bridges, the aqueducts of Segovia and Mérida, and vast exports of olive oil, wine, garum and silver to Rome. Latin, Roman law and urban citizenship spread widely, and the peninsula gave the empire Seneca, Martial, Trajan and Hadrian.

Zeitgeschichte (Germany, AD 1850–AD 2000.label: Zeitgeschichte
Zeitgeschichte (Germany, AD 1850–AD 2000.prose:
[Germany, Switzerland, Czech Republic, Liechtenstein, AD 1850–AD 2000] Zeitgeschichte. Spatial coverage: Czech Republic, Germany, Liechtenstein, Switzerland. no source provided. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The century and a half in which Germany was industrialised, unified into an empire, fought and lost two world wars, carried out the Holocaust, was divided between rival blocs and then reunited. Cities were rebuilt twice over, populations were displaced on a huge scale and the state's form changed repeatedly, from monarchy to republic to dictatorship to two competing states. Museum collections from this span are often about memory and reckoning as much as about objects.

Bronstijd (Netherlands, 2000 BC–801 BC).label: Bronstijd
Bronstijd (Netherlands, 2000 BC–801 BC).prose:
[Netherlands, 2000 BC–801 BC] Bronstijd. Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Metal reached the low countries in quantity, mostly as imported bronze axes, swords and ornaments, since the region has neither copper nor tin. Farming communities lived in long timber byre houses on sandy soils, raising cattle and burying their dead first under round barrows and later in cremation urnfields. Bogs and rivers received deliberate deposits of weapons and ornaments, some of the most striking finds in Dutch archaeology.

желязна епоха (Bulgaria, 1100 BC–AD 14).label: желязна епоха
желязна епоха (Bulgaria, 1100 BC–AD 14).prose:
[Bulgaria, 1100 BC–AD 14] желязна епоха. National Institute of Archaeology with Museum, Automated Information System "Archaeological Map of Bulgaria". Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Iron working spread through the Thracian lands as tribal societies buried their leaders under monumental mounds and carved sanctuaries into the rocks of the Rhodopes and Sakar. Greek colonies on the Black Sea coast pulled the interior into Mediterranean trade, and by the fifth century the Odrysian kings ruled a state wealthy enough to commission the gold and silver hoards now famous from Panagyurishte and Rogozen. The era closes with Macedonian and then Roman domination, when Thrace became provincial territory rather than a kingdom.

Förromersk järnålder (Sweden, 500 BC–1 B.label: Förromersk järnålder
Förromersk järnålder (Sweden, 500 BC–1 B.prose:
[Sweden, 500 BC–1 BC] Förromersk järnålder. SND. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Iron, smelted from local bog ore, replaced imported bronze and put tools and weapons within reach of ordinary farmers. Settlements became small, dispersed farmsteads with byre-and-dwelling longhouses, grave goods grew sparse, and burials shifted to modest cremations. Contacts with the Celtic world to the south brought new forms and ideas well before Roman goods began arriving.

mlajša bronasta doba (Slovenia, 1250 BC–.label: mlajša bronasta doba
mlajša bronasta doba (Slovenia, 1250 BC–.prose:
[Slovenia, 1250 BC–1001 BC] mlajša bronasta doba. ZRC SAZU, Institute of Archaeology. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Urnfield communities across the Slovenian lowlands and Alpine fringes cremated their dead and buried them in flat urn cemeteries, while bronze casting reached an industrial scale - hoards of axes, sickles and swords survive in quantity. Settlements clustered on defensible heights along routes between the Adriatic, the Pannonian plain and the Alps. Much of the settlement geography of the later Hallstatt hillforts was fixed in this time.

Baja Edad Media (Spain, AD 1200–AD 1499).label: Baja Edad Media
Baja Edad Media (Spain, AD 1200–AD 1499).prose:
[Spain, AD 1200–AD 1499] Baja Edad Media. Institute of Heritage Sciences, Spanish National Research Council (CSIC Incipit). Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The great southward conquests after Las Navas de Tolosa left Castile and the Crown of Aragon holding almost all Iberia, with Muslim rule reduced to Granada paying tribute. Aragon turned seaward to Sicily, Sardinia and Naples while Castile developed wool exports, Cortes assemblies and violent noble factionalism; plague, pogroms against Jewish communities and civil wars punctuated the era. It closes with the marriage of Ferdinand and Isabella, the fall of Granada and the voyages that carried Iberian power across the Atlantic.

Vroege Middeleeuwen A (Netherlands, AD 4.label: Vroege Middeleeuwen A
Vroege Middeleeuwen A (Netherlands, AD 4.prose:
[Netherlands, AD 450–AD 524] Vroege Middeleeuwen A. Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The generations immediately after Roman authority vanished, when many river-valley settlements lay empty and population was at its lowest for centuries. Small groups from the north and east moved into the abandoned landscape, and material culture shifted to handmade pottery and furnished burials of a distinctly Germanic character.

Evul Mediu Timpuriu (Romania, AD 800–AD.label: Evul Mediu Timpuriu
Evul Mediu Timpuriu (Romania, AD 800–AD.prose:
[Romania, AD 800–AD 1299] Evul Mediu Timpuriu. Romanian Academy. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Small agrarian communities living in sunken-floored houses gradually coalesced into larger polities, while Hungarian expansion brought Transylvania under the Árpád kings and drew in Saxon and Szekler colonists. The Mongol invasion of 1241 devastated the region and prompted a wave of stone castle building. By the end of the period, local voivodes east and south of the Carpathians were laying the groundwork for independent principalities.

Moderne (Albania, AD 1850–AD 1949).label: Moderne
Moderne (Albania, AD 1850–AD 1949).prose:
[Albania, AD 1850–AD 1949] Moderne. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Albanian lands remained Ottoman provinces while the Rilindja movement built a written language and a national idea across religious divisions. Independence was declared in 1912 amid the Balkan Wars, but the new state's borders left large Albanian populations outside them, and the interwar years under Ahmet Zogu were poor and unstable. Italian occupation in 1939 and then German control ended in 1944 with the victory of the communist partisans.

srednji vek (Slovenia, AD 600–AD 1499).label: srednji vek
srednji vek (Slovenia, AD 600–AD 1499).prose:
[Slovenia, AD 600–AD 1499] srednji vek. ZRC SAZU, Institute of Archaeology. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Slavic settlers moved into the eastern Alps and formed the principality of Carantania, one of the earliest Slavic polities, before Frankish and later Habsburg lordship drew the lands into the Holy Roman Empire. Christianisation brought churches, monasteries and Latin literacy, while towns such as Ljubljana, Ptuj and Škofja Loka grew around markets and castles. Visitors can still trace the period in hilltop fortresses, Gothic frescoes and the ritual of the Carantanian ducal inauguration on the Prince's Stone.

Protohistorie (Netherlands, 12 BC–AD 449.label: Protohistorie
Protohistorie (Netherlands, 12 BC–AD 449.prose:
[Netherlands, 12 BC–AD 449] Protohistorie. Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The Rhine became the frontier of the Roman Empire, with forts, roads and towns south of it and Frisian and other Germanic communities on terpen and sandy soils beyond. Local people left no writing of their own, so they appear only through excavation and through Roman authors — most famously in the account of the Batavian revolt. Roman control ebbed away in the fourth and fifth centuries as Franks and Saxons moved in.

Yngre vasatiden (Sweden, AD 1611–AD 1654.label: Yngre vasatiden
Yngre vasatiden (Sweden, AD 1611–AD 1654.prose:
[Sweden, AD 1611–AD 1654] Yngre vasatiden. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Gustav II Adolf's reformed army and Axel Oxenstierna's administration turned a thinly populated kingdom into a great power, decisive in the Thirty Years' War until the king's death at Lützen. Copper and iron exports, Walloon ironmasters and new towns funded the effort, while war booty filled Swedish libraries and castles. It ends with Queen Christina's conversion and abdication, an event that startled Protestant Europe.

népvándorlás kor (Hungary, AD 400–AD 884.label: népvándorlás kor
népvándorlás kor (Hungary, AD 400–AD 884.prose:
[Hungary, AD 400–AD 884] népvándorlás kor. Hungarian National Museum. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The Carpathian Basin passed through the hands of Huns, Gepids, Lombards and then the Avars, whose khaganate ruled for over two centuries before Charlemagne destroyed it. Cemeteries from these centuries are spectacular: horse burials, gold and garnet ornaments, cast bronze belt sets and the famous Avar griffin-and-tendril mounts. The era ends just before the arrival of the Hungarians, and it shaped the ethnic and political map they inherited.

Frühe Bronzezeit (Austria, 2200 BC–1601.label: Frühe Bronzezeit
Frühe Bronzezeit (Austria, 2200 BC–1601.prose:
[Austria, 2200 BC–1601 BC] Frühe Bronzezeit. Austrian Academy of Sciences. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Copper and tin alloys replace pure copper, and metalworking becomes an organised industry supplying axes, daggers and pins across long distances. Alpine copper ores drew traders from far afield, and buried hoards of ingots and ornaments show both wealth and insecurity. Settlements become more permanent and cemeteries more orderly, with grave goods marking out ranks within communities for the first time.

Vroeg Romeinse Tijd B (Netherlands, AD 2.label: Vroeg Romeinse Tijd B
Vroeg Romeinse Tijd B (Netherlands, AD 2.prose:
[Netherlands, AD 25–AD 69] Vroeg Romeinse Tijd B. Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The decades when Roman control north of the Rhine collapsed and the river hardened into an imperial frontier, lined with forts and supply roads. Batavian and Cananefate communities supplied auxiliary troops to the army while adopting Roman coinage, wheel-thrown pottery and imported wine. The phase closes with the Batavian Revolt of AD 69, when those same auxiliaries turned on Rome and burned the legionary base at Nijmegen.

Neolitico (Spain, 4500 BC–2301 BC).label: Neolitico
Neolitico (Spain, 4500 BC–2301 BC).prose:
[Spain, 4500 BC–2301 BC] Neolitico. Institute of Heritage Sciences, Spanish National Research Council (CSIC Incipit). Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Farming communities across Iberia grew cereals and herded sheep and goats, living in caves, rock shelters and open villages and making pottery decorated with impressions of shell and cord. Over these millennia they raised the peninsula's dolmens and passage graves, some among the largest megalithic monuments in Europe. The period closes with copper working, fortified settlements and the beginnings of visible social hierarchy.

Hekuri i hershëm (Albania, 1100 BC–601 B.label: Hekuri i hershëm
Hekuri i hershëm (Albania, 1100 BC–601 B.prose: [Albania, 1100 BC–601 BC] Hekuri i hershëm. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

ранна римска епоха (Bulgaria, AD 15–AD 2.label: ранна римска епоха
ранна римска епоха (Bulgaria, AD 15–AD 2.prose:
[Bulgaria, AD 15–AD 283] ранна римска епоха. National Institute of Archaeology with Museum, Automated Information System "Archaeological Map of Bulgaria". Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The provinces of Moesia and Thracia were organised, legions were stationed along the Danube, and roads linked new cities — Nicopolis ad Istrum, Oescus, Ratiaria, Augusta Traiana — with colonnaded streets, baths and theatres. Veterans settled, mining and grain production expanded, and Latin took hold on the Danube while Greek prevailed in the south. Prosperity broke in the mid-third century when Gothic raiders sacked cities and killed the emperor Decius at Abritus.

Middeleeuwen (Netherlands, AD 450–AD 149.label: Middeleeuwen
Middeleeuwen (Netherlands, AD 450–AD 149.prose:
[Netherlands, AD 450–AD 1499] Middeleeuwen. Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The thousand years between Roman withdrawal and the Habsburg era, during which the Low Countries were settled by Frisians, Franks and Saxons, Christianised, and drawn into the Carolingian world. Rising sea levels and human drainage made water management the central fact of life, producing dikes, dams and polders. By the end, the region held some of Europe's densest concentrations of towns, living on cloth, shipping and trade.

pozna bronasta doba (Slovenia, 1000 BC–7.label: pozna bronasta doba
pozna bronasta doba (Slovenia, 1000 BC–7.prose:
[Slovenia, 1000 BC–751 BC] pozna bronasta doba. ZRC SAZU, Institute of Archaeology. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Cremation in urnfield cemeteries became the standard rite, with large burial grounds at Ruše, Dobova and Ljubljana holding hundreds of graves. Bronze production peaked, evidenced by hoards of axes, sickles and swords buried in the ground, and fortified hilltop settlements watched over the passes between the Alps and the Pannonian plain. The social hierarchies and settlement patterns established here carried straight into the Iron Age.

Frühes Neolithikum (Germany, 5600 BC–480.label: Frühes Neolithikum
Frühes Neolithikum (Germany, 5600 BC–480.prose:
[Germany, Switzerland, Czech Republic, Liechtenstein, 5600 BC–4801 BC] Frühes Neolithikum. Spatial coverage: Czech Republic, Germany, Liechtenstein, Switzerland. no source provided. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The first farmers moved up the Danube and along the loess soils, bringing wheat, barley, cattle, pottery and a completely new way of living. They built timber longhouses tens of metres long, clustered in small hamlets, and left the distinctive incised Linear Pottery that gives the culture its name. Forests were cleared, land became something to hold and inherit, and mass graves at sites like Talheim show that the arrival of farming brought violence as well as surplus.

késő vaskor (Hungary, 450 BC–101 BC).label: késő vaskor
késő vaskor (Hungary, 450 BC–101 BC).prose:
[Hungary, 450 BC–101 BC] késő vaskor. Hungarian National Museum. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Celtic settlement transformed the Carpathian Basin, bringing the La Tène style, the potter's wheel, coinage and mass iron production. Tribes such as the Boii and Scordisci built fortified oppida - genuine towns with craft quarters and mints - while eastern Hungary saw growing Dacian influence. The Celtic order was broken in the first century BC by Dacian and then Roman expansion toward the Danube.

Epoca Fierului (Romania, 1050 BC–AD 106).label: Epoca Fierului
Epoca Fierului (Romania, 1050 BC–AD 106).prose:
[Romania, 1050 BC–AD 106] Epoca Fierului. Romanian Academy. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Iron replaced bronze for tools and weapons as Hallstatt and later La Tène styles spread through the Carpathians, while Greek colonies on the Black Sea coast drew the interior into Mediterranean trade. The Getae and Dacians built hilltop fortresses and, under Burebista and later Decebalus, a kingdom powerful enough to alarm Rome, which finally conquered it under Trajan.

Arkaike/Para qytetare ilire (Albania, 60.label: Arkaike/Para qytetare ilire
Arkaike/Para qytetare ilire (Albania, 60.prose:
[Albania, 600 BC–481 BC] Arkaike/Para qytetare ilire. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Illyrian tribes in the Albanian interior built fortified hilltop settlements and buried their elites under tumuli filled with weapons, bronze jewellery and imported goods. Contact with the Greek colonies of Apollonia and Epidamnos brought pottery, coinage habits and craft ideas inland, and some strongholds grew into recognisable towns. These communities became the kingdoms that later confronted Macedon and Rome.

Mittlere Kupferzeit (Germany, 3400 BC–30.label: Mittlere Kupferzeit
Mittlere Kupferzeit (Germany, 3400 BC–30.prose:
[Germany, Switzerland, Czech Republic, Liechtenstein, 3400 BC–3001 BC] Mittlere Kupferzeit. Spatial coverage: Czech Republic, Germany, Liechtenstein, Switzerland. no source provided. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Farming communities across central Germany buried their dead collectively in megalithic chambers and gallery graves, leaving behind the pottery styles archaeologists label Salzmünde, Walternienburg and Bernburg. Copper objects were still scarce and prestigious, but the plough, ox traction and the earliest wheeled vehicles were transforming how land was worked and goods moved. It is the world of the Alpine lake villages and of Ötzi, and it set the stage for the sweeping cultural changes of the Corded Ware horizon that followed.

kora rézkor (Hungary, 4500 BC–4001 BC).label: kora rézkor
kora rézkor (Hungary, 4500 BC–4001 BC).prose:
[Hungary, 4500 BC–4001 BC] kora rézkor. Hungarian National Museum. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Communities abandoned the crowded Neolithic tells for smaller, scattered settlements, and for the first time buried their dead in large cemeteries set apart from the living, as at Tiszapolgár-Basatanya. Copper was now cast into heavy tools and ornaments rather than just hammered trinkets, drawing on ores from the Carpathians and Balkans. Cattle-keeping grew in importance, a shift that shaped the following centuries.

Midden Neolithicum B (Netherlands, 3400.label: Midden Neolithicum B
Midden Neolithicum B (Netherlands, 3400.prose:
[Netherlands, 3400 BC–2851 BC] Midden Neolithicum B. Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The Funnel Beaker people of Drenthe built the hunebedden, chambered tombs of glacial boulders used for communal burial with pottery and flint offerings. Further south and west, Vlaardingen groups kept up a mixed hunting, fishing and farming economy in the wetlands. The great stone tombs remain the oldest visible monuments in the country.

középső bronzkor (Hungary, 1900 BC–1401.label: középső bronzkor
középső bronzkor (Hungary, 1900 BC–1401.prose:
[Hungary, 1900 BC–1401 BC] középső bronzkor. Hungarian National Museum. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Fortified tell settlements rose along the Danube and Tisza, their layered house mounds occupied for centuries by the Nagyrév, Hatvan, Vatya and Füzesabony communities. Bronze-working became a specialist craft, and hoards of weapons, ingots and elaborate ornaments show both wealth and insecurity. Amber, faience and metal types link the Carpathian Basin to the Baltic and the Aegean world of Mycenae.

Late IJzertijd (Netherlands, 250 BC–13 B.label: Late IJzertijd
Late IJzertijd (Netherlands, 250 BC–13 B.prose:
[Netherlands, 250 BC–13 BC] Late IJzertijd. Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Farming communities lived in scattered byre-houses shared with their cattle, working small Celtic-field systems and burying their dead in urnfield-derived cemeteries. Imported goods, coinage and weaponry show growing contact with the La Tène world to the south, and tribal groupings such as the Batavi and Frisii took shape. The period ends abruptly with Roman armies on the Rhine, which became an imperial frontier.

Classical (Cypro-Classical) I (Cyprus, 4.label: Classical (Cypro-Classical) I
Classical (Cypro-Classical) I (Cyprus, 4.prose:
[Cyprus, 475 BC–401 BC] Classical (Cypro-Classical) I. Jamieson, 2007 (Ian Potter Museum exhibition). Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Cyprus remained a patchwork of city-kingdoms under Persian overlordship, torn between loyalty to the Great King and the pull of the Greek world. Evagoras of Salamis pushed Hellenizing culture and the Greek alphabet, minted fine coinage and led a long revolt against Persia before being forced back into submission. Sculpture and architecture on the island blend Greek, Levantine and Egyptian models.

железното доба (Republic of Macedonia, 1.node: железното доба (Republic of Macedonia, 1000 BC–601 BC)
железното доба (Republic of Macedonia, 1.label: железното доба
железното доба (Republic of Macedonia, 1.prose:
[Macedonia, 1000 BC–601 BC] железното доба. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Iron replaced bronze for tools and weapons while bronze remained the metal of ornament, and communities lived in hillforts commanding fertile valleys. Rich burials, notably at Trebenište, contain gold, silver and imported Greek bronzes, showing local elites who could obtain the finest Mediterranean goods. This is the setting in which the Paeonian, Illyrian and Macedonian groups named by later Greek authors first become visible.

moderna doba (Slovenia, AD 1800–AD 2000).label: moderna doba
moderna doba (Slovenia, AD 1800–AD 2000).prose:
[Slovenia, AD 1800–AD 2000] moderna doba. ZRC SAZU, Institute of Archaeology. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Slovene lands moved from Habsburg provinces to nationhood: a literary and political awakening in the nineteenth century, industry and railways linking Ljubljana to Vienna and Trieste, then the break-up of Austria-Hungary in 1918. The twentieth century brought Yugoslavia, occupation and partition in the Second World War, socialist rule, and finally independence in 1991. Museum collections from this span cover everything from peasant crafts to factory goods and wartime relics.

Bronze Age (Cyprus, 2500 BC–1801 BC).label: Bronze Age
Bronze Age (Cyprus, 2500 BC–1801 BC).prose:
[Cyprus, 2500 BC–1801 BC] Bronze Age. Jamieson, 2007 (Ian Potter Museum exhibition). Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Pile-dwelling villages on the Ljubljana Marshes and hilltop settlements to the east mark a landscape of small farming communities well connected to the Alpine and Pannonian metal trade. From the later centuries the Urnfield tradition took hold, with cremation cemeteries and large hoards of bronze axes, sickles and weapons buried in the ground. These hoards are among the region's richest prehistoric finds and hint at both ritual deposition and the workshops of travelling smiths.

Midden IJzertijd (Netherlands, 500 BC–25.label: Midden IJzertijd
Midden IJzertijd (Netherlands, 500 BC–25.prose:
[Netherlands, 500 BC–251 BC] Midden IJzertijd. Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Farming communities across the sandy soils lived in scattered farmsteads with byre-houses, surrounded by the ditched plots archaeologists call Celtic fields. Iron smelted from local bog ore became commonplace, while imported ornaments and weapons show contact with the La Tène world to the south. In the northern coastal marshes people began raising dwelling mounds (terpen and wierden) to stay above the tides, a practice that shaped that landscape for the next two thousand years.

Haut Moyen Âge (France, AD 500–AD 999).label: Haut Moyen Âge
Haut Moyen Âge (France, AD 500–AD 999).prose:
[France, AD 500–AD 999] Haut Moyen Âge. INRAP. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The centuries between the collapse of Roman authority and the year 1000, when Frankish kings — first Merovingian, then Carolingian — built kingdoms out of the western provinces. Charlemagne's coronation in 800 revived the idea of a western empire and sponsored a revival of Latin learning and manuscript production in monastic scriptoria. Viking, Muslim and Magyar raids and the break-up of the Carolingian inheritance then shifted real power to counts and castellans, laying the ground for feudal society.

Stenålder (Sweden, 8200 BC–1800 BC).label: Stenålder
Stenålder (Sweden, 8200 BC–1800 BC).prose:
[Sweden, 8200 BC–1800 BC] Stenålder. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The Swedish Stone Age begins with hunters following the retreating ice sheet north along a coastline that was still rising out of the sea. Later came Funnel Beaker farmers with their megalithic tombs, the seal-hunting Pitted Ware people of the Baltic islands, and the Battle Axe groups whose corded pottery and stone axes link Sweden to a wider northern European world.

Steentijd (Netherlands, 1000000 BC–2001.label: Steentijd
Steentijd (Netherlands, 1000000 BC–2001.prose:
[Netherlands, 1000000 BC–2001 BC] Steentijd. Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The Dutch Stone Age, spanning everything from Neanderthal hunting camps on the river terraces to the last farming communities before metal. Highlights include the waterlogged Mesolithic and early Neolithic sites of the wetlands, where wooden tools, dugout canoes and even burials survive, and the great boulder tombs of Drenthe built by Funnel Beaker farmers.

zgodnjerimska doba (Slovenia, 30 BC–AD 2.label: zgodnjerimska doba
zgodnjerimska doba (Slovenia, 30 BC–AD 2.prose:
[Slovenia, 30 BC–AD 299] zgodnjerimska doba. ZRC SAZU, Institute of Archaeology. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Rome absorbed the eastern Alpine and Pannonian lands, and the region was carved into the provinces of Italia, Noricum and Pannonia. New towns — Emona, Celeia, Poetovio — were laid out on a grid, linked by paved roads carrying troops and trade between Italy and the Danube frontier; villas, aqueducts, stone inscriptions and Mediterranean imports became ordinary. Latin, Roman law and Roman gods mixed with older Celtic and Illyrian traditions among the local population.

La Tène D (Germany, 120 BC–51 BC).label: La Tène D
La Tène D (Germany, 120 BC–51 BC).prose:
[Germany, Switzerland, Czech Republic, Liechtenstein, 120 BC–51 BC] La Tène D. Spatial coverage: Czech Republic, Germany, Liechtenstein, Switzerland. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The final Iron Age phase, dominated by the oppida: huge walled towns with streets, workshops, mints and imported Roman wine. Political life sharpened into named tribes with magistrates and coinage, and the archaeological record ends with the Gallic Wars and the absorption of the region into the Roman world.

Äldre bronsålder (Sweden, 1800 BC–1100 B.label: Äldre bronsålder
Äldre bronsålder (Sweden, 1800 BC–1100 B.prose:
[Sweden, 1800 BC–1100 BC] Äldre bronsålder. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Bronze arrived in Scandinavia through exchange networks reaching to Central Europe and the British Isles — Sweden had no copper or tin of its own, so metal was wealth. Chiefly families were buried in stone cairns and earth barrows placed prominently on ridges and coasts, accompanied by swords, razors, and spiral-ornamented ornaments, while rock carvings of ships, sun discs and axe-bearing figures cover the granite of Bohuslän and Östergötland. Farming settlements with longhouses and the beginnings of a sun-centred religion define the era.

époque contemporaine (France, AD 1800–AD.label: époque contemporaine
époque contemporaine (France, AD 1800–AD.prose:
[France, AD 1800–AD 2000] époque contemporaine. INRAP. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Industrialisation, railways and mass politics reshaped daily life more thoroughly than anything since farming. Empires expanded and collapsed, two world wars killed on an unprecedented scale, and by the end most people lived in cities and worked away from the land. The material record shifts from handmade to mass-produced, and archaeology of this period deals as much with factories and battlefields as with settlements.

Edad del Hierro (Spain, 800 BC–51 BC).label: Edad del Hierro
Edad del Hierro (Spain, 800 BC–51 BC).prose: [Spain, 800 BC–51 BC] Edad del Hierro. Institute of Heritage Sciences, Spanish National Research Council (CSIC Incipit). Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Modern tid (Sweden, AD 1521–AD 2000).label: Modern tid
Modern tid (Sweden, AD 1521–AD 2000).prose:
[Sweden, AD 1521–AD 2000] Modern tid. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Gustav Vasa's revolt broke the Kalmar Union with Denmark and created a hereditary Swedish monarchy that seized church property and imposed the Lutheran Reformation. In the seventeenth century Sweden became a great power controlling much of the Baltic coast, funded by copper and iron exports, until defeat by Russia ended that ambition. Later came agrarian reform, mass emigration to America, industrialisation around timber and ore, and the building of the twentieth-century welfare state.

La Tène finale (France, 150 BC–51 BC).label: La Tène finale
La Tène finale (France, 150 BC–51 BC).prose:
[France, 150 BC–51 BC] La Tène finale. INRAP. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The oppidum age in Gaul: large fortified towns with planned streets, coin mints, ironworking and glass workshops, and warehouses of Italian wine amphorae. Political units had hardened into named tribal states with treasuries and elected magistrates. The phase closes with the Gallic Wars and the absorption of Gaul into the Roman empire.

Zeitgeschichte (Austria, AD 1850–AD 2000.label: Zeitgeschichte
Zeitgeschichte (Austria, AD 1850–AD 2000.prose:
[Austria, AD 1850–AD 2000] Zeitgeschichte. Austrian Academy of Sciences. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The century and a half in which Germany was industrialised, unified into an empire, fought and lost two world wars, carried out the Holocaust, was divided between rival blocs and then reunited. Cities were rebuilt twice over, populations were displaced on a huge scale and the state's form changed repeatedly, from monarchy to republic to dictatorship to two competing states. Museum collections from this span are often about memory and reckoning as much as about objects.

Modern (Cyprus, AD 1914–AD 2000).label: Modern
Modern (Cyprus, AD 1914–AD 2000).prose:
[Cyprus, AD 1914–AD 2000] Modern. no source provided. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Kosovo passed from the last decades of Ottoman rule - years of Albanian national awakening around the League of Prizren and repeated uprisings - into Serbian and then Yugoslav control after the Balkan Wars of 1912. Land was redistributed and colonists settled, tens of thousands emigrated, and rival Albanian and Serbian national claims hardened into the contest that would define the territory for the next century. The Second World War brought Italian and German occupation, partition, and brutal reprisals before Yugoslav partisans took control.

Post Medieval (Poland, AD 1250–AD 1499).label: Post Medieval
Post Medieval (Poland, AD 1250–AD 1499).prose:
[Poland, AD 1250–AD 1499] Post Medieval. ARENA1/ADS. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Beginning with the dissolution of the monasteries and the Reformation's stripping of parish churches, these centuries carried England through civil war, the growth of an Atlantic empire, enclosure of open fields, and industrialisation. Excavations of the period yield mass-produced goods - tin-glazed and transfer-printed pottery, glass bottles, clay tobacco pipes, machine-made nails - that let sites be dated to within a decade or two. Landscapes changed as thoroughly as objects: hedged fields, canals, railways, mines and terraced workers' housing all belong to this span.

Nieuwe Tijd (Netherlands, AD 1500–AD 194.label: Nieuwe Tijd
Nieuwe Tijd (Netherlands, AD 1500–AD 194.prose:
[Netherlands, AD 1500–AD 1944] Nieuwe Tijd. Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The Dutch 'modern era', running from the Habsburg Netherlands through the Revolt, the Republic and its overseas trading empire to industrialisation and the Second World War. Its archaeology is one of brick towns and canal frontages, reclaimed polders and windmill drainage, clay pipes, tin-glazed earthenware and shipwrecks carrying Asian porcelain. It is the period in which the physical landscape of the modern Netherlands was essentially engineered into being.

római kor (Hungary, 100 BC–AD 399).label: római kor
római kor (Hungary, 100 BC–AD 399).prose:
[Hungary, 100 BC–AD 399] római kor. Hungarian National Museum. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Rome annexed the lands west of the Danube as the province of Pannonia, fortifying the river as a frontier with legionary bases and watchtowers. Towns such as Aquincum, Savaria and Sopianae acquired amphitheatres, baths, aqueducts and mosaic-floored villas, while the Great Plain beyond the river stayed in the hands of Sarmatian horsemen – a divide that shaped centuries of raiding and diplomacy.

Eisenzeit (Germany, 1200 BC–51 BC).label: Eisenzeit
Eisenzeit (Germany, 1200 BC–51 BC).prose:
[Germany, Switzerland, Czech Republic, Liechtenstein, 1200 BC–51 BC] Eisenzeit. Spatial coverage: Czech Republic, Germany, Liechtenstein, Switzerland. no source provided. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Iron working spread through the region, first in the Hallstatt culture, whose chieftains were buried with wagons, gold and imported Mediterranean wine vessels, then in the La Tene culture with its swirling ornamental art. Hilltop strongholds grew into fortified towns with coinage, workshops and long-distance trade, while Germanic-speaking groups consolidated north of the Celtic zone. The era closes with Caesar's conquest of Gaul, which pushed the Roman frontier to the Rhine.

Roman (Poland, AD 100–AD 374).label: Roman
Roman (Poland, AD 100–AD 374).prose:
[Poland, AD 100–AD 374] Roman. ARENA1/ADS. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

After Actium and the death of Cleopatra, Egypt became the personal possession of the emperor, governed by a prefect and squeezed for the grain that fed Rome. Greek remained the language of administration, temples went on being built in pharaonic style with emperors shown as pharaohs, and the desert quarries and Red Sea ports linked the Nile to India. The dry sands preserved tens of thousands of papyri and the startlingly lifelike Fayum mummy portraits, while Alexandria became a cradle of Christian thought.

Laat Romeinse Tijd B (Netherlands, AD 35.label: Laat Romeinse Tijd B
Laat Romeinse Tijd B (Netherlands, AD 35.prose:
[Netherlands, AD 350–AD 449] Laat Romeinse Tijd B. Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The end of Roman power in the Low Countries. Garrisons were withdrawn or turned into local warbands, coin supply dried up, and Frankish and Saxon settlers established themselves on land that had been provincial territory. Hand-made pottery and timber farmsteads replace the Roman material world in the archaeological record.

Bronz i vonë (Albania, 1500 BC–1101 BC).label: Bronz i vonë
Bronz i vonë (Albania, 1500 BC–1101 BC).prose:
[Albania, 1500 BC–1101 BC] Bronz i vonë. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Mycenaean pottery, swords and rapiers turn up in tumulus burials in the interior, showing that the communities of the region were tied into Aegean exchange networks. Burial under earthen mounds, often used and reused over centuries by the same groups, is the defining feature of the period and continued long afterwards, which is why archaeologists have argued about its links to the later Illyrian tribes.

Senmesolitikum (Sweden, 6000 BC–4200 BC).label: Senmesolitikum
Senmesolitikum (Sweden, 6000 BC–4200 BC).prose:
[Sweden, 6000 BC–4200 BC] Senmesolitikum. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Hunter-fisher-gatherers along the coasts and lakes lived off seals, fish, wild boar and hazelnuts, using slotted bone points set with tiny flint blades and, at the end of the period, pottery. Their large shell middens, dugout canoes and cemeteries with carefully furnished graves show settled, well-fed communities rather than restless wanderers. Farming arrived at the close of the period, brought in by contact with neighbours to the south.

Vroege Middeleeuwen C (Netherlands, AD 7.label: Vroege Middeleeuwen C
Vroege Middeleeuwen C (Netherlands, AD 7.prose:
[Netherlands, AD 725–AD 899] Vroege Middeleeuwen C. Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Carolingian power absorbed Frisia after decades of conflict, and missionaries backed by Frankish arms made Christianity the official religion. Dorestad grew into one of northern Europe's busiest trading places, its wharves handling Rhineland pottery, quernstones and coin, until Viking fleets began raiding the river mouths in the ninth century.

Nieuwe Tijd Laat (Netherlands, AD 1850–A.label: Nieuwe Tijd Laat
Nieuwe Tijd Laat (Netherlands, AD 1850–A.prose:
[Netherlands, AD 1850–AD 1944] Nieuwe Tijd Laat. Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Industry, railways and steam arrived late but fast: the Nieuwe Waterweg and North Sea Canal reopened Rotterdam and Amsterdam to ocean shipping, steam pumps drained land that windmills never could, and cities burst beyond their old walls into brick working-class districts. Society organised itself into confessional and political 'pillars', each with its own schools, papers and clubs. The period closes with occupation, bombing and the fortifications of the Atlantic Wall, all now the subject of conflict archaeology.

Venetian (Cyprus, AD 1489–AD 1571).label: Venetian
Venetian (Cyprus, AD 1489–AD 1571).prose:
[Cyprus, AD 1489–AD 1571] Venetian. no source provided. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Venice took formal control of the island after the last Lusignan queen, Caterina Cornaro, was persuaded to abdicate, running it as a colony geared to sugar, cotton and grain exports. Facing the Ottoman threat, Venetian engineers threw up the massive walls of Nicosia and Famagusta that still ring both cities. The Ottoman invasion of 1570 took Nicosia in weeks; Famagusta held out for nearly a year before falling in 1571.

Laat Romeinse Tijd A (Netherlands, AD 27.label: Laat Romeinse Tijd A
Laat Romeinse Tijd A (Netherlands, AD 27.prose:
[Netherlands, AD 270–AD 349] Laat Romeinse Tijd A. Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Decades of crisis and partial recovery on the Rhine frontier: raids and civil war emptied large parts of the countryside, villa estates collapsed, and settlement contracted sharply. Emperors from Diocletian onward rebuilt a chain of smaller, thick-walled forts and increasingly filled them with soldiers recruited from across the river.

bronasta doba (Slovenia, 1750 BC–751 BC).label: bronasta doba
bronasta doba (Slovenia, 1750 BC–751 BC).prose:
[Slovenia, 1750 BC–751 BC] bronasta doba. ZRC SAZU, Institute of Archaeology. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.
