Bronze working spread through the eastern Alps and the Sava and Drava valleys, supported by local copper ores and by trade routes linking the Adriatic to central Europe. Fortified hilltop settlements appeared, and by the later phases the dead were cremated and buried in vast urnfields — a change in belief as much as in burial practice. Hoards of axes, sickles and scrap bronze buried in the ground are among the most common finds.

Late Middeleeuwen (Netherlands, AD 1050–.label: Late Middeleeuwen
Late Middeleeuwen (Netherlands, AD 1050–.prose:
[Netherlands, AD 1050–AD 1499] Late Middeleeuwen. Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Systematic diking and drainage turned peat bog and marsh into farmland, and the reclaimed landscape of ditches, dwelling mounds and windmills took the shape it still largely has. Towns like Utrecht, Dordrecht, Bruges' northern rivals and the Zuiderzee ports won charters and grew rich on cloth, herring and the carrying trade, joining Hanseatic networks. Political power passed from local counts and bishops to the Burgundian dukes, who gathered the provinces into a single administration.

Bronz i hershëm (Albania, 2100 BC–1801 B.label: Bronz i hershëm
Bronz i hershëm (Albania, 2100 BC–1801 B.prose: [Albania, 2100 BC–1801 BC] Bronz i hershëm. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

srednji neolitik (Slovenia, 4000 BC–3501.label: srednji neolitik
srednji neolitik (Slovenia, 4000 BC–3501.prose:
[Slovenia, 4000 BC–3501 BC] srednji neolitik. ZRC SAZU, Institute of Archaeology. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Farming villages in the Ljubljana Marshes and along the Sava and Drava valleys became firmly established, with pottery styles linking the region both to the Adriatic and to the Danubian world. Cattle, sheep and cereals underpinned settlement, and the first copper objects began to circulate. The distinctive pile-dwellings on the marsh margins, later famous for their preserved wooden piles and a wooden wheel, belong to this broad horizon.

Laat Neolithicum (Netherlands, 2850 BC–2.label: Laat Neolithicum
Laat Neolithicum (Netherlands, 2850 BC–2.prose:
[Netherlands, 2850 BC–2001 BC] Laat Neolithicum. Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Farming communities across the Low Countries adopted new burial rites and new drinking and weapon sets, first the battle-axes and beakers of the Corded Ware world, then the distinctive Bell Beaker package. Single graves under low round barrows replaced older communal monuments, and copper objects and the first metalworking knowledge appeared. Ordinary life still combined cereal cultivation, cattle, and heavy reliance on wild resources in the wetlands.

Äldre stenålder (Sweden, 8200 BC–4200 BC.label: Äldre stenålder
Äldre stenålder (Sweden, 8200 BC–4200 BC.prose:
[Sweden, 8200 BC–4200 BC] Äldre stenålder. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

As the ice sheet melted back, hunter-gatherer-fishers followed the retreating shoreline into what became Sweden, living on seal, fish, elk and wild plants and moving between coastal and inland camps. Their toolkits of flint blades, microliths, bone points and dugout canoes link them to the Maglemose, Kongemose and Ertebølle traditions of the southern Baltic. Rapid land uplift and sea-level change means many of their settlements now lie far inland or beneath the sea, which is why coastal sites are so prized by archaeologists.

Vasatiden (Sweden, AD 1521–AD 1654).label: Vasatiden
Vasatiden (Sweden, AD 1521–AD 1654).prose:
[Sweden, AD 1521–AD 1654] Vasatiden. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Gustav Vasa's rebellion broke Sweden out of the Kalmar Union and made him king of a state he then rebuilt: church lands were seized, the Reformation imposed, and the crown made hereditary in his family. His successors turned a poor, thinly populated kingdom into a Baltic military power, financed by copper and iron and expanded by war in Livonia, Poland and Germany. The era's monuments – Vasa castles, Lutheran churches and the warship Vasa itself – come from this drive to look like a European great power.

Néolithique moyen (France, 5300 BC–4501.label: Néolithique moyen
Néolithique moyen (France, 5300 BC–4501.prose:
[France, 5300 BC–4501 BC] Néolithique moyen. INRAP. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Farming communities across France moved beyond the tightly uniform longhouse villages of the first settlers into a patchwork of regional groups with their own pottery and burial customs. In the west, people began raising long earthen mounds and stone chambered tombs – among the earliest monumental architecture in Europe – while enclosures ringed by ditches and palisades appeared in the north and the Paris basin. Cattle herding, flint mining and long-distance movement of polished stone axes tied these communities together.

Néolitique récent (France, 4500 BC–2201.label: Néolitique récent
Néolitique récent (France, 4500 BC–2201.prose:
[France, 4500 BC–2201 BC] Néolitique récent. INRAP. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Late farming societies in France left their most conspicuous monuments in this span: dolmens, passage graves and standing stones, alongside ditched enclosures and large flint-mining fields. Regional pottery traditions multiplied, and collective burial in stone chambers became widespread. The period closes with the arrival of copper metallurgy and Beaker pottery.

Доцна во архајскиот период (Republic of.node: Доцна во архајскиот период (Republic of Macedonia, 600 BC–501 BC)
Доцна во архајскиот период (Republic of.label: Доцна во архајскиот период
Доцна во архајскиот период (Republic of.prose:
[Macedonia, 600 BC–501 BC] Доцна во архајскиот период. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Greek colonies on the Aegean coast and Paeonian and Illyrian communities inland were drawn into a wider Mediterranean economy of coinage, imported pottery and monumental building. The Argead kings began consolidating a Macedonian territorial state, and after 512 BC the region fell within the orbit of the Persian Empire, whose armies marched through it on their way to Greece. The rich burials at sites such as Trebenishte show local elites with silver masks, gold ornaments and Greek bronze vessels.

Perandorake e vonë (Albania, AD 300–AD 5.label: Perandorake e vonë
Perandorake e vonë (Albania, AD 300–AD 5.prose:
[Albania, AD 300–AD 564] Perandorake e vonë. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Diocletian's reorganisation made these lands a strategic corridor between the empire's halves, guarded by fortified towns and controlling the road from the Adriatic to Constantinople. Christianity became dominant, and basilicas with mosaic floors were built at Butrint, Byllis and Lin. Gothic and Hunnic raids, earthquakes and plague thinned the cities, and Justinian's fortress-building was the last great imperial investment before the Slavic migrations.

Iron Age (Poland, 400 BC–AD 99).label: Iron Age
Iron Age (Poland, 400 BC–AD 99).prose:
[Poland, 400 BC–AD 99] Iron Age. ARENA1/ADS. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The formative era of the southern Levant, when the Canaanite city-state system gave way to territorial kingdoms - Israel, Judah, Philistia, Phoenician ports and the Transjordanian states. Iron tools became common, olive oil and wine were produced on an industrial scale, and alphabetic script came into everyday administrative use. The period closes with conquest by Assyria and Babylon and the destruction of Jerusalem's temple, the setting for much of the Hebrew Bible.

Römische (Germany, AD 1–AD 374).label: Römische
Römische (Germany, AD 1–AD 374).prose:
[Germany, Switzerland, Czech Republic, Liechtenstein, AD 1–AD 374] Römische. Spatial coverage: Czech Republic, Germany, Liechtenstein, Switzerland. no source provided. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The centuries when the Rhine and Danube marked the edge of the Roman world and the lands beyond looked in. Behind the limes grew cities like Cologne, Trier and Mainz, with stone architecture, wine, baths and coinage; outside it, Germanic groups traded, served in the army and coalesced into larger confederations. Sustained raiding from the third century onward eroded the frontier long before it finally gave way.

Erteböllekulturen (Sweden, 5200 BC–4000.label: Erteböllekulturen
Erteböllekulturen (Sweden, 5200 BC–4000.prose:
[Sweden, 5200 BC–4000 BC] Erteböllekulturen. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The last hunter-fisher societies of southern Scandinavia, living in large coastal settlements and leaving behind enormous mounds of oyster and mussel shells. They made pointed-base pottery and blubber lamps, fished from dugout canoes with nets and traps, and buried their dead in cemeteries — signs of a settled, prosperous way of life without farming. They traded with and knew about the farmers to the south for centuries before finally adopting crops and livestock.

Frühe Römische (Austria, AD 1–AD 179).label: Frühe Römische
Frühe Römische (Austria, AD 1–AD 179).prose:
[Austria, AD 1–AD 179] Frühe Römische. Austrian Academy of Sciences. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The Alpine kingdom of Noricum passed peacefully into Roman hands and was joined to the Danube frontier province of Pannonia, bringing legions, roads and towns. Cities like Virunum and Carnuntum grew up around administration and the army, Norican iron was exported across the empire, and local elites adopted Latin, togas and stone inscriptions. The period closes with the Marcomannic Wars, when Germanic armies broke across the Danube and ended the long frontier peace.

Späte Bronzezeit (Germany, 1300 BC–800 B.label: Späte Bronzezeit
Späte Bronzezeit (Germany, 1300 BC–800 B.prose:
[Germany, Switzerland, Czech Republic, Liechtenstein, 1300 BC–800 BC] Späte Bronzezeit. Spatial coverage: Czech Republic, Germany, Liechtenstein, Switzerland. no source provided. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The Urnfield tradition spread across central Europe: the dead were cremated and buried in pottery urns in large flat cemeteries, replacing the barrows of earlier centuries. Bronze-working reached industrial scale, with sheet-metal vessels, shields and swords, and huge hoards were deposited in rivers and bogs. Fortified hilltop settlements suggest growing competition over metal routes.

Späte Römische (Germany, AD 180–AD 374).label: Späte Römische
Späte Römische (Germany, AD 180–AD 374).prose:
[Germany, Switzerland, Czech Republic, Liechtenstein, AD 180–AD 374] Späte Römische. Spatial coverage: Czech Republic, Germany, Liechtenstein, Switzerland. no source provided. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

In the Germanic provinces the Marcomannic wars marked the end of easy frontier security; by the mid-third century the Limes east of the Rhine was abandoned and the Agri Decumates lost to the Alamanni. Roman life retreated behind fortified towns and river forts, with new burgi and heavily walled settlements along the Rhine and Danube, while Germanic groups settled inside the frontier as soldiers and farmers.

Eneolitic Dezvoltat (Romania, 4600 BC–38.label: Eneolitic Dezvoltat
Eneolitic Dezvoltat (Romania, 4600 BC–38.prose:
[Romania, 4600 BC–3801 BC] Eneolitic Dezvoltat. Romanian Academy. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The peak of Copper Age society in the Carpathian-Danubian region, when Cucuteni and Gumelnita communities lived in large planned villages, produced spectacular multicoloured painted pottery, and traded copper, gold, Spondylus shell and flint over long distances. Population and craft specialisation reached levels not seen again for millennia, before the tells were abandoned and steppe-influenced groups moved in.

Osmane (Albania, AD 1389–AD 1849).label: Osmane
Osmane (Albania, AD 1389–AD 1849).prose:
[Albania, AD 1389–AD 1849] Osmane. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Ottoman rule reshaped Albanian society over more than four centuries: Skanderbeg's long resistance in the fifteenth century became the founding national legend, but after his death the highlands and coastal towns were absorbed into the empire's provincial system. Large numbers converted to Islam, Albanians rose to the highest offices in Istanbul and Cairo, and semi-independent pashas such as Ali of Tepelena carved out near-sovereign domains. Mosques, bridges, bazaars and hillside citadels from these centuries still dominate towns like Berat and Gjirokastër.

Ältere Kupferzeit (Austria, 4250 BC–3401.label: Ältere Kupferzeit
Ältere Kupferzeit (Austria, 4250 BC–3401.prose:
[Austria, 4250 BC–3401 BC] Ältere Kupferzeit. Austrian Academy of Sciences. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Copper objects — flat axes, awls, daggers and ornaments — begin appearing in Central European graves and settlements, evidence of smelting and casting knowledge spreading up from the south-east. Farming communities such as the Michelsberg culture built large ditched enclosures on hilltops and river terraces, while in the north the first megalithic tombs were being raised. Metal was still rare and largely a marker of status rather than a workaday material, but the skills involved would transform the following centuries.

visoki srednji vek (Slovenia, AD 1000–AD.label: visoki srednji vek
visoki srednji vek (Slovenia, AD 1000–AD.prose:
[Slovenia, AD 1000–AD 1299] visoki srednji vek. ZRC SAZU, Institute of Archaeology. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Castles, market towns and monasteries reshaped the Slovene lands as noble families and church lordships carved out territories under the Holy Roman Empire. Population grew, forests were cleared for new villages, and mining and trade routes over the Alps brought coin and craft goods. Many towns that still exist received their charters and walls in these centuries.

Mellanneolitisk tid B (Sweden, 2800 BC–2.label: Mellanneolitisk tid B
Mellanneolitisk tid B (Sweden, 2800 BC–2.prose:
[Sweden, 2800 BC–2400 BC] Mellanneolitisk tid B. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The Battle Axe culture, the Scandinavian branch of the Corded Ware world, brought a new burial custom: individual graves with the body on its side, a cord-decorated beaker and a polished stone axe shaped like a boat. Collective megalithic burial faded and the emphasis shifted to the single person, herding and mobility. Ancient DNA links these people to migrations out of the eastern steppes, a population shift that left its mark on later Scandinavian ancestry.

Bajo Romano (Spain, AD 200–AD 399).label: Bajo Romano
Bajo Romano (Spain, AD 200–AD 399).prose:
[Spain, AD 200–AD 399] Bajo Romano. Institute of Heritage Sciences, Spanish National Research Council (CSIC Incipit). Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Hispania passed through third-century insecurity into the reorganised empire of Diocletian and Constantine, split into new provinces under a vicarius and taxed more heavily. Cities shrank behind walls while enormous rural villas with mosaic floors — Carranque, La Olmeda, Centcelles — became the centres of aristocratic power and wealth. Christianity spread fast, producing bishops, the council of Elvira and the Priscillianist controversy, and the landowning elite that emerged here survived to serve the Visigothic kings.

Bronsålder (Sweden, 1800 BC–500 BC).label: Bronsålder
Bronsålder (Sweden, 1800 BC–500 BC).prose:
[Sweden, 1800 BC–500 BC] Bronsålder. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Southern Scandinavia had no copper or tin of its own, yet became one of the richest bronze-using regions in Europe by trading amber, furs and hides southwards along routes to central Europe and the Mediterranean. The wealth shows in mound burials with swords and folding stools, in the great bronze lurs, and in tens of thousands of rock carvings of ships, sun discs and warriors along the Bohuslän coast. It is also the period when the sun-and-ship imagery that underlies later Norse cosmology first appears.

Midden Romeinse Tijd B (Netherlands, AD.label: Midden Romeinse Tijd B
Midden Romeinse Tijd B (Netherlands, AD.prose:
[Netherlands, AD 150–AD 269] Midden Romeinse Tijd B. Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Prosperity along the frontier peaked and then faltered: villas and rural settlements were at their most numerous around AD 150-200, before troop withdrawals, Germanic raids and worsening drainage emptied much of the countryside. Hoards of coins and silver buried in the mid-third century mark the disruption. By the end, many forts and farms in the western river area stood abandoned.

srednja bakrena doba (Slovenia, 2500 BC–.label: srednja bakrena doba
srednja bakrena doba (Slovenia, 2500 BC–.prose:
[Slovenia, 2500 BC–2201 BC] srednja bakrena doba. ZRC SAZU, Institute of Archaeology. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Copper metallurgy was now established, with cast axes and daggers circulating alongside distinctive decorated pottery linked to Danubian traditions. Communities lived in pile-built settlements on the Ljubljana Marshes and in upland caves and hilltop sites, herding livestock and taking part in exchange networks that reached the Adriatic and the Carpathian Basin.

középső vaskor (Hungary, 700 BC–451 BC).label: középső vaskor
középső vaskor (Hungary, 700 BC–451 BC).prose:
[Hungary, 700 BC–451 BC] középső vaskor. Hungarian National Museum. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Horse-riding groups of the eastern steppe orbit reached the Great Plain, bringing trilobate arrowheads, animal-style bronzes and the horse gear that archaeologists label the Vekerzug or Scythian-period culture. Western Transdanubia meanwhile looked to the Hallstatt world, with rich tumulus burials and hillforts. Iron became an everyday material, and the region sat on the frontier between Mediterranean-facing Europe and the steppe.

Epoca Migraţiilor (Romania, AD 374–AD 79.label: Epoca Migraţiilor
Epoca Migraţiilor (Romania, AD 374–AD 79.prose:
[Romania, AD 374–AD 799] Epoca Migraţiilor. Romanian Academy. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Wave after wave of peoples crossed or settled the lands north of the Danube: Goths and Gepids, the Huns under Attila, then Avars and Slavs. Roman towns decayed, coin use dwindled, and settlement shifted to small villages, but Christianity survived and Slavic groups settled permanently, reshaping the region's languages and place names.

Epoca Post Romană (Romania, AD 275–AD 37.label: Epoca Post Romană
Epoca Post Romană (Romania, AD 275–AD 37.prose:
[Romania, AD 275–AD 373] Epoca Post Romană. Romanian Academy. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

After Aurelian pulled the army and administration back across the Danube, the former province was left to Free Dacians, Goths and Sarmatians, and to a mixed population who kept using Roman coins, pottery and Latin. The Sântana de Mureș–Chernyakhov culture spread across the region and Christianity took root, until the Huns shattered the Gothic order.

République romaine (France, 50 BC–28 BC).label: République romaine
République romaine (France, 50 BC–28 BC).prose:
[France, 50 BC–28 BC] République romaine. INRAP. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The last generation of the Roman Republic, when Caesar's newly conquered Gaul was absorbed into a state tearing itself apart in civil war. Gallic communities were reorganised, taxed and drawn into Roman military recruitment, and local elites began the shift to Latin, coinage and Roman-style towns that would define the provinces under the empire that followed.

Eneolitic Timpuriu (Romania, 5000 BC–460.label: Eneolitic Timpuriu
Eneolitic Timpuriu (Romania, 5000 BC–460.prose:
[Romania, 5000 BC–4601 BC] Eneolitic Timpuriu. Romanian Academy. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The first phase of copper use among the region's farming communities, when small cast and hammered tools and ornaments appear alongside older stone technology. Villages of the Boian, Hamangia and Precucuteni groups grew larger and more permanent, building up the earliest tells and developing the incised and painted pottery styles that would culminate in the Cucuteni tradition.

La Tène A (Germany, 480 BC–401 BC).label: La Tène A
La Tène A (Germany, 480 BC–401 BC).prose:
[Germany, Switzerland, Czech Republic, Liechtenstein, 480 BC–401 BC] La Tène A. Spatial coverage: Czech Republic, Germany, Liechtenstein, Switzerland. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The opening phase of the La Tène Iron Age, when a wealthy elite in the Rhine, Moselle and Marne regions buried its dead with two-wheeled chariots, gold neck-rings and imported Etruscan and Greek wine service. Out of contact with those Mediterranean imports came the Early Style of Celtic art, which took palmettes, lotus buds and lion masks and reworked them into the swirling, ambiguous designs seen on the Glauberg and Reinheim finds. The old Hallstatt hillfort centres further west collapsed at about this time, and power shifted north.

Midden Bronstijd B (Netherlands, 1500 BC.label: Midden Bronstijd B
Midden Bronstijd B (Netherlands, 1500 BC.prose:
[Netherlands, 1500 BC–1101 BC] Midden Bronstijd B. Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The classic Dutch Bronze Age landscape: three-aisled byre-houses up to thirty metres long, rebuilt every generation on shifting plots, with fields, wells and cattle pens around them. Bronze circulated far more freely now, deposited in rivers and bogs as well as buried with the dead, and cremation under low mounds became the norm. The period ends as barrow cemeteries give way to the great urnfields.

Hekur i zhvilluar (Albania, 800 BC–601 B.label: Hekur i zhvilluar
Hekur i zhvilluar (Albania, 800 BC–601 B.prose: [Albania, 800 BC–601 BC] Hekur i zhvilluar. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Recent (Netherlands, AD 1945–AD 2000).label: Recent
Recent (Netherlands, AD 1945–AD 2000).prose:
[Netherlands, AD 1945–AD 2000] Recent. Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Marshall Aid, rapid industrial rebuilding and Groningen gas turned a war-shattered country into one of Europe's richest, with an extensive welfare state and the world's largest port at Rotterdam. The Netherlands lost Indonesia in 1949 and turned instead to European integration, signing the treaties that created the EEC and, at Maastricht, the European Union. Delta Works sea defences, built after the 1953 flood, and a liberal social climate on drugs, abortion and sexuality became national hallmarks.

Bronz (Albania, 2100 BC–1101 BC).label: Bronz
Bronz (Albania, 2100 BC–1101 BC).prose: [Albania, 2100 BC–1101 BC] Bronz. This period is derived from the aggregation of three periods in the 2004 Fasti Periodization:. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Bronz i mesëm (Albania, 1800 BC–1501 BC).label: Bronz i mesëm
Bronz i mesëm (Albania, 1800 BC–1501 BC).prose: [Albania, 1800 BC–1501 BC] Bronz i mesëm. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

second âge du Fer (France, 450 BC–51 BC).node: second âge du Fer (France, 450 BC–51 BC)

second âge du Fer (France, 450 BC–51 BC).prose:
[France, 450 BC–51 BC] second âge du Fer. INRAP. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The La Tène era, when Gaulish societies developed a distinctive curvilinear art style, struck their own gold and silver coinage, and traded wine and slaves with the Mediterranean. In its last centuries people concentrated in oppida – large fortified towns with workshops, mints and imported goods – until Caesar's campaigns of the 50s BC brought the whole territory under Rome.

Neuzeit (Germany, AD 1500–AD 1849).label: Neuzeit
Neuzeit (Germany, AD 1500–AD 1849).prose:
[Germany, Switzerland, Czech Republic, Liechtenstein, AD 1500–AD 1849] Neuzeit. Spatial coverage: Czech Republic, Germany, Liechtenstein, Switzerland. no source provided. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The centuries in which the German lands passed through the Reformation, the devastation of the Thirty Years' War, the rise of Prussia, the Napoleonic upheaval and the first stirrings of industry and national unification. Printing, gunpowder fortification, overseas trade goods and porcelain reshaped daily life and material culture. Archaeologically it is the age of surviving townscapes, factory sites and mass-produced ceramics and glass.

Edad del Bronce Final (Spain, 1200 BC–80.node: Edad del Bronce Final (Spain, 1200 BC–801 BC)
Edad del Bronce Final (Spain, 1200 BC–80.label: Edad del Bronce Final
Edad del Bronce Final (Spain, 1200 BC–80.prose:
[Spain, 1200 BC–801 BC] Edad del Bronce Final. Institute of Heritage Sciences, Spanish National Research Council (CSIC Incipit). Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Long-distance Atlantic exchange peaked, moving bronze weapons, cauldrons and gold ornaments between Iberia, Brittany, Britain and Ireland, while carved warrior stelae in the southwest depict shields, swords and mirrors as symbols of rank. In the south, contacts with the eastern Mediterranean prepared the ground for Phoenician colonies and the emergence of Tartessos. Hoards of scrap and finished metal from these centuries are among the richest in western Europe.

Iron Age (Denmark, 500 BC–AD 1049).label: Iron Age
Iron Age (Denmark, 500 BC–AD 1049).prose:
[Denmark, 500 BC–AD 1049] Iron Age. ARENA1/ADS. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The formative era of the southern Levant, when the Canaanite city-state system gave way to territorial kingdoms - Israel, Judah, Philistia, Phoenician ports and the Transjordanian states. Iron tools became common, olive oil and wine were produced on an industrial scale, and alphabetic script came into everyday administrative use. The period closes with conquest by Assyria and Babylon and the destruction of Jerusalem's temple, the setting for much of the Hebrew Bible.

Folkungatiden (Sweden, AD 1250–AD 1363).label: Folkungatiden
Folkungatiden (Sweden, AD 1250–AD 1363).prose:
[Sweden, AD 1250–AD 1363] Folkungatiden. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Sweden under the Bjälbo dynasty, begun when Birger Jarl put his son on the throne and ruled in his name. Royal power grew with written law, a tax-paying peasantry and a knightly nobility exempt from tax in return for cavalry service; towns like Stockholm were founded and German merchants of the Hanse settled in them. Dynastic quarrels and the deposition of Magnus Eriksson ended the period and pulled Sweden into union politics with Denmark and Norway.

kora vaskor (Hungary, 900 BC–701 BC).label: kora vaskor
kora vaskor (Hungary, 900 BC–701 BC).prose:
[Hungary, 900 BC–701 BC] kora vaskor. Hungarian National Museum. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Iron replaced bronze for edged tools and weapons as the Carpathian Basin was drawn into the Hallstatt world to the west and the steppe world to the east. Eastern horse-riding groups brought new bridle gear, trilobate arrowheads and animal-style ornament, while western Transdanubia saw richly furnished tumulus burials. Fortified hilltop centres and a growing gap between elite and ordinary graves mark the period.

Midden Bronstijd A (Netherlands, 1800 BC.label: Midden Bronstijd A
Midden Bronstijd A (Netherlands, 1800 BC.prose:
[Netherlands, 1800 BC–1501 BC] Midden Bronstijd A. Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

A transitional phase in which Bronze Age lifeways took hold but metal remained rare, with the Hilversum, Drakenstein and Elp traditions producing coarse, bucket-shaped urns. The dead were still buried under round barrows, often in cemeteries reused for centuries, and the first substantial farmhouses appear. Contacts across the North Sea, especially with southern Britain, show in pottery styles and burial practice.

Frühe Bronzezeit (Germany, 2200 BC–1601.label: Frühe Bronzezeit
Frühe Bronzezeit (Germany, 2200 BC–1601.prose:
[Germany, Switzerland, Czech Republic, Liechtenstein, 2200 BC–1601 BC] Frühe Bronzezeit. Spatial coverage: Czech Republic, Germany, Liechtenstein, Switzerland. no source provided. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Copper and tin alloys replace pure copper, and metalworking becomes an organised industry supplying axes, daggers and pins across long distances. Alpine copper ores drew traders from far afield, and buried hoards of ingots and ornaments show both wealth and insecurity. Settlements become more permanent and cemeteries more orderly, with grave goods marking out ranks within communities for the first time.

âge du Bronze moyen (France, 1600 BC–140.node: âge du Bronze moyen (France, 1600 BC–1401 BC)
âge du Bronze moyen (France, 1600 BC–140.label: âge du Bronze moyen
âge du Bronze moyen (France, 1600 BC–140.prose:
[France, 1600 BC–1401 BC] âge du Bronze moyen. INRAP. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Settlements became more permanent and field systems more organised, while metalworkers turned out palstave axes, rapiers and elaborate ornaments in growing quantities. Burial under barrows, often with weapons, marked out warrior elites. The scale of bronze circulation in this phase shows communities firmly locked into continental exchange networks.

Äldre järnålder (Sweden, 500 BC–AD 400).label: Äldre järnålder
Äldre järnålder (Sweden, 500 BC–AD 400).prose:
[Sweden, 500 BC–AD 400] Äldre järnålder. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Iron smelted from bog ore replaced imported bronze, putting metal within reach of ordinary farmers and changing tools, weapons and land clearance. Villages of longhouses with stone-walled field systems spread across Öland, Gotland and the mainland; hillforts multiplied, and Roman glass, bronze and coins reached the north through trade and mercenary service. Weapon-rich graves and the earliest runic inscriptions signal an emerging warrior aristocracy.

Hellenistic II (Cyprus, 150 BC–51 BC).label: Hellenistic II
Hellenistic II (Cyprus, 150 BC–51 BC).prose:
[Cyprus, 150 BC–51 BC] Hellenistic II. Jamieson, 2007 (Ian Potter Museum exhibition). Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Ptolemaic rule continued but weakened as Egypt itself fell into dynastic crisis and Roman interference. Rome annexed the island in 58 BC, briefly restored it to Cleopatra, and finally absorbed it for good - a shift from Alexandrian to Roman orbit that reoriented Cypriot trade and administration westward.

Senneolitikum (Sweden, 2400 BC–1800 BC).label: Senneolitikum
Senneolitikum (Sweden, 2400 BC–1800 BC).prose:
[Sweden, 2400 BC–1800 BC] Senneolitikum. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Farming communities across the south adopted the flint dagger, skilfully pressure-flaked in imitation of imported metal blades and produced almost industrially at the Scanian mine sites. Large gallery graves held collective burials, longhouses grew substantial, and the first copper and bronze objects trickled in through wide exchange networks. These contacts set up the metal-rich Bronze Age that followed.

Republikane (Albania, 168 BC–AD 1).label: Republikane
Republikane (Albania, 168 BC–AD 1).prose:
[Albania, 168 BC–AD 1] Republikane. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Roman power replaced the Illyrian kingdoms after the defeat of King Gentius, and the lands of present-day Albania were absorbed into the Republic's Balkan holdings. The Via Egnatia was driven across the region, linking the Adriatic ports of Dyrrachium and Apollonia to Macedonia and, ultimately, to the East. Those coastal cities grew rich as gateways between Italy and the Greek world, and Roman legions repeatedly used them as staging grounds in the civil wars.

Neolithic (Cyprus, 4600 BC–4001 BC).label: Neolithic
Neolithic (Cyprus, 4600 BC–4001 BC).prose:
[Cyprus, 4600 BC–4001 BC] Neolithic. Jamieson, 2007 (Ian Potter Museum exhibition). Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

In the southern Levant this is where farming villages first take hold: wheat, barley, sheep and goats replace foraging, and settlements like Jericho grow to unprecedented size behind stone walls and a tower. Households plastered their floors, kept the skulls of their dead under them and modelled faces onto them in plaster, and at 'Ain Ghazal produced large human statues of lime plaster over reed frames. Pottery arrives only in the later centuries, long after the farming economy itself.

среден eнеолит (Bulgaria, 4600 BC–4401 B.label: среден eнеолит
среден eнеолит (Bulgaria, 4600 BC–4401 B.prose:
[Bulgaria, 4600 BC–4401 BC] среден eнеолит. National Institute of Archaeology with Museum, Automated Information System "Archaeological Map of Bulgaria". Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Farming communities kept piling up tell settlements, layer on layer, on the plains of the lower Danube and Thrace, living in tightly packed rectangular houses with painted pottery and clay figurines. Copper working moved beyond trinkets to heavy cast axes and hammer-axes, fed by deep shaft mining at sites such as Ai Bunar. The accumulation of metal, gold and imported shell in a few hands set the stage for the extraordinarily rich cemeteries of the following centuries.

енеолитот (Republic of Macedonia, 4500 B.label: енеолитот
енеолитот (Republic of Macedonia, 4500 B.prose:
[Macedonia, 4500 BC–2201 BC] енеолитот. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Farming communities added copper tools and ornaments to a long-established village way of life, working ore from local sources and exchanging finished metal with neighbouring regions. Settlements included both lowland villages and upland sites, and painted and burnished pottery styles link the area to Aegean and Danubian traditions. The later stages of the period brought greater mobility and new burial customs, marking the transition toward the Bronze Age.

късно средновековие (Bulgaria, AD 1396–A.label: късно средновековие
късно средновековие (Bulgaria, AD 1396–A.prose:
[Bulgaria, AD 1396–AD 1761] късно средновековие. National Institute of Archaeology with Museum, Automated Information System "Archaeological Map of Bulgaria". Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Ottoman rule replaced the Bulgarian tsardoms: the aristocracy disappeared, church hierarchy was subordinated to Constantinople, and towns were reshaped around mosques, hans, hamams and covered markets. Land was redistributed under timar tenure, Christian villages paid the poll tax, and some populations converted or were resettled. Monasteries preserved literacy and painting, and this long span of provincial life ends as revolts and the first stirrings of national revival begin.

La Tène II (France, 260 BC–151 BC).label: La Tène II
La Tène II (France, 260 BC–151 BC).prose:
[France, 260 BC–151 BC] La Tène II. INRAP. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The middle Celtic Iron Age, defined by long iron swords in decorated scabbards, new brooch forms, and cremation replacing inhumation across much of Gaul. Settlement shifted toward larger open villages and the first defended centres, and Gallic mercenaries and migrants ranged from Italy to Anatolia. Craft production in iron, glass and coinage became increasingly specialised.

Laat Neolithicum B (Netherlands, 2450 BC.label: Laat Neolithicum B
Laat Neolithicum B (Netherlands, 2450 BC.prose:
[Netherlands, 2450 BC–2001 BC] Laat Neolithicum B. Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The Bell Beaker phase, recognised by finely decorated drinking vessels, archers' wristguards, flint daggers and the first copper ornaments and tools in the region. Beaker graves belong to a network of contacts stretching from Iberia to central Europe, and the barrows raised over them were often added to existing cemeteries. It sets up the metal-using societies of the Bronze Age that follow.

Völkerwanderungszeit (Austria, AD 375–AD.label: Völkerwanderungszeit
Völkerwanderungszeit (Austria, AD 375–AD.prose:
[Austria, AD 375–AD 567] Völkerwanderungszeit. Austrian Academy of Sciences. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Roman Noricum and Pannonia unravelled as Goths, Huns, Lombards and others moved through and settled the Danube provinces. Towns shrank to fortified hilltop refuges, the frontier garrisons dissolved, and the population that stayed mixed with the newcomers. The period ends with the Lombards leaving for Italy and Avars and Slavs filling the space behind them.

zgodnja bakrena doba (Slovenia, 2800 BC–.label: zgodnja bakrena doba
zgodnja bakrena doba (Slovenia, 2800 BC–.prose:
[Slovenia, 2800 BC–2501 BC] zgodnja bakrena doba. ZRC SAZU, Institute of Archaeology. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Copper working spread into the Slovenian lands during the Eneolithic, with axes, awls and daggers cast from smelted ore appearing alongside the older stone toolkit — the first time metal reshaped both economy and status. Settlement included pile-dwelling villages on the Ljubljana Marshes, whose waterlogged remains preserve wooden posts, pottery and even textiles. Cattle-herding, wheeled transport and contacts along the Danube and Adriatic routes bound the region into a wider Central European world.

Yngre bronsålder (Sweden, 1100 BC–500 BC.label: Yngre bronsålder
Yngre bronsålder (Sweden, 1100 BC–500 BC.prose:
[Sweden, 1100 BC–500 BC] Yngre bronsålder. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Cremation and urn burial replaced mound inhumation, and bronze was worked into thin ornamental sheet metal, hanging vessels and lur trumpets, much of it deliberately deposited in bogs and lakes. This is the period of the great rock-carving sites of Bohuslän and Östergötland, with their ships, sun discs and processions, and of far-reaching trade that carried southern metal deep into Scandinavia.

Vroeg Romeinse Tijd A (Netherlands, 12 B.label: Vroeg Romeinse Tijd A
Vroeg Romeinse Tijd A (Netherlands, 12 B.prose:
[Netherlands, 12 BC–AD 24] Vroeg Romeinse Tijd A. Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The decades of conquest and consolidation, beginning with Drusus' campaigns and the building of bases along the Rhine and the Waal. Germanicus' expeditions into free Germany ended without permanent gain, and Rome settled for holding the river line, dealing with the Batavians and Frisians as tribute-paying allies who supplied cavalry to the army.

Mittel Neolithikum (Germany, 4800 BC–425.label: Mittel Neolithikum
Mittel Neolithikum (Germany, 4800 BC–425.prose:
[Germany, Switzerland, Czech Republic, Liechtenstein, 4800 BC–4251 BC] Mittel Neolithikum. Spatial coverage: Czech Republic, Germany, Liechtenstein, Switzerland. no source provided. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Farming communities of the Danube basin in this period built enormous circular ditched enclosures, the Kreisgrabenanlagen, with precisely aligned entrance causeways that are among Europe's oldest monumental architecture. The Lengyel culture's painted pottery, longhouse villages and copper ornaments show settled communities with growing social complexity. Why the enclosures were built, and why they were abandoned within a few centuries, remains debated.

Tidig medeltid (Sweden, AD 1050–AD 1200).label: Tidig medeltid
Tidig medeltid (Sweden, AD 1050–AD 1200).prose:
[Sweden, AD 1050–AD 1200] Tidig medeltid. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Sweden became Christian in these generations: bishoprics were established, the last pagan cult centre at Uppsala gave way to a cathedral, and wooden churches were replaced by stone ones whose fonts and portals survive across the countryside. Rune stones fell out of fashion as parchment charters and Latin literacy arrived with monks and canons. Rival royal houses, the Sverkers and the Eriks, fought for a crown that was still elective, while Sigtuna, Skara and Visby grew into real towns.

Late Middeleeuwen B (Netherlands, AD 125.label: Late Middeleeuwen B
Late Middeleeuwen B (Netherlands, AD 125.prose:
[Netherlands, AD 1250–AD 1499] Late Middeleeuwen B. Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Towns dominated: brick town halls, weigh houses and Gothic churches went up, guilds organised production, and Holland's ports moved cloth, grain, beer and herring across northern Europe. Repeated storm surges reshaped the coast and enlarged the Zuiderzee, while plague and civil wars such as the Hook and Cod struggles disrupted the countryside. Burgundian dukes absorbed the provinces one by one, laying the administrative groundwork for the later Netherlands.

Edad Media central (Spain, AD 700–AD 119.label: Edad Media central
Edad Media central (Spain, AD 700–AD 119.prose:
[Spain, AD 700–AD 1199] Edad Media central. Institute of Heritage Sciences, Spanish National Research Council (CSIC Incipit). Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The centuries of al-Andalus at its height and of the Christian counter-advance: the Umayyad caliphate of Córdoba flourished and then shattered into taifa kingdoms, inviting Almoravid and Almohad intervention from North Africa. Northern kingdoms — León, Castile, Navarre, Aragon, Portugal — pushed south, repopulating conquered land with charters and towns, while the pilgrimage road to Santiago de Compostela drew people and Romanesque architecture across the Pyrenees. The decisive Christian victory at Las Navas de Tolosa in 1212 opened Andalusia to conquest.

Midden Neolithicum (Netherlands, 4200 BC.label: Midden Neolithicum
Midden Neolithicum (Netherlands, 4200 BC.prose:
[Netherlands, 4200 BC–2851 BC] Midden Neolithicum. Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Farming took hold unevenly: in the wetlands people kept hunting, fishing and fowling while adding cattle, pigs and cereals, whereas on the northern sand the Funnel Beaker communities built the megalithic hunebedden. Pottery, polished flint axes and permanent settlement sites become common finds. The period ends with the arrival of Corded Ware people and a very different burial tradition.

premier âge du Fer (France, 800 BC–451 B.node: premier âge du Fer (France, 800 BC–451 BC)
premier âge du Fer (France, 800 BC–451 B.label: premier âge du Fer
premier âge du Fer (France, 800 BC–451 B.prose:
[France, 800 BC–451 BC] premier âge du Fer. INRAP. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Iron replaced bronze as the everyday working metal, and Hallstatt-period elites in eastern and central Gaul built hilltop strongholds that controlled trade up the Rhône and Seine. Their power shows in spectacular burials under great mounds, furnished with four-wheeled wagons, gold torcs and imported Greek and Etruscan bronzes and wine vessels, the Vix krater being the most famous. This traffic in Mediterranean luxuries drew the region into a wider commercial world and set the stage for the Celtic societies of the following centuries.

Mellanneolitikum (Sweden, 3300 BC–2400 B.label: Mellanneolitikum
Mellanneolitikum (Sweden, 3300 BC–2400 B.prose:
[Sweden, 3300 BC–2400 BC] Mellanneolitikum. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Farming societies split into strikingly different traditions: megalith-building Funnel Beaker communities, the seal-hunting and fish-eating Pitted Ware people of the eastern coasts, and finally the Battle Axe groups with their single graves and corded pottery. Long stone chambers and passage graves were filled with generations of bones and offerings, while amber, flint axes and elaborately decorated pots moved along wide exchange networks. It is the period when Sweden's ancestry and culture were reshaped by newcomers from the Continental steppe world.

средна бронзова епоха (Bulgaria, 1900 BC.label: средна бронзова епоха
средна бронзова епоха (Bulgaria, 1900 BC.prose:
[Bulgaria, 1900 BC–1601 BC] средна бронзова епоха. National Institute of Archaeology with Museum, Automated Information System "Archaeological Map of Bulgaria". Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Settlement becomes hard to find in this stretch of Bulgarian prehistory: the big tells were largely abandoned and the clearest traces are burial mounds raised over crouched or cremated bodies. Populations seem to have been more mobile and pastoral, working bronze in forms shared across the Carpathian basin and the Aegean fringe. The period bridges the tell-dwelling world of earlier prehistory and the wealthy, Mycenaean-linked warrior societies of the Late Bronze Age.

Classical (Cypro-Classical) II (Cyprus,.label: Classical (Cypro-Classical) II
Classical (Cypro-Classical) II (Cyprus,.prose:
[Cyprus, 400 BC–326 BC] Classical (Cypro-Classical) II. Jamieson, 2007 (Ian Potter Museum exhibition). Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The island's kings continued to balance Persian tribute against Greek cultural and commercial ties, supplying ships and timber to whichever power was ascendant. Cypriot rulers backed Alexander at the siege of Tyre, and after his death the island became a prize in the wars of his successors. The Ptolemies eventually abolished the city-kingdoms, ending a political system that had lasted for centuries.

Hallstatt C (Germany, 750 BC–601 BC).label: Hallstatt C
Hallstatt C (Germany, 750 BC–601 BC).prose:
[Germany, Switzerland, Czech Republic, Liechtenstein, 750 BC–601 BC] Hallstatt C. Spatial coverage: Czech Republic, Germany, Liechtenstein, Switzerland. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Iron becomes the ordinary metal for weapons and tools, and a new warrior display emerges: long iron slashing swords, and burials under mounds containing four-wheeled wagons and horse gear. Salt extraction at Hallstatt reached its height, and the goods buried in its miners' graves show trade reaching to the Mediterranean and the Baltic.

Edad Media (Spain, AD 400–AD 1499).label: Edad Media
Edad Media (Spain, AD 400–AD 1499).prose:
[Spain, AD 400–AD 1499] Edad Media. Institute of Heritage Sciences, Spanish National Research Council (CSIC Incipit). Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Visigothic kingdoms gave way in 711 to the Muslim conquest, and for centuries the peninsula was divided between al-Andalus — with Córdoba among the largest and most learned cities in Europe — and the Christian kingdoms of the north. Warfare, frontier settlement and dynastic marriage steadily pushed the border south until only Granada remained, while Jews, Muslims and Christians lived in an uneasy and often violent proximity that also transmitted Greek and Arabic learning to the rest of Europe. Castile and Aragon were united by Ferdinand and Isabella, who took Granada in 1492.

honfoglalás kor (Hungary, AD 885–AD 999).label: honfoglalás kor
honfoglalás kor (Hungary, AD 885–AD 999).prose:
[Hungary, AD 885–AD 999] honfoglalás kor. Hungarian National Museum. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Magyar horsemen from the steppe took the Carpathian Basin at the end of the ninth century and used it as a base for raids deep into Germany, Italy and France until crushing defeats, above all at the Lechfeld, forced a change of course. Graves from these generations are unmistakable: sabres, decorated sabretache plates, silver harness mounts and horse burials laid with the dead. Within a century the raiding confederation had become a Christian kingdom under Stephen I.

késő neolitikum (Hungary, 5000 BC–4501 B.label: késő neolitikum
késő neolitikum (Hungary, 5000 BC–4501 B.prose:
[Hungary, 5000 BC–4501 BC] késő neolitikum. Hungarian National Museum. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The era of the great tells of the Hungarian plain, where villages such as Öcsöd and Berettyóújfalu-Herpály built up metres of occupation debris over generations. Tisza, Herpály and Lengyel communities produced elaborately incised and painted pottery, anthropomorphic vessels and figurines like the Sitting Woman of Szegvár-Tűzköves. Settlements grew larger and more sharply divided, with enclosure ditches and the first hints of social ranking and copper use.

Neolithicum (Netherlands, 5300 BC–2001 B.label: Neolithicum
Neolithicum (Netherlands, 5300 BC–2001 B.prose:
[Netherlands, 5300 BC–2001 BC] Neolithicum. Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Farming reached the Netherlands in two very different ways: Linear Pottery farmers settled the fertile loess of southern Limburg in longhouse villages, while in the wetlands to the north hunter-fisher communities of the Swifterbant tradition adopted cattle and cereals slowly, over centuries. Later came the Funnel Beaker builders of the hunebedden, the great boulder tombs of Drenthe, and finally Corded Ware and Bell Beaker groups burying individuals under round barrows. Waterlogged sites preserve wooden trackways, dugout canoes and even ploughed field surfaces.

Post Medieval (Denmark, AD 1536–AD 1659).label: Post Medieval
Post Medieval (Denmark, AD 1536–AD 1659).prose:
[Denmark, AD 1536–AD 1659] Post Medieval. ARENA1/ADS. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Beginning with the dissolution of the monasteries and the Reformation's stripping of parish churches, these centuries carried England through civil war, the growth of an Atlantic empire, enclosure of open fields, and industrialisation. Excavations of the period yield mass-produced goods - tin-glazed and transfer-printed pottery, glass bottles, clay tobacco pipes, machine-made nails - that let sites be dated to within a decade or two. Landscapes changed as thoroughly as objects: hedged fields, canals, railways, mines and terraced workers' housing all belong to this span.

Hoge Middeleeuwen (Netherlands, AD 900–A.label: Hoge Middeleeuwen
Hoge Middeleeuwen (Netherlands, AD 900–A.prose:
[Netherlands, AD 900–AD 1249] Hoge Middeleeuwen. Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Local counts and bishops consolidated territories such as Holland, Gelre, Brabant and the prince-bishopric of Utrecht out of the fragments of the Carolingian world. Farmers pushed into the peat bogs behind dikes and drainage ditches, creating both new farmland and a sinking landscape that demanded permanent water management; trade along the rivers and coast turned settlements like Dordrecht and Deventer into chartered towns. Stone castles, brick churches and the first urban privileges all date from these centuries.

Späte Römische (Austria, AD 180–AD 374).label: Späte Römische
Späte Römische (Austria, AD 180–AD 374).prose:
[Austria, AD 180–AD 374] Späte Römische. Austrian Academy of Sciences. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

In the Germanic provinces the Marcomannic wars marked the end of easy frontier security; by the mid-third century the Limes east of the Rhine was abandoned and the Agri Decumates lost to the Alamanni. Roman life retreated behind fortified towns and river forts, with new burgi and heavily walled settlements along the Rhine and Danube, while Germanic groups settled inside the frontier as soldiers and farmers.

Late Bronstijd (Netherlands, 1100 BC–801.label: Late Bronstijd
Late Bronstijd (Netherlands, 1100 BC–801.prose:
[Netherlands, 1100 BC–801 BC] Late Bronstijd. Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Communities in the low countries adopted the urnfield rite, cremating their dead and burying the ashes in pots under small round mounds in large communal cemeteries. Farmsteads with byre-houses shifted across the sandy soils, and bronze — swords, sickles, ornaments — arrived through networks reaching the Rhine and the Atlantic, often deposited in bogs and rivers as offerings. Iron appears at the close of the period.

vaskor (Hungary, 900 BC–101 BC).label: vaskor
vaskor (Hungary, 900 BC–101 BC).prose:
[Hungary, 900 BC–101 BC] vaskor. Hungarian National Museum. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Iron replaced bronze as the working metal of the Carpathian Basin, arriving with the Hallstatt world's hillforts, wagon burials and elaborate ironwork. Mounted groups from the steppe brought new weapons and animal-style ornament, and from the 4th century BC Celtic peoples settled the region, founding oppida and striking the first coins used here. The period closes as Roman power pushed towards the Danube.

âge du Fer (France, 800 BC–51 BC).label: âge du Fer
âge du Fer (France, 800 BC–51 BC).prose:
[France, 800 BC–51 BC] âge du Fer. INRAP. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Iron, cheap and widely available, replaced bronze for tools and weapons and changed who could arm and equip themselves. Princely burials, Mediterranean wine imports and later the fortified oppida trace the rise of Celtic chiefdoms with coinage, towns and craft specialisation. It ends with Caesar's conquest, which folded Gaul into the Roman world.

kora újkor (Hungary, AD 1526–AD 1710).label: kora újkor
kora újkor (Hungary, AD 1526–AD 1710).prose:
[Hungary, AD 1526–AD 1710] kora újkor. Hungarian National Museum. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The Ottoman victory at Mohács broke the medieval kingdom apart into three: Ottoman-occupied central Hungary, Habsburg Royal Hungary in the west and north, and a semi-independent Transylvania playing the two empires against each other. Border warfare, mosques and Turkish baths in the occupied towns, Reformation and Counter-Reformation, and depopulated stretches of the Great Plain all belong to these two centuries. Ottoman rule ended in the 1680s, and the last anti-Habsburg revolt closed with the Peace of Szatmár.

Gropkeramisk kultur (Sweden, 3200 BC–230.label: Gropkeramisk kultur
Gropkeramisk kultur (Sweden, 3200 BC–230.prose:
[Sweden, 3200 BC–2300 BC] Gropkeramisk kultur. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Coastal communities who turned away from farming and back to seal hunting, fishing and pig keeping, leaving behind round-based pots covered in rows of stamped pits. They lived alongside the farming societies of the interior yet kept a distinct way of life and, as ancient DNA has shown, a distinct ancestry descended from earlier hunter-gatherers. Their persistence complicates any simple story of agriculture sweeping northward.

középkor (Hungary, AD 1301–AD 1525).label: középkor
középkor (Hungary, AD 1301–AD 1525).prose:
[Hungary, AD 1301–AD 1525] középkor. Hungarian National Museum. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The late medieval kingdom at its most ambitious: Angevin kings tied Hungary to Naples and Poland, gold from the Slovak mines made its florin a European currency, and Sigismund of Luxembourg ruled as Holy Roman Emperor from Buda. Ottoman pressure defined the age, from Nicopolis to Hunyadi's defence of Belgrade, while Matthias Corvinus's court brought Renaissance art, humanism and one of Europe's great libraries north of the Alps. The era ends on the eve of Mohács, with a weakened crown facing an advancing empire.

késő római kor (Hungary, AD 270–AD 399).label: késő római kor
késő római kor (Hungary, AD 270–AD 399).prose:
[Hungary, AD 270–AD 399] késő római kor. Hungarian National Museum. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

After the crisis of the third century, Pannonia was rebuilt as a heavily militarised frontier zone: Diocletian split the provinces, and burgi, bridgehead forts and thickened Danube defences went up against Sarmatian and Germanic pressure. Cities shrank behind walls while fortified villas and inland strongholds such as Fenékpuszta took on new importance, and Christianity became publicly visible in cemeteries and painted burial chambers at Sopianae. Roman administration unravelled by the early fifth century, leaving the region to Huns and their successors.

Neolítico Antiquo (Spain, 4500 BC–2701 B.label: Neolítico Antiquo
Neolítico Antiquo (Spain, 4500 BC–2701 B.prose:
[Spain, 4500 BC–2701 BC] Neolítico Antiquo. Institute of Heritage Sciences, Spanish National Research Council (CSIC Incipit). Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The early farming centuries in Iberia, when cereal cultivation and herding took hold and communities began raising megalithic tombs of stone slabs under mounds. Pottery, polished axes and querns appear in caves and open settlements alike. Burial monuments become the principal marker of territory in a landscape still only lightly cleared.

kora római kor (Hungary, 100 BC–AD 269).label: kora római kor
kora római kor (Hungary, 100 BC–AD 269).prose:
[Hungary, 100 BC–AD 269] kora római kor. Hungarian National Museum. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Rome annexed the lands west of the Danube as the province of Pannonia and turned the river into a fortified frontier, with legionary bases and civilian towns at Aquincum, Carnuntum and Savaria. Roads, stone architecture, wine, coinage and villa estates arrived with the army, while beyond the river the Great Plain was held by Sarmatian Iazyges and the far north-east by Germanic groups. Trade and conflict across that frontier shaped the region's material culture on both banks.

bronzkor (Hungary, 2700 BC–901 BC).label: bronzkor
bronzkor (Hungary, 2700 BC–901 BC).prose:
[Hungary, 2700 BC–901 BC] bronzkor. Hungarian National Museum. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The Carpathian Basin became one of Europe's metalworking heartlands, with tell settlements piling up in the river valleys, fortified centres, and workshops turning out swords, axes and elaborate ornaments traded far to the north and west. Enormous hoards of bronze were buried in the ground, and gold work from this period is among the finest in prehistoric Europe. The later centuries saw cremation urnfields spread widely and settlement shift towards defended hilltops.

mlajši neolitik (Slovenia, 3500 BC–2801.label: mlajši neolitik
mlajši neolitik (Slovenia, 3500 BC–2801.prose:
[Slovenia, 3500 BC–2801 BC] mlajši neolitik. ZRC SAZU, Institute of Archaeology. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Late farming communities in the Ljubljana Marshes built pile dwellings on the wetlands, leaving waterlogged timbers, wooden tools and even a wheel with its axle preserved in the peat - among the oldest known anywhere. Copper metallurgy appears alongside stone tools, and pottery styles link the region to both the Alps and the Balkans. The sites are now UNESCO-listed for what their waterlogged deposits reveal about everyday prehistoric life.

Hallstatt B (Germany, 1000 BC–751 BC).label: Hallstatt B
Hallstatt B (Germany, 1000 BC–751 BC).prose:
[Germany, Switzerland, Czech Republic, Liechtenstein, 1000 BC–751 BC] Hallstatt B. Spatial coverage: Czech Republic, Germany, Liechtenstein, Switzerland. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The later Urnfield phase, still bronze-using, with cremation cemeteries, hoards of scrap and finished metalwork, and hilltop enclosures. Iron begins to appear in small quantities as an exotic material, and salt mining at Hallstatt itself gets under way, setting up the wealth of the centuries to come.

Midden Romeinse Tijd (Netherlands, AD 70.label: Midden Romeinse Tijd
Midden Romeinse Tijd (Netherlands, AD 70.prose:
[Netherlands, AD 70–AD 269] Midden Romeinse Tijd. Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

After the Batavian revolt was crushed, the Rhine frontier was rebuilt in stone and the region settled into two centuries of Roman order: forts and roads along the limes, towns such as Nijmegen and Forum Hadriani, and villa estates in the loess south. Local farmers supplied grain, hides and recruits to the army, and imported pottery, coins and glass reached even modest settlements. Third-century instability, raiding and a rising water table brought much of it to an end.

Romano (Spain, 50 BC–AD 399).label: Romano
Romano (Spain, 50 BC–AD 399).prose:
[Spain, 50 BC–AD 399] Romano. Institute of Heritage Sciences, Spanish National Research Council (CSIC Incipit). Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Southern and eastern Iberia under Roman rule, when native settlements were reorganised as towns with forums, baths and gridded streets, and the countryside filled with estates producing oil, wine and fish sauce for export. Latin, Roman law and Roman coinage displaced Iberian and Punic traditions, though local cults lingered.

Tranziţia de la Eneolitic la Epoca Bronz.node: Tranziţia de la Eneolitic la Epoca Bronzului (Romania, 3800 BC–3501 BC)
Tranziţia de la Eneolitic la Epoca Bronz.label: Tranziţia de la Eneolitic la Epoca Bronzului
Tranziţia de la Eneolitic la Epoca Bronz.prose:
[Romania, 3800 BC–3501 BC] Tranziţia de la Eneolitic la Epoca Bronzului. Romanian Academy. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The end of the great Copper Age tell cultures of the lower Danube and the Carpathians, whose painted pottery, copper axes and long-lived village mounds disappear within a few generations. In their place come more mobile, stock-raising communities using cord-impressed pottery and burying their dead under earthen mounds, with strong links eastward to the steppe - the groundwork for the Bronze Age societies of the region.

Tidigneolitikum (Sweden, 3900 BC–3300 BC.label: Tidigneolitikum
Tidigneolitikum (Sweden, 3900 BC–3300 BC.prose:
[Sweden, 3900 BC–3300 BC] Tidigneolitikum. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Farming reached southern Scandinavia: people began keeping cattle, sheep and pigs, sowing barley and wheat in clearings burned out of the forest, and making the flared funnel-necked pots that give the culture its name. They also began building for the dead, raising the first dolmens and passage graves out of massive stones — the oldest monuments in Sweden and often the most visible prehistoric feature in the landscape today. Flint mining, polished axes and long-distance exchange networks came with the new way of life.

Späte Bronzezeit (Austria, 1300 BC–801 B.label: Späte Bronzezeit
Späte Bronzezeit (Austria, 1300 BC–801 B.prose:
[Austria, 1300 BC–801 BC] Späte Bronzezeit. Austrian Academy of Sciences. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The Urnfield tradition spread across central Europe: the dead were cremated and buried in pottery urns in large flat cemeteries, replacing the barrows of earlier centuries. Bronze-working reached industrial scale, with sheet-metal vessels, shields and swords, and huge hoards were deposited in rivers and bogs. Fortified hilltop settlements suggest growing competition over metal routes.

Laat Neolithicum A (Netherlands, 2850 BC.label: Laat Neolithicum A
Laat Neolithicum A (Netherlands, 2850 BC.prose:
[Netherlands, 2850 BC–2451 BC] Laat Neolithicum A. Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The Corded Ware or Single Grave horizon, when individuals were buried under small round barrows with a stone battle-axe and a cord-decorated beaker. The shift to single burial and standardised grave goods marks a new emphasis on personal status, and is linked to population movement from the steppe. Barrows from this phase still stand on the sandy heaths of the eastern Netherlands.

Senmedeltid (Sweden, AD 1350–AD 1527).label: Senmedeltid
Senmedeltid (Sweden, AD 1350–AD 1527).prose:
[Sweden, AD 1350–AD 1527] Senmedeltid. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The centuries after the Black Death saw depopulated farms, a shift toward livestock, and Hanseatic merchants dominating the copper and iron trade through Stockholm and Visby. Politically it was the age of the Kalmar Union with Denmark and Norway, punctuated by revolts, the Stockholm Bloodbath, and finally Gustav Vasa's breakaway. Brick churches with vivid painted vaults, still standing across the countryside, are its most visible legacy.

енеолит (Bulgaria, 4900 BC–3801 BC).label: енеолит
енеолит (Bulgaria, 4900 BC–3801 BC).prose:
[Bulgaria, 4900 BC–3801 BC] енеолит. National Institute of Archaeology with Museum, Automated Information System "Archaeological Map of Bulgaria". Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Farming villages on tells grew large and densely built, and copper mining and smelting became a serious industry, with shafts at Ai Bunar among the earliest anywhere. The cemetery at Varna produced the oldest known concentration of worked gold in the world, its richest grave loaded with sceptres, ornaments and weapons, evidence that inherited rank and display had arrived. This flourishing world collapsed sharply toward the end of the period, with settlements burned or abandoned and the region left much emptier.

Tidigmodern tid (Sweden, AD 1500–AD 1789.label: Tidigmodern tid
Tidigmodern tid (Sweden, AD 1500–AD 1789.prose:
[Sweden, AD 1500–AD 1789] Tidigmodern tid. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Gustav Vasa broke with Denmark and with Rome, seizing church lands to fund a hereditary monarchy and pushing Sweden into the Lutheran camp. Over the next two centuries a thinly populated northern kingdom became a great power, holding Finland, the Baltic provinces and footholds in Germany, before Charles XII's defeat at Poltava and death in Norway ended the empire. The aristocratic 'Age of Liberty' and Gustav III's enlightened coup followed, and Linnaeus, Swedenborg and the Board of Mines made Sweden a centre of European science.

Mittelalter (Germany, AD 568–AD 1499).label: Mittelalter
Mittelalter (Germany, AD 568–AD 1499).prose:
[Germany, Switzerland, Czech Republic, Liechtenstein, AD 568–AD 1499] Mittelalter. Spatial coverage: Czech Republic, Germany, Liechtenstein, Switzerland. no source provided. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The long stretch between the end of Roman authority and the Renaissance, during which the Frankish kingdoms, the Ottonian and Salian emperors and finally the Holy Roman Empire shaped German lands. Monasteries preserved and copied texts, towns won charters and formed leagues such as the Hansa, cathedrals rose in Romanesque then Gothic style, and eastward settlement carried German speech to the Baltic. It closes with printing, universities and the tensions that would explode into the Reformation.

византийски период (Bulgaria, AD 1018–AD.label: византийски период
византийски период (Bulgaria, AD 1018–AD.prose:
[Bulgaria, AD 1018–AD 1186] византийски период. National Institute of Archaeology with Museum, Automated Information System "Archaeological Map of Bulgaria". Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The First Bulgarian Empire was annexed by Byzantium and governed from Constantinople as a group of provinces, with heavy taxation in coin replacing older obligations and Greek clergy installed in the church hierarchy. Nomadic Pecheneg and Cuman raids, Norman and Crusader armies, and repeated local revolts made it an unstable frontier zone. Discontent culminated in the rising of the brothers Asen and Peter, which restored an independent Bulgarian state.

Evul Mediu Dezvoltat (Romania, AD 1300–A.label: Evul Mediu Dezvoltat
Evul Mediu Dezvoltat (Romania, AD 1300–A.prose:
[Romania, AD 1300–AD 1600] Evul Mediu Dezvoltat. Romanian Academy. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The centuries when Wallachia and Moldavia matured as states with princely courts, chanceries, tax systems and metropolitan churches. Rulers such as Stephen the Great and Michael the Brave fought to hold off the Ottomans while Transylvania developed as an autonomous principality of nobles, Szeklers and Saxon towns. Stone monasteries, fortified towns and a flourishing Slavonic literary culture date from this period.

Mellanneolitisk tid A (Sweden, 3300 BC–2.label: Mellanneolitisk tid A
Mellanneolitisk tid A (Sweden, 3300 BC–2.prose:
[Sweden, 3300 BC–2800 BC] Mellanneolitisk tid A. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Funnel Beaker farmers reached their peak of monument-building, raising passage graves and gallery graves that were used and reopened over centuries and stacked with offerings of pots, flint and amber. On the Baltic islands and coasts the Pitted Ware groups turned back to seals, fish and pigs, making thousands of pits in their pottery and living in a way that looks more forager than farmer. The two ways of life overlapped in time and space, and archaeologists still argue about how they related.

Mittelalter (Austria, AD 568–AD 1499).label: Mittelalter
Mittelalter (Austria, AD 568–AD 1499).prose:
[Austria, AD 568–AD 1499] Mittelalter. Austrian Academy of Sciences. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The long stretch between the end of Roman authority and the Renaissance, during which the Frankish kingdoms, the Ottonian and Salian emperors and finally the Holy Roman Empire shaped German lands. Monasteries preserved and copied texts, towns won charters and formed leagues such as the Hansa, cathedrals rose in Romanesque then Gothic style, and eastward settlement carried German speech to the Baltic. It closes with printing, universities and the tensions that would explode into the Reformation.

Äldre vasatiden (Sweden, AD 1521–AD 1611.label: Äldre vasatiden
Äldre vasatiden (Sweden, AD 1521–AD 1611.prose:
[Sweden, AD 1521–AD 1611] Äldre vasatiden. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Gustav Vasa's rebellion broke Sweden away from the Kalmar Union and the Danish crown, and his reign turned a loose realm into a centrally administered hereditary monarchy. The Reformation transferred church lands and wealth to the state, Bibles and liturgy appeared in Swedish, and a permanent tax and record-keeping apparatus took shape. His quarrelling sons — Erik XIV, Johan III and Karl IX — fought over the crown and religion while Sweden began expanding into the eastern Baltic, the prelude to its rise as a great power.

Kalmarunionen (Sweden, AD 1397–AD 1523).label: Kalmarunionen
Kalmarunionen (Sweden, AD 1397–AD 1523).prose:
[Sweden, AD 1397–AD 1523] Kalmarunionen. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Three Nordic kingdoms — Denmark, Norway and Sweden — were bound under a single monarch, an arrangement engineered by Margaret I and sealed at Kalmar. In practice Danish interests dominated, and Swedish nobles and miners rebelled repeatedly against royal taxes and foreign bailiffs. The union collapsed after the Stockholm Bloodbath of 1520, when Christian II executed dozens of Swedish notables and provoked the revolt that put Gustav Vasa on the throne.

Yngre järnålder (Sweden, AD 400–AD 1050).label: Yngre järnålder
Yngre järnålder (Sweden, AD 400–AD 1050).prose:
[Sweden, AD 400–AD 1050] Yngre järnålder. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Spanning the Migration, Vendel and Viking periods, these centuries saw hoarded gold and gold-foil figures, boat burials at Vendel and Valsgärde, and the rise of central places such as Old Uppsala, Helgö and later Birka. Traders and raiders pushed east along the Russian rivers and west across the Atlantic, and by its close runestones record the arrival of Christianity and the making of a Swedish kingdom.

Temps moderne (France, AD 1492–AD 1814).label: Temps moderne
Temps moderne (France, AD 1492–AD 1814).prose:
[France, AD 1492–AD 1814] Temps moderne. INRAP. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

France's early modern age, running from the Italian wars and Renaissance court culture through the wars of religion, the absolutism of Louis XIV at Versailles, and the Enlightenment, to the Revolution and the fall of Napoleon. In these centuries the French state built its bureaucracy, standing army and overseas empire, and the country moved from a monarchy of divine right to a nation that had executed its king.

Edad del Bronce Media (Spain, 1700 BC–12.node: Edad del Bronce Media (Spain, 1700 BC–1201 BC)
Edad del Bronce Media (Spain, 1700 BC–12.label: Edad del Bronce Media
Edad del Bronce Media (Spain, 1700 BC–12.prose:
[Spain, 1700 BC–1201 BC] Edad del Bronce Media. Institute of Heritage Sciences, Spanish National Research Council (CSIC Incipit). Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

In southeastern Spain the El Argar world reached its height and then collapsed around 1550 BC, ending the fortified towns and their sharply hierarchical jar burials. Across the interior and the Atlantic side, herding communities used mould-cast bronze weapons and buried their dead in cists, and new alloys and forms circulated along routes that reached the Mediterranean and northwestern Europe. The period sets up the far-reaching metal trade of the Late Bronze Age.

neolitikum (Hungary, 6000 BC–4501 BC).label: neolitikum
neolitikum (Hungary, 6000 BC–4501 BC).prose:
[Hungary, 6000 BC–4501 BC] neolitikum. Hungarian National Museum. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The first farmers in the Carpathian Basin - Koros and Starcevo in the south, then the Alfold and Transdanubian Linear Pottery cultures - introduced wheat, cattle, pottery and permanent villages. In the Tisza region settlement mounds, or tells, grew up over centuries of rebuilding, and sites like Szegvar-Tuzkoves produced striking clay figurines such as the Sickle God. These communities were the northern frontier of the farming way of life spreading out of the Balkans.

Възраждане (Bulgaria, AD 1762–AD 1877).label: Възраждане
Възраждане (Bulgaria, AD 1762–AD 1877).prose:
[Bulgaria, AD 1762–AD 1877] Възраждане. National Institute of Archaeology with Museum, Automated Information System "Archaeological Map of Bulgaria". Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

A century of cultural and political awakening under Ottoman rule, usually dated from Paisii of Hilendar's history of the Bulgarians in 1762. Merchants and teachers founded secular schools and reading rooms, printed books in the vernacular, and campaigned successfully for a Bulgarian church independent of the Greek patriarchate in 1870. The movement turned into armed struggle with the April Uprising of 1876, whose brutal suppression brought European intervention and, after the Russo-Turkish war, an autonomous Bulgarian state.

Vroege Middeleeuwen D (Netherlands, AD 9.label: Vroege Middeleeuwen D
Vroege Middeleeuwen D (Netherlands, AD 9.prose:
[Netherlands, AD 900–AD 1049] Vroege Middeleeuwen D. Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Viking pressure and the fragmentation of the Carolingian empire left power in the hands of regional counts and bishops, the ancestors of Holland, Gelre and Utrecht. Trade shifted from Dorestad to newer places like Tiel and Deventer, and the first systematic diking and drainage of the peat lands began, opening a landscape that had to be permanently defended against water.

Neolit (Albania, 7000 BC–3061 BC).label: Neolit
Neolit (Albania, 7000 BC–3061 BC).prose:
[Albania, 7000 BC–3061 BC] Neolit. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Farming villages settled Albania's river valleys and the lake basins around Korçë, with Maliq and similar sites building up as mounds of debris from generations of mudbrick houses. Their painted and dark burnished pottery links them to the wider Balkan and Aegean Neolithic world, and copper begins to appear towards the end of the period. Livestock, grain storage and long-distance exchange in obsidian and fine wares mark the shift from scattered settlement to established communities.

starejša železna doba (Slovenia, 750 BC–.label: starejša železna doba
starejša železna doba (Slovenia, 750 BC–.prose:
[Slovenia, 750 BC–301 BC] starejša železna doba. ZRC SAZU, Institute of Archaeology. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

This is the age of the Hallstatt princes in what is now Slovenia: fortified hilltop centres such as Vače, Stična and Novo mesto, surrounded by cemeteries of great burial mounds. Warriors were buried with bronze helmets, weapons and horse gear, and local workshops produced the famous decorated bronze buckets, or situlae, whose embossed friezes show feasting, boxing and processions. The wealth came from iron ore, trade with the Adriatic Greek and Etruscan world, and control of routes through the Alps.

Hallstatt D (Germany, 600 BC–481 BC).label: Hallstatt D
Hallstatt D (Germany, 600 BC–481 BC).prose:
[Germany, Switzerland, Czech Republic, Liechtenstein, 600 BC–481 BC] Hallstatt D. Spatial coverage: Czech Republic, Germany, Liechtenstein, Switzerland. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The climax and collapse of Hallstatt society.
