Fortified "princely seats" like the Heuneburg, with its Mediterranean-style mudbrick wall, controlled trade in Greek wine, bronze vessels and coral, while nearby mounds held spectacular burials such as the woman of Vix with her huge Greek bronze krater. Long swords gave way to short daggers, and by the end of the phase the centres were abandoned and the La Tène style was taking shape.

Medieval (Denmark, AD 1050–AD 1535).label: Medieval
Medieval (Denmark, AD 1050–AD 1535).prose: [Denmark, AD 1050–AD 1535] Medieval. ARENA1/ADS. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Yngre stenåldern (Sweden, 3900 BC–1800 B.label: Yngre stenåldern
Yngre stenåldern (Sweden, 3900 BC–1800 B.prose:
[Sweden, 3900 BC–1800 BC] Yngre stenåldern. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Crops, domestic animals and permanent houses reshaped the landscape, and the dead were placed in stone-built chambered tombs that served whole communities for generations. Seal hunters using pitted-decorated pottery persisted on the Baltic islands alongside the farmers, a coexistence still argued over by archaeologists. The period closes with gallery graves, long-distance trade and flint daggers so finely worked they imitate metal.

преходен период (Bulgaria, 3800 BC–3401.label: преходен период
преходен период (Bulgaria, 3800 BC–3401.prose:
[Bulgaria, 3800 BC–3401 BC] преходен период. National Institute of Archaeology with Museum, Automated Information System "Archaeological Map of Bulgaria". Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The rich tell-dwelling copper cultures of the lower Danube collapsed, and for several centuries the great mounds stood empty. Settlement became smaller, shorter-lived and more mobile, herding gained ground, and burials under kurgans in the steppe manner appear along the Danube. What looks like an archaeological gap is really a reorganisation of society out of which the Early Bronze Age emerged.

Byzantine (Cyprus, AD 250–AD 1190).label: Byzantine
Byzantine (Cyprus, AD 250–AD 1190).prose:
[Cyprus, AD 250–AD 1190] Byzantine. no source provided. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Cyprus as a prosperous Christian province of the eastern Roman empire, covered in basilicas and mosaic floors and shipping copper, oil and wine across the Mediterranean. From the mid-seventh century Arab raids made the island a contested frontier, and for three centuries it was shared uneasily between Constantinople and the caliphate before Nikephoros Phokas took it back outright. The Byzantine centuries ended abruptly when Richard the Lionheart seized the island on his way to the Third Crusade and sold it on.

Romeinse Tijd (Netherlands, 12 BC–AD 449.label: Romeinse Tijd
Romeinse Tijd (Netherlands, 12 BC–AD 449.prose:
[Netherlands, 12 BC–AD 449] Romeinse Tijd. Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The Rhine became Rome's northern frontier, lined with forts, a military road and supply harbours, with the lands south of it inside the empire and the marshy north outside it. The Batavians supplied crack auxiliary units and then rose in a famous revolt in AD 69; towns grew at Nijmegen and Voorburg, and Roman goods spread far beyond the border. Rising water levels and Frankish pressure ended imperial control in the fourth and fifth centuries.

Renaissance (France, AD 1492–AD 1699).label: Renaissance
Renaissance (France, AD 1492–AD 1699).prose:
[France, AD 1492–AD 1699] Renaissance. INRAP. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

French armies invading Italy came home dazzled, and kings from Charles VIII to Francis I imported Italian architects, painters and gardeners wholesale — the result is the Loire châteaux, Fontainebleau, and Leonardo da Vinci dying near Amboise. Print shops in Lyon and Paris spread humanist scholarship and the French vernacular, which Francis I made the language of law in 1539. The same presses spread Calvin, and the century closed in the Wars of Religion, resolved only by Henry IV and the Edict of Nantes.

Stridsyxekulturen (Sweden, 2800 BC–2400.label: Stridsyxekulturen
Stridsyxekulturen (Sweden, 2800 BC–2400.prose:
[Sweden, 2800 BC–2400 BC] Stridsyxekulturen. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The Swedish branch of the Corded Ware world, marked by single graves containing a polished stone battle-axe, a beaker and a flint blade, the body laid on its side with men and women oriented differently. It arrived with a substantial movement of people carrying steppe ancestry, and brought a stronger emphasis on stock-keeping and individual burial in place of the collective megalithic tombs of the earlier farmers. Genetically and linguistically this horizon is a foundation of later Scandinavian populations.

âge du Bronze (France, 2200 BC–801 BC).label: âge du Bronze
âge du Bronze (France, 2200 BC–801 BC).prose:
[France, 2200 BC–801 BC] âge du Bronze. INRAP. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Copper and tin alloyed into bronze pulled the region into long-distance exchange networks running from Cornwall and Brittany to central Europe and the Mediterranean. Warrior elites were buried under tumuli with daggers and axes, and later centuries produced enormous hoards of scrap and finished metalwork, deliberately buried or thrown into rivers. By the closing phase, cremation in urnfields, fortified hilltop sites and mass-produced socketed axes point to the more crowded, competitive world that iron would inherit.

късна бронзова епоха (Bulgaria, 1600 BC–.label: късна бронзова епоха
късна бронзова епоха (Bulgaria, 1600 BC–.prose:
[Bulgaria, 1600 BC–1101 BC] късна бронзова епоха. National Institute of Archaeology with Museum, Automated Information System "Archaeological Map of Bulgaria". Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Fortified hilltop sites, rock-cut sanctuaries and hoards of bronze tools and weapons mark communities in contact with the Mycenaean world — Aegean swords, rapiers and pottery turn up in Thracian contexts, and Thracian metalwork travelled south. Cremation and mound burial spread, and the tribal names later recorded by Greek writers begin to take shape. The disruptions that ended the Mycenaean palaces around 1200 BC reached here too, opening the way to iron.

современи (Republic of Macedonia, AD 191.label: современи
современи (Republic of Macedonia, AD 191.prose:
[Macedonia, AD 1912–AD 2000] современи. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The Balkan Wars and the First World War pulled the region out of the Ottoman Empire and into a succession of new states, ending with incorporation into Yugoslavia. Decades as a Yugoslav republic brought industrialisation, mass literacy and the codification of a standard Macedonian language, punctuated by the 1963 Skopje earthquake that destroyed much of the capital. Independence in 1991 came peacefully, but left long disputes over name and identity with neighbours.

Early Bronze Age (Cyprus, 2500 BC–1801 B.label: Early Bronze Age
Early Bronze Age (Cyprus, 2500 BC–1801 B.prose:
[Cyprus, 2500 BC–1801 BC] Early Bronze Age. Jamieson, 2007 (Ian Potter Museum exhibition). Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

After the rich copper-working tell cultures of the Balkan Chalcolithic broke down, settlement in the Bulgarian lands was rebuilt on a different footing: fortified mounds such as Ezero and Yunatsite, alloyed copper and then true bronze, ox-drawn carts and the plough. Burial mounds of the kind raised by steppe pastoralists to the north spread across the Danube plain and the Thracian valleys, a sign of new populations and new ideas about rank. The dead were now marked by the tomb above ground rather than by the gold-filled graves of the earlier era.

Vroege Middeleeuwen (Netherlands, AD 450.label: Vroege Middeleeuwen
Vroege Middeleeuwen (Netherlands, AD 450.prose:
[Netherlands, AD 450–AD 1049] Vroege Middeleeuwen. Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

After Roman withdrawal much of the Netherlands was thinly settled, then repopulated as Frisian, Frankish and Saxon groups took shape. Terp mounds in the north and trading places like Dorestad linked the region to the North Sea economy, handling Rhenish pottery, wine and slaves. Frankish rule and Christian mission arrived with Willibrord and Boniface, and by the end of the period Viking raids and the rise of local lords were reshaping power along the rivers.

бронзеното време (Republic of Macedonia,.node: бронзеното време (Republic of Macedonia, 2200 BC–1001 BC)
бронзеното време (Republic of Macedonia,.label: бронзеното време
бронзеното време (Republic of Macedonia,.prose:
[Macedonia, 2200 BC–1001 BC] бронзеното време. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Communities moved onto defensible hills and terraces, building fortified settlements and burying their dead beneath stone-covered mounds. Bronze tools, weapons and ornaments circulated along routes linking the Aegean with the central Balkans, and pottery styles show contact with the Mycenaean world to the south. It is the era in which the tribal geography later described by Greek writers began to take shape.

Spätmittelalter (Austria, AD 1250–AD 149.label: Spätmittelalter
Spätmittelalter (Austria, AD 1250–AD 149.prose:
[Austria, AD 1250–AD 1499] Spätmittelalter. Austrian Academy of Sciences. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The Habsburgs supplanted the Babenbergs and Ottokar of Bohemia to make the Austrian duchies their family base, gradually accumulating Tyrol, Carinthia and Carniola. Towns grew on the Danube trade, mining brought silver and salt wealth, and universities and Gothic building flourished. By the reign of Maximilian I, dynastic marriage had turned a regional principality into the core of a European empire.

Archaic (Cypro-Archaic) I (Cyprus, 750 B.label: Archaic (Cypro-Archaic) I
Archaic (Cypro-Archaic) I (Cyprus, 750 B.prose:
[Cyprus, 750 BC–601 BC] Archaic (Cypro-Archaic) I. Jamieson, 2007 (Ian Potter Museum exhibition). Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The island's independent city-kingdoms — Salamis, Kition, Paphos and their rivals — flourished under a light Assyrian overlordship, paying tribute while running their own affairs. Rich chamber tombs at Salamis contain chariots, horse burials and bronze cauldrons that read like scenes from Homer, and sanctuaries filled with thousands of terracotta votive figures, as at Ayia Irini. Cypriot craftsmen worked Phoenician, Egyptian and Greek motifs into a distinctive local style, and the syllabic Cypriot script remained in use alongside Phoenician.

Neolithic (Poland, 4500 BC–1801 BC).label: Neolithic
Neolithic (Poland, 4500 BC–1801 BC).prose:
[Poland, 4500 BC–1801 BC] Neolithic. ARENA1/ADS. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

In the southern Levant this is where farming villages first take hold: wheat, barley, sheep and goats replace foraging, and settlements like Jericho grow to unprecedented size behind stone walls and a tower. Households plastered their floors, kept the skulls of their dead under them and modelled faces onto them in plaster, and at 'Ain Ghazal produced large human statues of lime plaster over reed frames. Pottery arrives only in the later centuries, long after the farming economy itself.

Roman I (Cyprus, 50 BC–AD 149).label: Roman I
Roman I (Cyprus, 50 BC–AD 149).prose:
[Cyprus, 50 BC–AD 149] Roman I. Jamieson, 2007 (Ian Potter Museum exhibition). Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Cyprus, annexed from the Ptolemies, settled into life as a quiet senatorial province exporting copper, timber, grain and wine. Cities such as Paphos, Salamis and Kourion were rebuilt in Roman style with theatres, gymnasia and aqueducts, often after devastating earthquakes. This is also the island of the earliest Christian mission recorded in Acts, when Paul and Barnabas preached to the Roman governor.

Frühes Neolithikum (Austria, 5600 BC–480.label: Frühes Neolithikum
Frühes Neolithikum (Austria, 5600 BC–480.prose:
[Austria, 5600 BC–4801 BC] Frühes Neolithikum. Austrian Academy of Sciences. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The first farmers moved up the Danube and along the loess soils, bringing wheat, barley, cattle, pottery and a completely new way of living. They built timber longhouses tens of metres long, clustered in small hamlets, and left the distinctive incised Linear Pottery that gives the culture its name. Forests were cleared, land became something to hold and inherit, and mass graves at sites like Talheim show that the arrival of farming brought violence as well as surplus.

Vendeltid (Sweden, AD 550–AD 800).label: Vendeltid
Vendeltid (Sweden, AD 550–AD 800).prose:
[Sweden, AD 550–AD 800] Vendeltid. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The generations before the Viking Age, named after the boat graves at Vendel where chieftains were buried with horses, weapons and ornate helmets of gilded bronze and garnet inlay. Aristocratic halls, great mounds at Old Uppsala and animal-style metalwork show a society of warrior retinues and long-distance contacts reaching Britain and the Continent. The seamanship, wealth and craft of these elites are what the Viking expeditions were built on.

A Doua Epocă a Fierului (Romania, 450 BC.node: A Doua Epocă a Fierului (Romania, 450 BC–AD 106)
A Doua Epocă a Fierului (Romania, 450 BC.label: A Doua Epocă a Fierului
A Doua Epocă a Fierului (Romania, 450 BC.prose:
[Romania, 450 BC–AD 106] A Doua Epocă a Fierului. Romanian Academy. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Celtic newcomers, wheel-thrown pottery and iron tools reshaped the communities of the Carpathian basin, blending with the older Thracian population. The Dacians built fortified centres in the Orăștie Mountains, struck their own coins and traded wine and luxury goods with the Greek and Roman worlds. Their kingdom under Burebista and Decebalus ended when Roman armies stormed Sarmizegetusa.

Medieval (Poland, AD 600–AD 1249).label: Medieval
Medieval (Poland, AD 600–AD 1249).prose: [Poland, AD 600–AD 1249] Medieval. ARENA1/ADS. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Neuzeit (Austria, AD 1500–AD 1849).label: Neuzeit
Neuzeit (Austria, AD 1500–AD 1849).prose:
[Austria, AD 1500–AD 1849] Neuzeit. Austrian Academy of Sciences. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The centuries in which the German lands passed through the Reformation, the devastation of the Thirty Years' War, the rise of Prussia, the Napoleonic upheaval and the first stirrings of industry and national unification. Printing, gunpowder fortification, overseas trade goods and porcelain reshaped daily life and material culture. Archaeologically it is the age of surviving townscapes, factory sites and mass-produced ceramics and glass.

Antiquité romaine (France, 50 BC–AD 499).label: Antiquité romaine
Antiquité romaine (France, 50 BC–AD 499).prose:
[France, 50 BC–AD 499] Antiquité romaine. INRAP. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

After Caesar's conquest, Gaul was reorganised into provinces, laid out with roads, and filled with towns modelled on Rome; local elites adopted Latin, togas and civic office while keeping many indigenous gods. Aqueducts, arenas, theatres and villa estates transformed the landscape, and cities such as Lugdunum became imperial centres in their own right. The Gallo-Roman synthesis that resulted underlies later French language, law and settlement patterns.

Late Middeleeuwen A (Netherlands, AD 105.label: Late Middeleeuwen A
Late Middeleeuwen A (Netherlands, AD 105.prose:
[Netherlands, AD 1050–AD 1249] Late Middeleeuwen A. Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Peasants and monastic houses cut drainage ditches into the raised bogs behind the coast, creating the long strip fields and dike systems that made the western Netherlands habitable — and, as the drained peat shrank, permanently vulnerable to flooding. Counts of Holland, bishops of Utrecht and Frisian communities competed for control, building brick and stone castles and granting the first town privileges. Trade along the Rhine and Meuse and across the North Sea began the region's commercial rise.

Högmedeltid (Sweden, AD 1200–AD 1350).label: Högmedeltid
Högmedeltid (Sweden, AD 1200–AD 1350).prose:
[Sweden, AD 1200–AD 1350] Högmedeltid. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Sweden became a settled kingdom in these years: stone castles and cathedrals went up, provincial laws were written down, and Stockholm and other towns grew on Hanseatic trade in iron, copper and butter. The Church, royal administration and a tax-exempt noble cavalry class took recognisable shape, and Magnus Eriksson's national law code drew the provinces together. Visitors will see brick and granite buildings, church wall paintings and imported German goods that mark the shift from a rural chiefly society to a European monarchy.

неолит (Bulgaria, 6300 BC–4901 BC).label: неолит
неолит (Bulgaria, 6300 BC–4901 BC).prose:
[Bulgaria, 6300 BC–4901 BC] неолит. National Institute of Archaeology with Museum, Automated Information System "Archaeological Map of Bulgaria". Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Farming arrived from Anatolia and the Aegean, and by 6000 BC villages of mudbrick houses with ovens, querns and storage pots covered the Thracian plain and the Struma valley. Repeated rebuilding on the same spot created the tells — Karanovo, Slatina, Stara Zagora — whose burnt houses preserve furniture, looms and pottery in place. White-on-red painted wares, clay figurines and the first cattle-keeping economies define a way of life that lasted more than a millennium.

Evul Mediu (Romania, AD 800–AD 1820).label: Evul Mediu
Evul Mediu (Romania, AD 800–AD 1820).prose:
[Romania, AD 800–AD 1820] Evul Mediu. Romanian Academy. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The long medieval span in Romanian usage, running from the early Slav-Romanian village communities through the founding of Wallachia and Moldavia to the eve of modern reform. It takes in Hungarian and Saxon settlement in Transylvania, the Mongol invasion, centuries of Ottoman suzerainty and Phanariot rule. Material culture ranges from timber hamlets and hoards to painted monasteries, princely courts and fortified Saxon churches.

Edad Moderno (Spain, AD 1500–AD 1899).label: Edad Moderno
Edad Moderno (Spain, AD 1500–AD 1899).prose:
[Spain, AD 1500–AD 1899] Edad Moderno. Institute of Heritage Sciences, Spanish National Research Council (CSIC Incipit). Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Spain unified under the Catholic Monarchs, expelled its Jewish and later Morisco populations, and used American silver to fund a Habsburg empire that dominated Europe for a century. Overextension, war and debt brought decline in the 1600s even as Cervantes, Velázquez and the Golden Age theatre flourished; a Bourbon dynasty then rebuilt the state along French centralist lines after 1700. The period ends with Napoleonic invasion and the loss of the mainland American colonies.

késő rézkor (Hungary, 3600 BC–2701 BC).label: késő rézkor
késő rézkor (Hungary, 3600 BC–2701 BC).prose:
[Hungary, 3600 BC–2701 BC] késő rézkor. Hungarian National Museum. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Dominated by the Baden culture, whose settlements spread widely and thinly across the Carpathian Basin after the tell villages were abandoned. This is the period of the earliest wagon models in Europe, of cattle burials and of paired draught animals - evidence that the wheel and the ox-team had transformed transport and farming. Cremation and inhumation coexisted, and copper metallurgy became routine.

Segunda Edad del Hierro (Spain, 400 BC–5.node: Segunda Edad del Hierro (Spain, 400 BC–51 BC)
Segunda Edad del Hierro (Spain, 400 BC–5.label: Segunda Edad del Hierro
Segunda Edad del Hierro (Spain, 400 BC–5.prose:
[Spain, 400 BC–51 BC] Segunda Edad del Hierro. Institute of Heritage Sciences, Spanish National Research Council (CSIC Incipit). Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Iberian communities along the Mediterranean coast built walled hilltop towns, wrote in their own scripts, minted coins and carved stone sculpture such as the Dama de Elche, while Celtiberian peoples of the interior fielded the warriors Rome found so hard to beat. Greek and Punic contact fed the trade in wine, oil and fine pottery. The period ends with the long Roman conquest, from the Second Punic War through the sieges of Numantia and the final campaigns in the north.

Frühe Römische (Germany, AD 1–AD 179).label: Frühe Römische
Frühe Römische (Germany, AD 1–AD 179).prose:
[Germany, Switzerland, Czech Republic, Liechtenstein, AD 1–AD 179] Frühe Römische. Spatial coverage: Czech Republic, Germany, Liechtenstein, Switzerland. no source provided. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The Alpine kingdom of Noricum passed peacefully into Roman hands and was joined to the Danube frontier province of Pannonia, bringing legions, roads and towns. Cities like Virunum and Carnuntum grew up around administration and the army, Norican iron was exported across the empire, and local elites adopted Latin, togas and stone inscriptions. The period closes with the Marcomannic Wars, when Germanic armies broke across the Danube and ended the long frontier peace.

pozna bakrena doba (Slovenia, 2200 BC–18.label: pozna bakrena doba
pozna bakrena doba (Slovenia, 2200 BC–18.prose:
[Slovenia, 2200 BC–1801 BC] pozna bakrena doba. ZRC SAZU, Institute of Archaeology. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Copper metallurgy became routine and the first tin-bronze objects appeared, while communities in the Ljubljana Marshes and along the river valleys traded along routes linking the Adriatic with the Danube. Bell Beaker pottery and Vučedol-derived styles show how far ideas travelled. These centuries laid the groundwork for the fully developed Bronze Age societies that followed.

rimska doba (Slovenia, 30 BC–AD 599).label: rimska doba
rimska doba (Slovenia, 30 BC–AD 599).prose:
[Slovenia, 30 BC–AD 599] rimska doba. ZRC SAZU, Institute of Archaeology. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Roman armies absorbed the eastern Alpine passes and the corridor between Italy and the Danube, planting the towns of Emona, Celeia and Poetovio along paved trunk roads. Latin, coinage, villas and mithraic shrines spread through valleys that had been Celtic and Illyrian, and the region became a strategic hinge crossed repeatedly by armies and, later, by Goths, Huns and Lombards.

starejši neolitik (Slovenia, 5000 BC–400.label: starejši neolitik
starejši neolitik (Slovenia, 5000 BC–400.prose:
[Slovenia, 5000 BC–4001 BC] starejši neolitik. ZRC SAZU, Institute of Archaeology. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The first farmers arrived, bringing wheat, barley, sheep, goats and pottery to a landscape previously occupied by hunter-gatherers. Two traditions met here: Impresso-style pottery spreading up from the Adriatic coast and Linear Pottery farming villages pushing in from the Pannonian plain. Caves and open-air sites alike show the slow shift from foraging to a settled agricultural life.

Archaic (Cypro-Archaic) II (Cyprus, 600.label: Archaic (Cypro-Archaic) II
Archaic (Cypro-Archaic) II (Cyprus, 600.prose:
[Cyprus, 600 BC–476 BC] Archaic (Cypro-Archaic) II. Jamieson, 2007 (Ian Potter Museum exhibition). Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Egyptian and then Persian overlords replaced the Assyrians, but the city-kingdoms kept minting their own coins and pursuing their own quarrels. Sculpture in soft local limestone flourished, mixing Egyptian stance with Greek drapery and Cypriot beards, and the free-field pottery style produced its famous birds and fish. The period ends in violence: most of the kingdoms joined the Ionian Revolt against Persia and were crushed at the battle of Salamis on Cyprus in 498 BC.

Perandorake e hershme (Albania, AD 1–AD.label: Perandorake e hershme
Perandorake e hershme (Albania, AD 1–AD.prose:
[Albania, AD 1–AD 99] Perandorake e hershme. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Illyria and Epirus settled into provincial life under the early emperors, with the Via Egnatia carrying traffic from the Adriatic ports of Dyrrachium and Apollonia towards Macedonia and Constantinople's future site. Roman colonies, forums, theatres and aqueducts reshaped older Greek and Illyrian towns such as Buthrotum, and Latin spread inland alongside Greek on the coast. Local elites bought into Roman citizenship and civic building.

Romak (Albania, 168 BC–AD 564).label: Romak
Romak (Albania, 168 BC–AD 564).prose:
[Albania, 168 BC–AD 564] Romak. Derived from FASTI, but no match in the 2004 dataset. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Rome's defeat of the Illyrian and Macedonian kingdoms brought this coast under its control, and it became a hinge of the empire: Dyrrachium and Apollonia were the Adriatic ports where the Via Egnatia began, carrying troops and traders east to Byzantium. Cities, roads and villas flourished, Christianity took root early, and the region later fell within the Byzantine sphere before the great earthquakes and Slavic migrations of the sixth century.

rézkor (Hungary, 4500 BC–2701 BC).label: rézkor
rézkor (Hungary, 4500 BC–2701 BC).prose:
[Hungary, 4500 BC–2701 BC] rézkor. Hungarian National Museum. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Copper smelting and casting became routine, producing heavy axe-adzes and gold ornaments that mark out a few burials from the rest. Communities of the Tiszapolgár and Bodrogkeresztúr traditions buried their dead in large orderly cemeteries, and later the Baden culture brought cattle-herding, wagons and the first evidence of wheeled transport in the Carpathian Basin.

Para qytetare ilire (Albania, 600 BC–337.label: Para qytetare ilire
Para qytetare ilire (Albania, 600 BC–337.prose:
[Albania, 600 BC–337 BC] Para qytetare ilire. Derived from FASTI, but no match in the 2004 dataset. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Illyrian communities in the hills and valleys inland lived in fortified settlements and tribal groupings, burying their leaders under tumuli with weapons and imported goods, before the rise of true towns with walls, streets and coinage in the following Hellenistic centuries. Along the coast, the Greek colonies of Apollonia and Epidamnos drew local produce into Mediterranean trade and pushed pottery, wine and silver inland. Archaeologically the period is known mainly from hillfort sites and cemeteries, which show growing wealth differences among the tribes that later kings would unite.

Midden Neolithicum A (Netherlands, 4200.label: Midden Neolithicum A
Midden Neolithicum A (Netherlands, 4200.prose:
[Netherlands, 4200 BC–3401 BC] Midden Neolithicum A. Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Communities in the delta and river wetlands mixed hunting, fishing and gathering with small-scale herding and cereal growing, leaving distinctive Swifterbant and Hazendonk pottery. Waterlogged sites preserve wooden fish traps, canoes and food remains in extraordinary detail. It shows farming spreading not as a sudden replacement but as a slow addition to an already rich way of life.

Epipaleolítico (Spain, 7000 BC–4501 BC).label: Epipaleolítico
Epipaleolítico (Spain, 7000 BC–4501 BC).prose:
[Spain, 7000 BC–4501 BC] Epipaleolítico. Institute of Heritage Sciences, Spanish National Research Council (CSIC Incipit). Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

After the ice sheets retreated, hunter-gatherers adapted to warmer forests and rising seas, hunting deer and rabbit, gathering shellfish in huge quantities and making tiny geometric flint blades to arm composite tools. Their shell middens and cemeteries show settled, territorial communities living in the same coasts and river valleys that farmers would occupy a few centuries later.

Folkvandringstid (Sweden, AD 400–AD 550).label: Folkvandringstid
Folkvandringstid (Sweden, AD 400–AD 550).prose:
[Sweden, AD 400–AD 550] Folkvandringstid. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The Migration Period in Scandinavia, when contact with a collapsing Roman world brought floods of gold into the North: bracteates, neck-rings and hoards buried in bogs and fields. Chieftains built hillforts and ring-forts such as Eketorp on Öland, and abandoned farms across the region hint at the crisis following the dust-veil and cold years of the 530s. Out of this upheaval came the wealthy warrior aristocracy of the Vendel age.

Midden Bronstijd (Netherlands, 1800 BC–1.label: Midden Bronstijd
Midden Bronstijd (Netherlands, 1800 BC–1.prose:
[Netherlands, 1800 BC–1101 BC] Midden Bronstijd. Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Farming communities settled into a stable pattern of long timber houses shared with their cattle, standing amid arable fields and pasture rather than in nucleated villages. Barrow burial continued from earlier centuries but cremation gradually took over, and metalwork - axes, spearheads, ornaments - arrived through exchange networks reaching Britain and central Europe. Much of what is known comes from house plans and post holes recovered on the sandy soils of the south and east.

Eneolitic (Romania, 5000 BC–3801 BC).label: Eneolitic
Eneolitic (Romania, 5000 BC–3801 BC).prose:
[Romania, 5000 BC–3801 BC] Eneolitic. Romanian Academy. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The Copper Age in the lower Danube and Carpathian region saw farming villages grow into long-lived tell settlements, with copper axes and gold ornaments produced on a scale unmatched elsewhere at the time. Cultures such as Boian, Hamangia, Gumelnita and Cucuteni left elaborate painted pottery and thousands of clay figurines. The whole system collapsed in the late fourth millennium, replaced by more mobile, pastoral societies with kurgan burials.

Helenistike (Albania, 336 BC–169 BC).label: Helenistike
Helenistike (Albania, 336 BC–169 BC).prose:
[Albania, 336 BC–169 BC] Helenistike. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The age when the Illyrian south was drawn into the Hellenistic world: fortified cities such as Byllis, Amantia and Phoinike were built with monumental walls, theatres and stoas, coinage circulated widely, and local dynasts ruled alongside the Greek colonies of the coast. It closed with Rome's defeat of Macedon and the capture of the Illyrian king Gentius, which brought the region under Roman control.

Edad del Inicial (Spain, 2300 BC–1701 BC.label: Edad del Inicial
Edad del Inicial (Spain, 2300 BC–1701 BC.prose:
[Spain, 2300 BC–1701 BC] Edad del Inicial. Institute of Heritage Sciences, Spanish National Research Council (CSIC Incipit). Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The first bronze-using centuries in Iberia, when Copper Age settlements such as Los Millares were abandoned and the fortified El Argar towns of the southeast rose in their place. Burial shifted decisively to the individual — bodies placed in jars or cists with daggers, awls and silver ornaments — reflecting societies divided by rank and control of metal. Fortified hilltop sites, storage and craft specialisation appear across much of the peninsula.

késő bronzkor (Hungary, 1400 BC–901 BC).label: késő bronzkor
késő bronzkor (Hungary, 1400 BC–901 BC).prose:
[Hungary, 1400 BC–901 BC] késő bronzkor. Hungarian National Museum. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The age of urnfields in the Carpathian Basin, when cremated remains in pottery urns replaced older burial rites across huge areas. Bronze production reached industrial scale - swords, sheet-metal armour, cauldrons and vast buried hoards of scrap and finished goods - while fortified hilltop centres controlled trade routes. The Gáva and related groups of this era set the stage for the arrival of iron and of horse-riding peoples from the eastern steppe.

La Tène III (France, 150 BC–51 BC).label: La Tène III
La Tène III (France, 150 BC–51 BC).prose:
[France, 150 BC–51 BC] La Tène III. INRAP. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The last stage of independent Celtic culture in Gaul, dominated by oppida — walled towns of tens of hectares with streets, workshops, mints and market quarters. Coinage, mass-produced wheel-thrown pottery and enormous quantities of imported Italian wine mark an economy tightly linked to Rome. It ends with Caesar's conquest.

Perandorake e mesme (Albania, AD 100–AD.label: Perandorake e mesme
Perandorake e mesme (Albania, AD 100–AD.prose:
[Albania, AD 100–AD 299] Perandorake e mesme. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The high point of provincial prosperity in the Adriatic lands, when cities rebuilt their theatres, baths and water systems and coastal estates exported oil, wine and timber. Inscriptions show local families rising into the imperial administration and army, while eastern cults and early Christian communities took root in the port towns. The third-century crisis brought raids, walls around cities and the end of the building boom.

римскиот период (Republic of Macedonia,.label: римскиот период
римскиот период (Republic of Macedonia,.prose:
[Macedonia, AD 30–AD 299] римскиот период. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Roman rule turned the region into a well-connected province: the Via Egnatia carried traffic from the Adriatic to Byzantium, and cities like Stobi, Scupi and Heraclea Lyncestis filled with theatres, baths, colonnaded streets and mosaic floors. Veteran colonies and Latin-speaking settlers mixed with local Paeonian and Macedonian populations, and inscriptions show both Greek and Latin in daily use. By the end of the period Christianity was spreading fast, setting up the great basilica-building of later centuries.

Epoca Modernă (Romania, AD 1821–AD 1877).label: Epoca Modernă
Epoca Modernă (Romania, AD 1821–AD 1877).prose:
[Romania, AD 1821–AD 1877] Epoca Modernă. Romanian Academy. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Tudor Vladimirescu's rising against Phanariot rule opened decades of national agitation that ran through the 1848 revolutions to the election of Alexandru Ioan Cuza as prince of both Moldavia and Wallachia in 1859. The united principalities secularised monastery lands, reformed agriculture and law, invited in a German prince as Carol I, and ended the period fighting alongside Russia for independence from the Ottomans.

Geometric (Cypro-Geometric) II (Cyprus,.label: Geometric (Cypro-Geometric) II
Geometric (Cypro-Geometric) II (Cyprus,.prose:
[Cyprus, 950 BC–851 BC] Geometric (Cypro-Geometric) II. Jamieson, 2007 (Ian Potter Museum exhibition). Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

A quieter, more prosperous stretch when Cypriot towns rebuilt trade links across the eastern Mediterranean and Phoenicians from Tyre established themselves at Kition, rebuilding its great temple. Cypriot copper again moved abroad, and Bichrome pottery with its concentric circles and friezes reached the Levant and the Aegean. The island's separate kingdoms were beginning to take the shape they would hold for centuries.

Bronze Age (Denmark, 1700 BC–501 BC).label: Bronze Age
Bronze Age (Denmark, 1700 BC–501 BC).prose:
[Denmark, 1700 BC–501 BC] Bronze Age. ARENA1/ADS. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Pile-dwelling villages on the Ljubljana Marshes and hilltop settlements to the east mark a landscape of small farming communities well connected to the Alpine and Pannonian metal trade. From the later centuries the Urnfield tradition took hold, with cremation cemeteries and large hoards of bronze axes, sickles and weapons buried in the ground. These hoards are among the region's richest prehistoric finds and hint at both ritual deposition and the workshops of travelling smiths.

La Tène B (Germany, 400 BC–251 BC).label: La Tène B
La Tène B (Germany, 400 BC–251 BC).prose:
[Germany, Switzerland, Czech Republic, Liechtenstein, 400 BC–251 BC] La Tène B. Spatial coverage: Czech Republic, Germany, Liechtenstein, Switzerland. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The phase of the great Celtic migrations, when war bands from the north moved into the Po valley, the middle Danube and the Balkans; the sack of Rome and the raid on Delphi belong to these generations. Large flat cemeteries of inhumations replace the earlier princely tumuli, with men buried with sword, spear and shield and women with brooches and rings. Metalworkers developed the Waldalgesheim or Vegetal Style, a flowing tendril ornament that spread across Europe with astonishing uniformity.

âge du Bronze final (France, 1400 BC–801.node: âge du Bronze final (France, 1400 BC–801 BC)
âge du Bronze final (France, 1400 BC–801.label: âge du Bronze final
âge du Bronze final (France, 1400 BC–801.prose:
[France, 1400 BC–801 BC] âge du Bronze final. INRAP. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Bronze production reached industrial scale: founders' hoards of hundreds of broken axes and swords were buried, and standardised types circulated over vast distances. Cremation in urnfields replaced older burial customs, and fortified hilltop sites multiplied. It is the world just before iron, and its metalwork traditions fed directly into the first Iron Age chiefdoms.

Mesolithic (Denmark, 9000 BC–3901 BC).label: Mesolithic
Mesolithic (Denmark, 9000 BC–3901 BC).prose:
[Denmark, 9000 BC–3901 BC] Mesolithic. ARENA1/ADS. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

After the ice sheets withdrew, birch and then dense oak forest spread over Britain, and hunter-gatherers followed the red deer, wild pig and fish into it. They worked tiny flint microliths into composite arrows and harpoons, built shelters at places like Star Carr, and burned back woodland to draw game into clearings. For most of these millennia Britain was joined to the continent by the drowned plain of Doggerland, and the sea's final closure around 6000 BC turned the population into islanders.

Romersk järnålder (Sweden, AD 1–AD 399).label: Romersk järnålder
Romersk järnålder (Sweden, AD 1–AD 399).prose:
[Sweden, AD 1–AD 399] Romersk järnålder. SND. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Roman glass, bronze vessels, coins and weapons reached Sweden through trade and mercenary service, concentrating in the hands of emerging elites on Öland, Gotland and in the Mälar valley. Farms grew into more permanent settlements with stone-walled field systems, and burials became sharply unequal in wealth. The first runic inscriptions appear, and weapon deposits and hillforts point to organised warfare between competing chiefdoms.

ранно средновековие (Bulgaria, AD 610–AD.label: ранно средновековие
ранно средновековие (Bulgaria, AD 610–AD.prose:
[Bulgaria, AD 610–AD 1017] ранно средновековие. National Institute of Archaeology with Museum, Automated Information System "Archaeological Map of Bulgaria". Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Slavic settlers and the Bulgars of Asparuh established a state south of the Danube in 681, with capitals at Pliska and later Preslav built partly from Roman stone. Boris I accepted Christianity in 864 and the disciples of Cyril and Methodius made Bulgaria the cradle of Slavonic letters, producing the Cyrillic alphabet and a large translated literature. Simeon's reign brought territorial and cultural peak; defeat of Samuil and Byzantine conquest in 1018 ended the First Bulgarian Empire.

Tweede Wereldoorlog (Netherlands, AD 194.label: Tweede Wereldoorlog
Tweede Wereldoorlog (Netherlands, AD 194.prose:
[Netherlands, AD 1940–AD 1944] Tweede Wereldoorlog. Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

German forces overran the country in five days in May 1940, and occupation brought censorship, forced labour drafts, and the deportation of more than 100,000 Jews, among them Anne Frank. Resistance networks, underground presses and a national railway strike met with reprisals, and the winter of 1944-45 brought famine to the still-occupied west while the south was being liberated. Traces survive in bunkers, crash sites, camp remains and the bombed-out cores of Rotterdam and other towns.

Ottoman (Cyprus, AD 1572–AD 1913).label: Ottoman
Ottoman (Cyprus, AD 1572–AD 1913).prose:
[Cyprus, AD 1572–AD 1913] Ottoman. no source provided. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Ottoman victory at Kosovo opened the way to the absorption of the Serbian lands, completed with the fall of the Despotate in the fifteenth century. For some three hundred years Serbia was a frontier province, its peasants organised under the timar system and its Orthodox Church tolerated as a religious community, with a great migration of Serbs northwards after the failed Habsburg advance of the 1690s. Uprisings from 1804 won autonomy and set the country on the road to full independence.

Moyen Âge classique (France, AD 1000–AD.label: Moyen Âge classique
Moyen Âge classique (France, AD 1000–AD.prose:
[France, AD 1000–AD 1299] Moyen Âge classique. INRAP. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Population, ploughland and towns all expanded, the Capetian kings turned a small domain around Paris into the strongest monarchy in Europe, and cathedral builders invented the Gothic style at Saint-Denis, Chartres and Amiens. Universities took shape in Paris, fairs in Champagne linked Flemish cloth to Mediterranean trade, and knights left for the crusades. It is the France of Philip Augustus, Louis IX and the troubadours - confident, expanding, and not yet touched by plague.

Bas Moyen Âge (France, AD 1300–AD 1491).label: Bas Moyen Âge
Bas Moyen Âge (France, AD 1300–AD 1491).prose:
[France, AD 1300–AD 1491] Bas Moyen Âge. INRAP. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

War with England, recurring plague and rural depopulation dominated these generations, yet they also produced a stronger royal state: standing armies, permanent taxation and a crown that emerged from the Hundred Years' War far more powerful than before. Towns rebuilt in flamboyant Gothic, printing arrived in the 1470s, and the marriage politics of the 1490s folded Brittany into the kingdom.

Paleolit (Albania, 600000 BC–4001 BC).label: Paleolit
Paleolit (Albania, 600000 BC–4001 BC).prose:
[Albania, 600000 BC–4001 BC] Paleolit. This period is derived from the aggregation of three periods in the 2004 Fasti Periodization:. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The long era of hunting and gathering with chipped stone tools, spanning the ice ages and the arrival of modern humans in the Balkans. Traces come mostly from caves and open-air scatters of flint and quartz, where hunters pursued deer, wild cattle and other game and sheltered seasonally. Everything that follows in the region's prehistory rests on this period of small mobile bands.

újkor (Hungary, AD 1711–AD 1866).label: újkor
újkor (Hungary, AD 1711–AD 1866).prose:
[Hungary, AD 1711–AD 1866] újkor. Hungarian National Museum. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The long Habsburg peace after the Rákóczi uprising was settled by treaty. Depopulated lands in the south and centre were resettled by German, Serb and Slovak colonists, estates were reorganised, and Vienna governed through a compliant Hungarian nobility. From the 1820s a reform generation pushed Hungarian language, industry and constitutional rights, leading to the revolution of 1848, its defeat by Austrian and Russian armies, and the negotiations that would produce the Compromise of 1867.

Vroeg Neolithicum A (Netherlands, 5300 B.label: Vroeg Neolithicum A
Vroeg Neolithicum A (Netherlands, 5300 B.prose:
[Netherlands, 5300 BC–4901 BC] Vroeg Neolithicum A. Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The Linearbandkeramik settlers of the southern loess belt brought the first full farming economy to the region: substantial longhouses, cereal fields, cattle and sheep, and finely made pottery decorated with incised bands. Their villages, such as those around Elsloo and Sittard, sit in a small favoured pocket of the country while the rest remained the world of hunter-fishers.

Historisk tid (Sweden, AD 1050–AD 2000).label: Historisk tid
Historisk tid (Sweden, AD 1050–AD 2000).prose:
[Sweden, AD 1050–AD 2000] Historisk tid. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Written sources begin to supplement archaeology as Sweden was drawn into Latin Christendom: churches replaced cult sites, dioceses and a royal administration took shape, and the Viking-age world of raiding and rune-carving faded. Later centuries brought medieval towns and stone castles, the Reformation, an empire around the Baltic, and eventually industrialisation and emigration. Excavations from this period turn up urban waterfronts, cellars, coins and everyday objects that can be matched against surviving documents.

Epoca Târzie a Bronzului (Romania, 1600.node: Epoca Târzie a Bronzului (Romania, 1600 BC–1051 BC)
Epoca Târzie a Bronzului (Romania, 1600.label: Epoca Târzie a Bronzului
Epoca Târzie a Bronzului (Romania, 1600.prose:
[Romania, 1600 BC–1051 BC] Epoca Târzie a Bronzului. Romanian Academy. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Bronze production reached industrial scale, and hoards of hundreds of axes, sickles and broken scrap were buried across the region, hinting at crisis as much as wealth. Noua and Gáva communities, channelled pottery and new fortified sites signal the unsettled centuries in which iron began to appear and the Bronze Age trade system broke down.

Hallstatt A (Germany, 1200 BC–1001 BC).label: Hallstatt A
Hallstatt A (Germany, 1200 BC–1001 BC).prose:
[Germany, Switzerland, Czech Republic, Liechtenstein, 1200 BC–1001 BC] Hallstatt A. Spatial coverage: Czech Republic, Germany, Liechtenstein, Switzerland. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Despite the name, these are Late Bronze Age generations in Reinecke's scheme: the Urnfield world, where the dead were cremated and their ashes buried in pots in vast flat cemeteries. Bronzesmiths worked sheet metal into helmets, cuirasses and buckets, and fortified hilltop settlements multiplied across southern Germany.

Vroeg Neolithicum B (Netherlands, 4900 B.label: Vroeg Neolithicum B
Vroeg Neolithicum B (Netherlands, 4900 B.prose:
[Netherlands, 4900 BC–4201 BC] Vroeg Neolithicum B. Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

After the Bandkeramik villages ended, farming ideas spread slowly northwards into the river and coastal wetlands. Swifterbant communities made pottery, kept some cattle and pigs and grew small amounts of cereal, but continued to rely heavily on fish, fowl and wild plants, living in a landscape of creeks and marshes.

Bronzezeit (Austria, 2200 BC–801 BC).label: Bronzezeit
Bronzezeit (Austria, 2200 BC–801 BC).prose:
[Austria, 2200 BC–801 BC] Bronzezeit. Austrian Academy of Sciences. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Alpine copper from mines such as the Mitterberg fed a metal industry that supplied much of central Europe, and the Danube corridor carried goods and ideas in both directions. Burial fashions track the era's phases: rich flat graves early on, then great tumuli, then the cremation cemeteries of the Urnfield period. Salt digging began in the Hallstatt valley in these centuries, laying the foundation for the wealth of the Iron Age chieftains who followed.

Empire romaine (France, 27 BC–AD 499).label: Empire romaine
Empire romaine (France, 27 BC–AD 499).prose:
[France, 27 BC–AD 499] Empire romaine. INRAP. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Under the emperors, Gaul was remade as a Roman landscape of colonies, roads, aqueducts and villa estates, with Lugdunum (Lyon) as its administrative hub and Latin gradually replacing the Celtic tongues. Wine, pottery and grain moved along the Rhône and Rhine to feed cities and frontier armies. Third-century invasions and civil wars battered the province, and by the fifth century Frankish, Burgundian and Visigothic kingdoms were forming inside the shell of Roman institutions.

Kupferzeit (Germany, 4250 BC–2201 BC).label: Kupferzeit
Kupferzeit (Germany, 4250 BC–2201 BC).prose:
[Germany, Switzerland, Czech Republic, Liechtenstein, 4250 BC–2201 BC] Kupferzeit. Spatial coverage: Czech Republic, Germany, Liechtenstein, Switzerland. no source provided. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Copper working spread through central Europe alongside farming villages, and metal objects began to mark out status in a way pottery and stone never had. These centuries saw the Michelsberg and Corded Ware traditions, then Bell Beaker burials with their distinctive drinking vessels and archery gear, plus the first ox-drawn wagons and ploughs. The Alpine ice mummy known as Ötzi, carrying a copper axe, belongs to this world.

Hekuri i hershëm (Albania, 1100 BC–801 B.label: Hekuri i hershëm
Hekuri i hershëm (Albania, 1100 BC–801 B.prose: [Albania, 1100 BC–801 BC] Hekuri i hershëm. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Geometric (Cypro-Geometric) I (Cyprus, 1.label: Geometric (Cypro-Geometric) I
Geometric (Cypro-Geometric) I (Cyprus, 1.prose:
[Cyprus, 1050 BC–951 BC] Geometric (Cypro-Geometric) I. Jamieson, 2007 (Ian Potter Museum exhibition). Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Cyprus reorganised itself after the collapse of the Bronze Age palace world: many old towns were abandoned and new centres such as Salamis and Kition took their place. Greek-speaking settlers were absorbed into the island's population, chamber tombs replaced older burial forms, and iron working became routine for tools and weapons. White Painted and Bichrome wares decorated with compass-drawn circles and bands define the pottery of these generations.

късна античност (Bulgaria, AD 395–AD 609.label: късна античност
късна античност (Bulgaria, AD 395–AD 609.prose:
[Bulgaria, AD 395–AD 609] късна античност. National Institute of Archaeology with Museum, Automated Information System "Archaeological Map of Bulgaria". Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

After the empire split, these lands became the Balkan frontier of Constantinople: bishops' basilicas rose in Serdica, Philippopolis and the Danube towns, and Justinian poured money into refortifying the limes. Rural populations retreated to hilltop refuges as Huns, Goths, Avars and Slavs raided repeatedly. By the early seventh century the frontier gave way, Roman urban life ended in most places, and Slavic settlers were occupying the countryside.

Vroege Middeleeuwen B (Netherlands, AD 5.label: Vroege Middeleeuwen B
Vroege Middeleeuwen B (Netherlands, AD 5.prose:
[Netherlands, AD 525–AD 724] Vroege Middeleeuwen B. Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Settlement recovered as Merovingian Frankish influence pushed north from the Meuse and Scheldt, bringing wheel-thrown pottery, glass vessels and row-grave cemeteries with weapons and brooches. In the north, farmers built up terp mounds against the sea and Frisian traders began working the coastal routes, laying the ground for the emporium at Dorestad.

Frihetstiden (Sweden, AD 1719–AD 1772).label: Frihetstiden
Frihetstiden (Sweden, AD 1719–AD 1772).prose:
[Sweden, AD 1719–AD 1772] Frihetstiden. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

With the death of Charles XII and the collapse of the Baltic empire, power passed from the crown to the Riksdag of the Estates and its council, producing half a century of party politics between the war-minded Hats and the cautious Caps. It was an age of scientific and economic ambition - Linnaeus, Celsius, Polhem, the Royal Academy of Sciences - and of the world's first freedom-of-the-press ordinance, which also enshrined public access to official documents. Factional deadlock and foreign bribery discredited the system, and Gustav III ended it with a bloodless coup.

съвременна епоха (Bulgaria, AD 1878–AD 2.label: съвременна епоха
съвременна епоха (Bulgaria, AD 1878–AD 2.prose:
[Bulgaria, AD 1878–AD 2000] съвременна епоха. National Institute of Archaeology with Museum, Automated Information System "Archaeological Map of Bulgaria". Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The Russo-Turkish war and the Treaty of Berlin created a Bulgarian principality, which became a kingdom, expanded and lost territory in a run of wars, and ended up on the defeated side twice in world conflicts. A communist republic from 1946 collectivised farming, industrialised heavily and built the concrete apartment blocks that still house most city dwellers. The regime fell in 1989, opening a difficult transition to market economy and European integration.

Hallstatt Iron Age (Germany, 1200 BC–481.label: Hallstatt Iron Age
Hallstatt Iron Age (Germany, 1200 BC–481.prose:
[Germany, Switzerland, Czech Republic, Liechtenstein, 1200 BC–481 BC] Hallstatt Iron Age. Spatial coverage: Czech Republic, Germany, Liechtenstein, Switzerland. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The whole sequence Reinecke labelled Hallstatt A–D, running from the late Bronze Age Urnfield cemeteries through the adoption of iron to the wealthy princely centres of the sixth century. Over these centuries central Europe shifted from broadly egalitarian cremation cemeteries to towering burial mounds stuffed with wagons, gold and Mediterranean wine services. Its end coincides with the rise of La Tène art and the Celtic migrations that would take warriors as far as Rome and Delphi.

Early Medieval (Iceland, AD 1000–AD 1099.label: Early Medieval
Early Medieval (Iceland, AD 1000–AD 1099.prose:
[Iceland, AD 1000–AD 1099] Early Medieval. ARENA1/ADS. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Avar and Slav raids broke the Byzantine Danube frontier, emptying the old Roman towns and bringing permanent Slavic settlement to the central Balkans. Over the following centuries small Serb principalities emerged in the hills between Byzantine and Bulgarian spheres, and Christian missionaries introduced the Slavonic liturgy and Cyrillic letters. Archaeologically the shift is stark: masonry cities give way to timber villages, cremation cemeteries and simple hand-made pottery.

късен неолит (Bulgaria, 5200 BC–4901 BC).label: късен неолит
късен неолит (Bulgaria, 5200 BC–4901 BC).prose:
[Bulgaria, 5200 BC–4901 BC] късен неолит. National Institute of Archaeology with Museum, Automated Information System "Archaeological Map of Bulgaria". Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Villages on the tells of the Thracian plain grew taller and denser, their mudbrick houses rebuilt on the rubble of earlier ones, with the Karanovo mound as the classic sequence. Pottery shifted from painted wares to dark burnished vessels, and contacts with the Vinča world to the northwest brought new shapes and figurines. The groundwork for the copper-using cultures that followed — long-distance exchange, craft specialisation, permanent villages — was laid in these centuries.

Karolinska tiden (Sweden, AD 1654–AD 171.label: Karolinska tiden
Karolinska tiden (Sweden, AD 1654–AD 171.prose:
[Sweden, AD 1654–AD 1718] Karolinska tiden. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Sweden's Caroline age, under Charles X Gustav, Charles XI and Charles XII, when a thinly populated northern kingdom controlled the Baltic and fielded one of Europe's most feared armies. Charles XI built royal absolutism and a self-supporting regimental system; his son spent eighteen years at war, won stunning victories, lost at Poltava, and died at Fredriksten, leaving the empire to be dismantled.

prazgodovina (Slovenia, 1498000 BC–31 BC.label: prazgodovina
prazgodovina (Slovenia, 1498000 BC–31 BC.prose:
[Slovenia, 1498000 BC–31 BC] prazgodovina. ZRC SAZU, Institute of Archaeology. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Everything from the earliest traces of human presence in the caves of the Alpine and Karst borderlands to the Roman annexation of the eastern Adriatic hinterland. It includes the Palaeolithic hunters of Divje Babe and Potok Cave, the pile-dwelling villages of the Ljubljana Marshes, and the fortified hilltop settlements and richly furnished burial mounds of the Iron Age Hallstatt communities famous for their decorated bronze situlae. The territory's position on routes between the Danube basin, Italy and the Balkans made it a crossroads throughout.

средновековие (Bulgaria, AD 610–AD 1761).label: средновековие
средновековие (Bulgaria, AD 610–AD 1761).prose:
[Bulgaria, AD 610–AD 1761] средновековие. Added after initial ARIADNE collection creation at request of J. Richards on behalf of Bulgarian ARIADNE partners. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

An unusually long medieval span, running from the arrival of the Slavs and the founding of the Bulgarian state through the conversion to Christianity, the Cyrillic alphabet and the capitals at Pliska, Preslav and Tarnovo. Two Bulgarian empires rose and fell against Byzantium before Ottoman conquest in the late fourteenth century, after which Bulgarian culture survived largely in monasteries and village churches. The period closes on the eve of the national revival, with Paisius of Hilendar's history written in 1762.

Hochmittelalter (Germany, AD 976–AD 1249.label: Hochmittelalter
Hochmittelalter (Germany, AD 976–AD 1249.prose:
[Germany, Switzerland, Czech Republic, Liechtenstein, AD 976–AD 1249] Hochmittelalter. Spatial coverage: Czech Republic, Germany, Liechtenstein, Switzerland. no source provided. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The Babenberg margraves, granted the eastern march in 976, turned a frontier zone into a duchy with its own law, towns and Danube trade, with Vienna emerging as a residence city. Monasteries such as Melk and Klosterneuburg were founded or rebuilt in stone, hilltop castles multiplied, and forest and marsh were cleared for new villages. The dynasty died out in 1246, opening the succession struggle that would eventually bring the Habsburgs.

Prehistorie (Netherlands, 1000000 BC–13.label: Prehistorie
Prehistorie (Netherlands, 1000000 BC–13.prose:
[Netherlands, 1000000 BC–13 BC] Prehistorie. Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Everything in the Low Countries before written records begin with the Roman conquest: Neanderthal hunting camps, Mesolithic foragers on the sandy uplands, the first farmers with their longhouses and flint mines, the hunebedden built of glacial boulders, and Bronze and Iron Age communities whose barrows and bog deposits dot the landscape. Much of it survives only because peat and clay sealed and preserved it.

starejša bronasta doba (Slovenia, 1750 B.label: starejša bronasta doba
starejša bronasta doba (Slovenia, 1750 B.prose:
[Slovenia, 1750 BC–1501 BC] starejša bronasta doba. ZRC SAZU, Institute of Archaeology. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Metalworking became a regular part of life rather than a rarity, with bronze axes, daggers and ornaments produced in local styles and traded along Alpine and Danubian routes. Settlements clustered in river valleys and on defensible rises, and hoards buried in the ground show both wealth and anxiety. Copper from Alpine sources and tin brought from far away tied the region into long-distance exchange networks.

Vroege IJzertijd (Netherlands, 800 BC–50.label: Vroege IJzertijd
Vroege IJzertijd (Netherlands, 800 BC–50.prose:
[Netherlands, 800 BC–501 BC] Vroege IJzertijd. Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Iron, smelted locally from bog ore, freed communities from dependence on distant copper and tin sources, and ploughs, axes and knives became commonplace. Farmsteads with byre-houses spread across the sandy soils, and the dead were cremated and buried in vast urnfields marked by small mounds and ditches. Rich chieftains' graves such as Oss, with its imported bronze bucket and bent iron sword, hint at contact with the Hallstatt world to the south.

Edad del Bronce (Spain, 2300 BC–801 BC).label: Edad del Bronce
Edad del Bronce (Spain, 2300 BC–801 BC).prose:
[Spain, 2300 BC–801 BC] Edad del Bronce. Institute of Heritage Sciences, Spanish National Research Council (CSIC Incipit). Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Metalworking in copper and tin spread across the peninsula, and in the southeast the El Argar culture built fortified hilltop towns with rectangular houses, buried its dead in jars beneath house floors, and marked out sharp differences of wealth in silver and bronze grave goods. Elsewhere communities raised cairns and stelae, worked gold, and traded along Atlantic and Mediterranean routes. It was the first period in Iberia with clearly stratified societies controlling metal and land.

архајскиот период (Republic of Macedonia.node: архајскиот период (Republic of Macedonia, 500 BC–351 BC)
архајскиот период (Republic of Macedonia.label: архајскиот период
архајскиот период (Republic of Macedonia.prose:
[Macedonia, 500 BC–351 BC] архајскиот период. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Small kingdoms and tribal groups, among them the Paeonians and the Lyncestians, controlled the river valleys and traded with the Greek south and the Adriatic; the richest graves, such as those at Trebenište, held gold face masks, bronze kraters and imported weapons. Persian armies passed through in the early 5th century, and Greek coinage and pottery spread widely. The period closes as the Argead kings of Macedon under Philip II absorbed these polities into a single expanding state.

zgodnji srednji vek (Slovenia, AD 600–AD.label: zgodnji srednji vek
zgodnji srednji vek (Slovenia, AD 600–AD.prose:
[Slovenia, AD 600–AD 999] zgodnji srednji vek. ZRC SAZU, Institute of Archaeology. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

After Roman order collapsed, Slavic groups settled the valleys and hill country, and the Alpine principality of Carantania emerged with its own ritual of installing dukes. Bavarian and then Frankish overlordship followed, bringing missionaries from Salzburg and Aquileia and drawing the region into the Carolingian empire and the Latin Church. Cemeteries of this era, with their simple jewellery and weapons, chart the mingling of newcomers with surviving late-antique communities — and Slovene begins to take shape as a distinct language.

Edad Contemporáneo (Spain, AD 1900–AD 20.label: Edad Contemporáneo
Edad Contemporáneo (Spain, AD 1900–AD 20.prose:
[Spain, AD 1900–AD 2000] Edad Contemporáneo. Institute of Heritage Sciences, Spanish National Research Council (CSIC Incipit). Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Spain's twentieth century ran from the trauma of losing Cuba and the Philippines through dictatorship, the Second Republic, and a civil war that killed hundreds of thousands and brought nearly forty years of Franco's rule. Isolation gave way to industrial and tourist boom in the 1960s, and after Franco's death the country rebuilt itself as a parliamentary monarchy, joining the European Community in 1986. Rapid urbanisation drained the countryside and turned Madrid and Barcelona into vast modern cities.

Jüngere Kupferzeit (Germany, 3000 BC–220.label: Jüngere Kupferzeit
Jüngere Kupferzeit (Germany, 3000 BC–220.prose: [Germany, Switzerland, Czech Republic, Liechtenstein, 3000 BC–2201 BC] Jüngere Kupferzeit. Spatial coverage: Czech Republic, Germany, Liechtenstein, Switzerland. no source provided. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

отоманскиот период (Republic of Macedoni.label: отоманскиот период
отоманскиот период (Republic of Macedoni.prose:
[Macedonia, AD 1371–AD 1911] отоманскиот период. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

After the Ottoman victory on the Maritsa in 1371 the region's local lords were absorbed into a new imperial order, and its towns were rebuilt with mosques, bridges, caravanserais and bazaars — Skopje's Old Bazaar and Bitola's markets grew from this. Christian, Muslim, Jewish and Vlach communities lived under a tax and land system organised from Istanbul, while monasteries kept Slavonic literacy alive. Nineteenth-century schools, printing and church disputes turned into competing national movements, and Ottoman rule ended with the Balkan Wars.

Vroeg Neolithicum (Netherlands, 5300 BC–.label: Vroeg Neolithicum
Vroeg Neolithicum (Netherlands, 5300 BC–.prose:
[Netherlands, 5300 BC–4201 BC] Vroeg Neolithicum. Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Farming reached the Low Countries in two very different ways. On the fertile loess of southern Limburg, incoming Bandkeramik villagers built long timber houses and grew wheat and barley, while in the wetlands to the north communities kept hunting, fishing and gathering, adopting pottery and a few domestic animals on their own terms. The result was a long overlap between farmers and foragers rather than a clean transition.

Frühes Mittelalter (Germany, AD 568–AD 9.label: Frühes Mittelalter
Frühes Mittelalter (Germany, AD 568–AD 9.prose:
[Germany, Switzerland, Czech Republic, Liechtenstein, AD 568–AD 975] Frühes Mittelalter. Spatial coverage: Czech Republic, Germany, Liechtenstein, Switzerland. no source provided. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Frankish, Saxon, Bavarian and Alemannic territories were gradually welded together, first under the Merovingians and then by the Carolingians, whose empire under Charlemagne reached from the Elbe to Rome. Christianity spread through monastic foundations and missionary bishoprics, Latin learning was revived in court schools, and the manorial estate became the basic economic unit. After the empire split, the eastern kingdom developed into Germany, and the Ottonians revived the imperial title in 962.

Frühes Mittelalter (Austria, AD 568–AD 9.label: Frühes Mittelalter
Frühes Mittelalter (Austria, AD 568–AD 9.prose:
[Austria, AD 568–AD 975] Frühes Mittelalter. Austrian Academy of Sciences. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Frankish, Saxon, Bavarian and Alemannic territories were gradually welded together, first under the Merovingians and then by the Carolingians, whose empire under Charlemagne reached from the Elbe to Rome. Christianity spread through monastic foundations and missionary bishoprics, Latin learning was revived in court schools, and the manorial estate became the basic economic unit. After the empire split, the eastern kingdom developed into Germany, and the Ottonians revived the imperial title in 962.

novi vek (Slovenia, AD 1500–AD 1799).label: novi vek
novi vek (Slovenia, AD 1500–AD 1799).prose:
[Slovenia, AD 1500–AD 1799] novi vek. ZRC SAZU, Institute of Archaeology. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Habsburg rule, Protestant preaching and then forceful Counter-Reformation, Ottoman raids on the southeastern frontier, and peasant uprisings all reshaped Slovene lands. The first books in Slovene were printed in this era, fixing a written language that later carried national identity. Towns rebuilt in Baroque style, and mining, ironworking and the trade road to Trieste tied the region into wider European markets.

La Tène (France, 450 BC–51 BC).label: La Tène
La Tène (France, 450 BC–51 BC).prose:
[France, 450 BC–51 BC] La Tène. INRAP. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Named after a votive deposit of weapons in a Swiss lake, this culture spread across Gaul with a new elite of horse-riding warriors buried with chariots, swords and imported wine services. Its curvilinear art, all tendrils, palmettes and hidden faces, is the most recognisable Celtic style. By the final century large fortified towns, coinage and mass production were emerging, and it all ended with the Roman conquest.

Mittlere Kupferzeit (Austria, 3400 BC–30.label: Mittlere Kupferzeit
Mittlere Kupferzeit (Austria, 3400 BC–30.prose:
[Austria, 3400 BC–3001 BC] Mittlere Kupferzeit. Austrian Academy of Sciences. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Farming communities across central Germany buried their dead collectively in megalithic chambers and gallery graves, leaving behind the pottery styles archaeologists label Salzmünde, Walternienburg and Bernburg. Copper objects were still scarce and prestigious, but the plough, ox traction and the earliest wheeled vehicles were transforming how land was worked and goods moved. It is the world of the Alpine lake villages and of Ötzi, and it set the stage for the sweeping cultural changes of the Corded Ware horizon that followed.

Bashkëkohore (Albania, AD 1944–AD 2000).label: Bashkëkohore
Bashkëkohore (Albania, AD 1944–AD 2000).prose:
[Albania, AD 1944–AD 2000] Bashkëkohore. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Enver Hoxha's communist party took power at the end of the Second World War and held Albania in Europe's most rigid isolation — collectivised farms, banned religion, hundreds of thousands of concrete bunkers, and successive ruptures with Yugoslavia, the USSR and finally China. The regime collapsed in 1990–91, followed by mass emigration, the ruinous pyramid-scheme crisis of 1997 and a difficult transition to a market economy.

Primera Edad del Hierro (Spain, 800 BC–4.node: Primera Edad del Hierro (Spain, 800 BC–401 BC)
Primera Edad del Hierro (Spain, 800 BC–4.label: Primera Edad del Hierro
Primera Edad del Hierro (Spain, 800 BC–4.prose:
[Spain, 800 BC–401 BC] Primera Edad del Hierro. Institute of Heritage Sciences, Spanish National Research Council (CSIC Incipit). Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Phoenician traders settled the southern coasts, bringing iron, the potter's wheel, the alphabet and wine, and the wealth of the mines fed the legend of Tartessos. Inland, urnfield communities in the northeast absorbed influences from beyond the Pyrenees while Greek merchants founded Emporion. Out of this mix emerged the Iberian and Celtiberian cultures that Carthage and Rome would later fight over.

Förhistorisk tid (Sweden, 8200 BC–AD 105.label: Förhistorisk tid
Förhistorisk tid (Sweden, 8200 BC–AD 105.prose:
[Sweden, 8200 BC–AD 1050] Förhistorisk tid. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Everything from the first hunters following the retreating ice to the end of the Viking Age: reindeer and seal hunters, the arrival of farming, monumental stone tombs, rock carvings, bronze imported from the far south, and the rise of chieftains and trading places like Birka. Writing arrives only with the runic alphabet and, at the very end, with the church, so almost the whole story is told by graves, bogs, hoards and settlement traces. It ends conventionally around 1050, when Christianity and written record-keeping take hold.

средновековен (Republic of Macedonia, AD.label: средновековен
средновековен (Republic of Macedonia, AD.prose:
[Macedonia, AD 600–AD 1370] средновековен. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Slavic groups settled among the surviving late Roman towns, and the region was fought over for centuries by Byzantium and the Bulgarian state, with Ohrid serving as the capital of Tsar Samuil's realm around AD 1000. Ohrid also became a great church centre, home to the archbishopric and to the Slavonic literary tradition of Clement and Naum, whose disciples spread the Cyrillic script. Frescoed churches and monasteries from the Komnenian and Palaiologan centuries survive in numbers, before Ottoman armies absorbed the area in the later fourteenth century.

Chalcolithic (Cyprus, 4000 BC–2401 BC).label: Chalcolithic
Chalcolithic (Cyprus, 4000 BC–2401 BC).prose:
[Cyprus, 4000 BC–2401 BC] Chalcolithic. Jamieson, 2007 (Ian Potter Museum exhibition). Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The copper-using centuries before the first cities, and one of the most visually striking periods in the southern Levant: the Nahal Mishmar hoard of over four hundred cast copper maceheads and standards, the sanctuary at Ein Gedi, carved ivory figurines and bone-box ossuaries for secondary burial. Villagers such as those at Teleilat Ghassul added olives and dates to their fields and made cheese and wool from their herds. The whole system collapsed before the walled towns of the Early Bronze Age appeared.

mlajša železna doba (Slovenia, 300 BC–31.label: mlajša železna doba
mlajša železna doba (Slovenia, 300 BC–31.prose:
[Slovenia, 300 BC–31 BC] mlajša železna doba. ZRC SAZU, Institute of Archaeology. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Celtic-speaking groups, chiefly the Taurisci, brought La Tene material culture to the region: iron weapons, brooches, wheel-thrown pottery, and cemeteries of the Mokronog type. A local kingdom, Noricum, minted its own silver coinage and traded iron with Italy. Roman annexation at the end of the first century BC folded the whole area into the empire.

Post Medieval (Iceland, AD 1600–AD 1899).label: Post Medieval
Post Medieval (Iceland, AD 1600–AD 1899).prose:
[Iceland, AD 1600–AD 1899] Post Medieval. ARENA1/ADS. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Beginning with the dissolution of the monasteries and the Reformation's stripping of parish churches, these centuries carried England through civil war, the growth of an Atlantic empire, enclosure of open fields, and industrialisation. Excavations of the period yield mass-produced goods - tin-glazed and transfer-printed pottery, glass bottles, clay tobacco pipes, machine-made nails - that let sites be dated to within a decade or two. Landscapes changed as thoroughly as objects: hedged fields, canals, railways, mines and terraced workers' housing all belong to this span.

srednja bronasta doba (Slovenia, 1500 BC.label: srednja bronasta doba
srednja bronasta doba (Slovenia, 1500 BC.prose:
[Slovenia, 1500 BC–1251 BC] srednja bronasta doba. ZRC SAZU, Institute of Archaeology. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Communities across the eastern Alps and Pannonian fringe buried their dead under earthen mounds, a custom shared with the tumulus cultures of central Europe. Bronze working matured into regional workshop traditions turning out swords, sickles and elaborate pins, and hoards of finished metal were deposited in rivers and bogs. Hilltop settlements began to appear, foreshadowing the fortified centres of the later Bronze Age.

Árpád-kor (Hungary, AD 1000–AD 1300).label: Árpád-kor
Árpád-kor (Hungary, AD 1000–AD 1300).prose:
[Hungary, AD 1000–AD 1300] Árpád-kor. Hungarian National Museum. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The Hungarian kingdom took its Christian and European form under the descendants of Árpád, beginning with Stephen I's coronation, the founding of bishoprics and the organisation of royal counties. Nomadic traditions gave way to villages, stone churches, coinage and Latin charters, while the Mongol invasion of 1241 devastated the country and prompted a wave of stone castle building. The line died out in 1301, leaving a kingdom that had become a major Central European power.

kora középkor (Hungary, AD 885–AD 1300).label: kora középkor
kora középkor (Hungary, AD 885–AD 1300).prose:
[Hungary, AD 885–AD 1300] kora középkor. Hungarian National Museum. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

Hungary under the Árpád dynasty became a Latin Christian kingdom, organised into royal counties with bishoprics, monasteries and a royal coinage. Stone castles, market towns and immigrant German and Walloon settlers reshaped the countryside. The Mongol invasion of 1241 devastated the kingdom and prompted a systematic programme of stone fortification afterwards.

Siècle des Lumières (France, AD 1700–AD.label: Siècle des Lumières
Siècle des Lumières (France, AD 1700–AD.prose:
[France, AD 1700–AD 1799] Siècle des Lumières. INRAP. Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.

The French Enlightenment, when writers such as Voltaire, Montesquieu, Diderot and Rousseau subjected religion, law and monarchy to the test of reason in salons, cafés and the vast Encyclopédie. Their ideas circulated across Europe in French, the language of courts and correspondence, and made Paris the intellectual capital of the continent. The arguments about natural rights, tolerance and the sources of political authority fed directly into the Revolution at the century's end.

Alta Edad Media (Spain, AD 400–AD 699).label: Alta Edad Media
Alta Edad Media (Spain, AD 400–AD 699).prose:
[Spain, AD 400–AD 699] Alta Edad Media. Institute of Heritage Sciences, Spanish National Research Council (CSIC Incipit). Period definition from ARIADNE Data Collection — ARIADNE Consortium, 2015.
