The transitional century in which the Theban kings turned from tributaries into conquerors, waging war on the Hyksos of Avaris and on Kerma to the south. Seqenenre Tao died violently in battle - his skull still shows the axe wounds - and Kamose and Ahmose completed the campaign. Reunification brought a militarised monarchy, a professional army with chariotry, and the beginning of Egyptian expansion into Syria-Palestine.

Second World War (Algeria, AD 1939–AD 19.label: Second World War
Second World War (Algeria, AD 1939–AD 19.prose:
[MENA, AD 1939–AD 1945] Second World War. Spatial coverage: Algeria, Bahrain, Egypt, Iran, Iraq, Israel, Jordan, Kuwait. Period definition from EAMENA Database — University of Oxford, 2021.

Britain fought from the first day to the last: evacuation at Dunkirk, the air battle over southern England, and the Blitz that gutted city centres from London to Coventry. Rationing, conscription of women into war work, and the evacuation of children reshaped everyday life, while cracking German codes at Bletchley Park quietly changed the war at sea. Victory came at the cost of exhaustion, debt and the beginning of the end of empire.

South Arabian Period (Yemen, 800 BC–AD 6.label: South Arabian Period
South Arabian Period (Yemen, 800 BC–AD 6.prose:
[Southern Arabia, 800 BC–AD 640] South Arabian Period. Period definition from EAMENA Database — University of Oxford, 2021.

The era of the incense kingdoms - Saba, Ma'in, Qataban, Hadramawt and later Himyar - whose wealth came from frankincense and myrrh carried by camel caravan to the Mediterranean. They built monumental temples and the great dam at Marib, wrote in a distinctive monumental script, and irrigated the desert margins on a scale not matched again for centuries. Himyar's later adoption of Judaism and then Christianity, Aksumite and Persian intervention, and the coming of Islam closed the period.

Third Intermediate (Egypt, 1050 BC–650 B.label: Third Intermediate
Third Intermediate (Egypt, 1050 BC–650 B.prose:
[Egypt, 1050 BC–650 BC] Third Intermediate. Period definition from EAMENA Database — University of Oxford, 2021.

After the New Kingdom collapsed, Egypt split between kings ruling from the Delta and the high priests of Amun controlling Thebes. Libyan dynasties from settled military families took the throne, royal burials moved into temple precincts at Tanis, and the country fractured further into competing local rulers. Egypt's weakness invited outside powers, and the era ends with Kushite kings from Nubia asserting control over the south.

Vandal (Algeria, AD 430–AD 530).label: Vandal
Vandal (Algeria, AD 430–AD 530).prose:
[Maghreb, AD 430–AD 530] Vandal. Spatial coverage: Algeria, Libya, Mauritania, Morocco, Tunisia, Western Sahara. Period definition from EAMENA Database — University of Oxford, 2021.

After crossing from Spain and taking Carthage, the Vandals turned the richest grain-producing region of the western empire into an independent kingdom with its own fleet. They confiscated senatorial estates, promoted their Arian clergy over the Catholic hierarchy, and raided across the Mediterranean, sacking Rome in 455. Roman city life, Latin poetry and mosaic workshops carried on under them until Belisarius destroyed the kingdom in a single campaign in 533–34.

Contemporary Islamic, Early 20th century.label: Contemporary Islamic, Early 20th century
Contemporary Islamic, Early 20th century.prose:
[MENA, AD 1900–AD 1950] Contemporary Islamic, Early 20th century. Spatial coverage: Algeria, Bahrain, Egypt, Iran, Iraq, Israel, Jordan, Kuwait. Period definition from EAMENA Database — University of Oxford, 2021.

Algeria was administered as part of France itself, with the best farmland in European settler hands and the Muslim majority denied full citizenship. Algerians fought and died in both world wars, and the massacres at Sétif and Guelma in 1945 hardened a nationalist movement that had begun among reformist ulama, migrant workers in France and a small French-educated elite.

Epoca Pietrei (Romania, 1399999 BC–3499.label: Epoca Pietrei
Epoca Pietrei (Romania, 1399999 BC–3499.prose:
[Romania, 1399999 BC–3499 BC] Epoca Pietrei. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

The vast stretch from the earliest stone tools through the last hunter-gatherers and the first farming villages. Caves in the Carpathians have yielded some of Europe's oldest modern human remains, and later Neolithic communities of the Criș, Vinča and Hamangia traditions built villages, fired painted pottery and carved figurines such as the famous seated Thinker.

Neolitic dezvoltat (Romania, 5599 BC–499.label: Neolitic dezvoltat
Neolitic dezvoltat (Romania, 5599 BC–499.prose:
[Romania, 5599 BC–4999 BC] Neolitic dezvoltat. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

The mature phase of farming in the Carpathian–Danubian region, when tell settlements grew up and cultures such as Vinča, Dudești, Boian and Hamangia produced accomplished pottery and figurines. Villages were larger and longer-lived than before, with copper first appearing as ornaments and small tools. It set the stage for the spectacular Eneolithic cultures — Gumelnița and Cucuteni — that followed.

Eneolitic timpuriu (Romania, 4999 BC–449.label: Eneolitic timpuriu
Eneolitic timpuriu (Romania, 4999 BC–449.prose:
[Romania, 4999 BC–4499 BC] Eneolitic timpuriu. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

Copper metallurgy took hold among established farming villages, at first for small ornaments and simple cast tools. Communities of the Boian, Hamangia and Precucuteni traditions built up tell settlements and developed the pottery styles and figurine cults that define the later Copper Age here.

Eneolitic dezvoltat (Romania, 4499 BC–36.label: Eneolitic dezvoltat
Eneolitic dezvoltat (Romania, 4499 BC–36.prose:
[Romania, 4499 BC–3699 BC] Eneolitic dezvoltat. sau 4600-3800 a. Chr. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

The mature Copper Age of the Carpathian-Danubian area, dominated by the Cucuteni and Gumelnita cultures: large villages, sometimes fortified, fine polychrome painted pottery, abundant clay figurines and heavy cast copper tools. Exchange networks moved gold, copper, shell and flint across the region before these communities dissolved at the end of the fourth millennium.

Epoca Metalelor (Romania, 3699 BC–1099 B.label: Epoca Metalelor
Epoca Metalelor (Romania, 3699 BC–1099 B.prose:
[Romania, 3699 BC–1099 BC] Epoca Metalelor. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

A broad label covering the long stretch from the first widespread use of copper through the end of the Bronze Age. It groups together the rise of specialist metalworking, spectacular gold and copper hoards, and the more hierarchical, fortified societies that came with control of ore sources and trade routes.

Bronzul târziu (Romania, 1599 BC–1149 BC.label: Bronzul târziu
Bronzul târziu (Romania, 1599 BC–1149 BC.prose:
[Romania, 1599 BC–1149 BC] Bronzul târziu. Vulpe Al., 2020, p. 70; Motzoi-Chicideanu, I., Șandor-Chicideanu, M.,  2015, p. 9-53. Finalul epocii bronzului este plasat in secolul XII a. Chr. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

Fortified settlements, cremation cemeteries and workshop traditions such as the Wietenberg and Noua groups mark the Carpathian and Danubian lands at their Bronze Age height. The region is famous for its hoards — dozens of kilograms of axes, sickles, swords and ornaments deposited in the ground — along with some of prehistoric Europe's most spectacular gold work. Transylvania's copper and gold made it a supplier to distant markets, linking the area to the Aegean and central Europe.

Prima Epoca A Fierului (Romania, 1149 BC.node: Prima Epoca A Fierului (Romania, 1149 BC–449 BC)
Prima Epoca A Fierului (Romania, 1149 BC.label: Prima Epoca A Fierului
Prima Epoca A Fierului (Romania, 1149 BC.prose:
[Romania, 1149 BC–449 BC] Prima Epoca A Fierului. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

Iron replaced bronze across the Carpathian basin and lower Danube, and the great bronze hoards of the previous age gave way to fortified settlements and tumulus cemeteries. This is the world in which Thracian and Getic identities took shape, later described by Greek writers who traded along the Black Sea coast. Horse gear, ornate belt fittings and the first Greek imports mark the growing wealth of local elites.

Hallstatt târziu (Romania, 649 BC–449 BC.label: Hallstatt târziu
Hallstatt târziu (Romania, 649 BC–449 BC.prose:
[Romania, 649 BC–449 BC] Hallstatt târziu. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

The closing centuries of the Early Iron Age, when iron tools and weapons became ordinary rather than prestigious and fortified settlements multiplied. Greek colonies on the Black Sea coast drew the interior into Mediterranean trade, bringing wine amphorae and fine pottery upriver, while horse gear and weapons of steppe type mark contact with Scythian groups. Out of these communities emerged the Geto-Dacian world described by later Greek writers.

A Doua Epoca A Fierului (Romania, 449 BC.node: A Doua Epoca A Fierului (Romania, 449 BC–AD 106)
A Doua Epoca A Fierului (Romania, 449 BC.label: A Doua Epoca A Fierului
A Doua Epoca A Fierului (Romania, 449 BC.prose:
[Romania, 449 BC–AD 106] A Doua Epoca A Fierului. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

The La Tène-era Iron Age of the Carpathian-Danubian lands, when Celtic groups moved into Transylvania and mixed with local Thracian populations, bringing the potter's wheel and new metalwork styles. Out of this emerged the Dacian kingdoms, with hilltop fortresses, silver hoards and a lively trade in Greek and Roman goods. It closes with Trajan's wars and the conversion of Dacia into a Roman province.

Latene timpuriu (Romania, 449 BC–299 BC).label: Latene timpuriu
Latene timpuriu (Romania, 449 BC–299 BC).prose:
[Romania, 449 BC–299 BC] Latene timpuriu. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

Celtic groups moved east into Transylvania and the Danube plain, bringing flat inhumation cemeteries with iron swords, spears, brooches and fast-wheel-turned pottery. Their metalworking and wheel technology were taken up by the local Geto-Dacian population, whose fortified settlements and chieftains grew stronger through contact with Greek traders on the Black Sea coast. The mixing of these traditions laid the groundwork for the later Dacian kingdom.

Cultura ceramicii pictate, Faza II (Arad.node: Cultura ceramicii pictate, Faza II (Arad County, 5199 BC–4999 BC)
Cultura ceramicii pictate, Faza II (Arad.label: Cultura ceramicii pictate, Faza II
Cultura ceramicii pictate, Faza II (Arad.prose:

Lazarovici drept grupul Pişcolt, deoarece cele mai reprezentative şi mai numeroase materiale au fost descoperite la Pişcolt şi nu la Ciumeşti (Lazarovici - Nemeti 1983, p. 36). Doina Ignat a propus denumirea de grupul Sântandrei -Oradea - Săcuieni - Vărzari, argumentându-şi propunerea prin existenţa unui grup Pişcolt la niveul epocii bronzului fapt care, potrivit autoarei, ar putea crea confuzie. (Virag, Cristian)

Grupul Pişcolt se încadrează cronologic la nivel Vinca A2/ A3 - .B, contemporan cu grupele Cluj - Cheile Turzii - Lumea Nouă (Maxim 1999, p. 69; Lazarovici - Nemeti 1983, p. 23).

Ceramica liniara timpurie (Neamț County,.node: Ceramica liniara timpurie (Neamț County, 5499 BC–4999 BC)
Ceramica liniara timpurie (Neamț County,.label: Ceramica liniara timpurie
Ceramica liniara timpurie (Neamț County,.prose:
[Estul Transilvaniei, Moldova, 5499 BC–4999 BC] Ceramica liniara timpurie. Spatial coverage: Bacău County, Brașov County, Covasna County, Galați County, Harghita County, Iași County, Neamț County, Vaslui County. Ursulescu, N. 2001 (2), p.144-147. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

The earliest Linear Pottery farmers reached the hills of eastern Romania, bringing wheat, barley, cattle, longhouses and pots incised with running linear designs. Their arrival marks the point at which agriculture displaced foraging across this region, and the settlements they founded became the seedbed for the great painted-pottery cultures that followed.

Lumea Noua (Alba County, 5499 BC–4999 BC.label: Lumea Noua
Lumea Noua (Alba County, 5499 BC–4999 BC.prose:
[Zona circumscrisa muntilor Apuseni, 5499 BC–4999 BC] Lumea Noua. Spatial coverage: Alba County, Arad County, Bihor County, Cluj County, Hunedoara County. Ursulescu, N. 2001 (2), p.139-143. Complexul Cluj-Cheile Turzii-Lumea Nouă. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

A Neolithic settlement group in Transylvania known for its distinctive painted pottery, decorated in dark bands and geometric motifs on a pale ground. The style marks contact between the local Vinča-related communities and painted-ware traditions arriving from the south, and gave its name to a wider horizon of finds in the middle Mureș valley.

Boian (Olt County, 5299 BC–4499 BC).label: Boian
Boian (Olt County, 5299 BC–4499 BC).prose:
[Estul Olteniei, Muntenia, Sud-estul Transilvaniei,Sudul Moldovei, Vestul Dobrogei, 5299 BC–4499 BC] Boian. Farming communities of the lower Danube plain who lived in clustered villages of rectangular houses, some of them building up into low tells over generations. Their pottery is distinctive: dark burnished vessels with deeply excised meanders and spirals filled with white paste. Out of these communities grew the Gumelnița world, with its copper metallurgy, gold ornaments and famous clay figurines.

Bolintineanu (Ilfov County, 5299 BC–4499.label: Bolintineanu
Bolintineanu (Ilfov County, 5299 BC–4499.prose:
[centrul, sudul, estul Munteniei si Sudul Moldovei., 5299 BC–4499 BC] Bolintineanu. Spatial coverage: Argeș County, Brașov County, Brăila County, Bucharest, Buzău County, Covasna County, Călărași County, Dâmbovița County. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

The earliest stage of the Boian world on the lower Danube plain, when small farming settlements of light huts and pits spread along the river terraces. Its pottery, decorated with fine incised bands and white-encrusted lines, marks the beginning of a ceramic tradition that would run for centuries in the region.

Giulesti (Argeș County, 5299 BC–4499 BC).label: Giulesti
Giulesti (Argeș County, 5299 BC–4499 BC).prose:
[Muntenia, Sud-estul Transilvaniei, Sudul Moldovei, 5299 BC–4499 BC] Giulesti. Spatial coverage: Argeș County, Brașov County, Brăila County, Bucharest, Buzău County, Covasna County, Călărași County, Dâmbovița County. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

A phase of the Boian culture in the lower Danube region, marked by incised and excised pottery filled with white paste and by small farming settlements of pit-houses and surface dwellings. Communities kept cattle, sheep and pigs and cultivated cereals, and their cemeteries are among the earliest well-documented burial grounds of the region's Neolithic.

Vidra (Giurgiu County, 5299 BC–4499 BC).label: Vidra
Vidra (Giurgiu County, 5299 BC–4499 BC).prose:
[sudul Munteniei, nordul Bulgariei, 5299 BC–4499 BC] Vidra. Spatial coverage: Bucharest, Călărași County, Giurgiu County, Ialomița County, Ilfov County, Teleorman County. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

A tell settlement on the plain south of Bucharest that gives its name to a developed phase of the Boian culture, when Neolithic communities of Muntenia began piling their villages into mounds of superimposed houses. Its pottery is distinctive for deeply excised and channelled decoration filled with white paste, and for the first regular use of graphite paint that would become the hallmark of the later Gumelnița culture.

Spanțov (Olt County, 4899 BC–4499 BC).label: Spanțov
Spanțov (Olt County, 4899 BC–4499 BC).prose:
[Estul Olteniei, Muntenia, Sud-estul Transilvaniei,Sudul Moldovei, Vestul Dobrogei, 4899 BC–4499 BC] Spanțov. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

The final stage of the Boian culture on the lower Danube, when settlements grew larger and pottery decoration shifted toward the excised and graphite-painted styles that mark the transition into the Gumelnița world. Copper and Spondylus shell ornaments show communities plugged into long-distance exchange across the Balkans.

Dudești (Mehedinți County, 5399 BC–4999.label: Dudești
Dudești (Mehedinți County, 5399 BC–4999.prose:
[Muntenia, Oltenia, 5399 BC–4999 BC] Dudești. Spatial coverage: Argeș County, Brăila County, Bucharest, Buzău County, Călărași County, Dolj County, Dâmbovița County, Giurgiu County. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

A Neolithic culture of the Wallachian plain, marked by dark burnished pottery with incised and channelled decoration showing strong links to the Balkans and the Vinča world. Its farmers lived in small settlements of pit-dwellings and surface houses along river terraces. It fed directly into the later Boian culture, part of the sequence that culminated in the great tell communities of the lower Danube.

faza Malul Roșu (Dolj County, 5399 BC–49.node: faza Malul Roșu (Dolj County, 5399 BC–4999 BC)

faza Malul Roșu (Dolj County, 5399 BC–49.prose: [în zona de câmpie a Munteniei și Olteniei, aproximativ între râurile Dâmbovița în est și Desnățui în vest, 5399 BC–4999 BC] faza Malul Roșu. faza Fundeni (Buzău County, 5399 BC–4999.prose: [De la cursul superior al râului Călmățui din estul Munteniei și până în vestul Olteniei, 5399 BC–4999 BC] faza Fundeni. Hamangia incipienta (Tulcea County, 5199.label: Hamangia incipienta
Hamangia incipienta (Tulcea County, 5199.prose:
[Dobrogea, 5199 BC–4999 BC] Hamangia incipienta. Spatial coverage: Constanța County, Tulcea County. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

The formative stage of the Hamangia communities on the Dobrujan coast, when the first farming settlements appear with a distinctive burnished pottery and shell ornaments. The maritime and Danube contacts visible here have led many archaeologists to see the group as arriving from the Anatolian or Aegean side rather than developing locally.

faza Cernica (Călărași County, 5399 BC–4.label: faza Cernica
faza Cernica (Călărași County, 5399 BC–4.prose:
[Sudul Munteniei și Olteniei, între Râul Mosiștea și până aproape de Jiu, 5399 BC–4999 BC] faza Cernica. Spatial coverage: Bucharest, Călărași County, Dolj County, Giurgiu County, Gorj County, Ilfov County, Olt County, Teleorman County. Comșa 1987, 29. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

One of the earliest stages of the Boian culture on the lower Danube plain, named after the cemetery at Cernica outside Bucharest, where hundreds of inhumation graves were excavated. The burials, with their shell ornaments and stone tools, give an unusually full picture of a Neolithic community's size, health and social divisions at a time when farming was becoming firmly established in the region.

Vinca tarzie, faza C (Timiș County, 4999.node: Vinca tarzie, faza C (Timiș County, 4999 BC–4699 BC)
Vinca tarzie, faza C (Timiș County, 4999.label: Vinca tarzie, faza C
Vinca tarzie, faza C (Timiș County, 4999.prose:

Ursulescu, N. 2001 (2), p.148. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

The later stages of the Vinča world in the Banat, when settlements spread out from the old tells and copper objects became more common. Pottery grew more varied in decoration and figurine styles changed, while contacts stretched towards the Tisza and the Carpathian Basin. Within a few centuries the great Vinča settlements were abandoned, a break that marks the end of the region's Neolithic order.

Vadastra (Dolj County, 4999 BC–4499 BC).label: Vadastra
Vadastra (Dolj County, 4999 BC–4499 BC).prose: [Sud-estul Olteniei, Vestul Munteniei, 4999 BC–4499 BC] Vadastra. Spatial coverage: Argeș County, Dolj County, Mehedinți County, Teleorman County. Also, it has two phases, but the creator did not specify the marks for the start and end dates for these two phases, called Vadastra I and Vadastra II. Hamangia (Tulcea County, 4999 BC–4499 BC.label: Hamangia
Hamangia (Tulcea County, 4999 BC–4499 BC.prose:
[Dobrogea, 4999 BC–4499 BC] Hamangia. Spatial coverage: Constanța County, Tulcea County. Farming and fishing communities on the Black Sea shore of the Dobruja, whose potters made elegant burnished ware and whose sculptors produced the most famous figurines of the European Neolithic — the seated, brooding pair known as the Thinker of Cernavodă and his companion. Their large flat cemeteries, with the dead laid out with shell ornaments and pots, offer a rare view of an entire prehistoric population. Contacts by sea and along the Danube tie them to Anatolia and the Aegean.

Medgidia (Constanța County, 4999 BC–4499.label: Medgidia
Medgidia (Constanța County, 4999 BC–4499.prose: [Constanța, 4999 BC–4499 BC] Medgidia. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

Golovita (Romania, 4999 BC–4499 BC).label: Golovita
Golovita (Romania, 4999 BC–4499 BC).prose: [Romania, 4999 BC–4499 BC] Golovita. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

Ceamurlia (Tulcea County, 4999 BC–4499 B.label: Ceamurlia
Ceamurlia (Tulcea County, 4999 BC–4499 B.prose:
[Tulcea , 4999 BC–4499 BC] Ceamurlia. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

Named after the Dobrujan settlement of Ceamurlia de Jos, this is an early stage of the Hamangia culture, whose farmers kept cattle and sheep on the Black Sea steppe fringe and buried their dead in flat cemeteries. Hamangia potters produced burnished wares decorated with stabbed and incised patterns, and its sculptors made the seated clay figures known as the Thinker and his companion, among the most reproduced images of Neolithic Europe.

Mangalia (Tulcea County, 4999 BC–4499 BC.label: Mangalia
Mangalia (Tulcea County, 4999 BC–4499 BC.prose: [Dobrogea, 4999 BC–4499 BC] Mangalia. Spatial coverage: Constanța County, Tulcea County. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

Romanesti-Tiszapolgar (Caraș-Severin Cou.prose: [Banat, Crisana si Transilvania, 4599 BC–3799 BC] Romanesti-Tiszapolgar. Bodrogkeresztur (Caraș-Severin County, 4.label: Bodrogkeresztur
Bodrogkeresztur (Caraș-Severin County, 4.prose:
[Campia Tisei, Banat, Crisana, 4499 BC–3999 BC] Bodrogkeresztur. A Copper Age culture of the Carpathian Basin whose smiths worked native copper on an unprecedented scale, hammering and casting the heavy shaft-hole axe-adzes found in graves and hoards across the region. Cemeteries lie apart from settlements, with bodies laid crouched on their side and accompanied by tall twin-handled 'milk jugs' and thin gold discs and pendants. The differences in grave wealth are among the earliest clear signs of ranked society in the region.

Gornesti (Mureș County, 4499 BC–3799 BC).label: Gornesti
Gornesti (Mureș County, 4499 BC–3799 BC).prose: [Centrul Transilvaniei, 4499 BC–3799 BC] Gornesti. Spatial coverage: Alba County, Mureș County, Sibiu County. Petrescu-Dambovita, M. 2001 (2), p.167. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

Cernavoda (Argeș County, 3999 BC–3499 BC.prose:
[Muntenia, Sudul Olteniei, sudul Moldovei, Dobrogea, 3999 BC–3499 BC] Cernavoda. Petrescu-Dambovita, M. 2001 (2),, p.168-169. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

A culture of the lower Danube that emerged as the great tell-dwelling societies of Copper Age southeastern Europe collapsed. Its coarse shell-tempered pots, hilltop settlements and heavy reliance on herding — including horses — contrast sharply with what came before, and many archaeologists read it as evidence of steppe peoples pressing into the Balkans, a key episode in debates over Indo-European origins.

Cernavoda I (Tulcea County, 4099 BC–3799.label: Cernavoda I
Cernavoda I (Tulcea County, 4099 BC–3799.prose:
[Dobrogea, Nord-Estul Munteniei, Sudul Moldovei, 4099 BC–3799 BC] Cernavoda I. Spatial coverage: Brăila County, Buzău County, Constanța County, Galați County, Ialomița County, Tulcea County, Vrancea County. Petrescu-Dȋmboviţa, M  2001 (2), p.168-169; Vulpe, Al. 2001 (5), p. 224. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

The phase that directly follows the disappearance of the Gumelnița tell villages, with their painted pottery and copper wealth, along the lower Danube and Black Sea coast. Settlements shift to defensible spots, pottery becomes plain and shell-tempered, and animal bone assemblages show a swing towards mobile stock-keeping — the archaeological face of a major social rupture.

Cernavoda III (Tulcea County, 3899 BC–35.label: Cernavoda III
Cernavoda III (Tulcea County, 3899 BC–35.prose:
[Dobrogea, Muntenia, Oltenia, Transilvania , 3899 BC–3599 BC] Cernavoda III. Spatial coverage: Alba County, Argeș County, Bistrița-Năsăud County, Brașov County, Brăila County, Bucharest, Buzău County, Cluj County. Petrescu-Dȋmboviţa, M  2001 (2)  p.168-169; Vulpe, Al. 2001 (5), p. 224. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

Better understood as one end of the Cernavodă III–Boleráz horizon, a pottery style that stretched from the lower Danube up into the Carpathian Basin and Central Europe. This wide, thin spread of shared shapes and decoration signals long-distance contact along the river corridor, and it feeds directly into the Baden culture.

Cernavoda II (Tulcea County, 3799 BC–349.label: Cernavoda II
Cernavoda II (Tulcea County, 3799 BC–349.prose:
[Dobrogea, Sudul Moldovei, 3799 BC–3499 BC] Cernavoda II. Spatial coverage: Bucharest, Constanța County, Călărași County, Giurgiu County, Ialomița County, Ilfov County, Teleorman County, Tulcea County. Petrescu-Dȋmboviţa, M  2001 (2)  p.168-169; Vulpe, Al. 2001 (5), p. 224. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

A late stage of the lower Danube sequence, poorly represented in settlements and known largely from pottery, when the region lay between the steppe world to the east and the Baden cultures of the Carpathian Basin. It falls in the run-up to the Bronze Age, when metal, wheeled transport and barrow burial were beginning to reshape the region.

Cucuteni-Ariusd-Tripolie (Bacău County,.label: Cucuteni-Ariusd-Tripolie
Cucuteni-Ariusd-Tripolie (Bacău County,.prose:
[Moldova , 3699 BC–2999 BC] Cucuteni-Ariusd-Tripolie. Spatial coverage: Bacău County, Galați County, Iași County, Neamț County, Vaslui County, Vrancea County. Faza Culturala: Cucuteni C. Vulpe Al., 2001 (I), p.  225-228. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

The eastern Carpathian and Dniester branches of one great painted-pottery world, with Ariușd marking its Transylvanian wing. Its people lived in planned villages of substantial clay-plastered houses, farmed and herded, worked copper, and produced ceramics of a quality unmatched in contemporary Europe. Its dissolution in the later fourth millennium coincides with the spread of steppe pastoralist influence into the region.

Coțofeni (Caraș-Severin County, 3699 BC–.label: Coțofeni
Coțofeni (Caraș-Severin County, 3699 BC–.prose:
[Banat, Transilvania, Oltenia, Vestul Munteniei, 3699 BC–2699 BC] Coțofeni. Spatial coverage: Alba County, Argeș County, Bistrița-Năsăud County, Brașov County, Caraș-Severin County, Cluj County, Covasna County, Dolj County. Faza Culturala: are trei faze. Bloc Cultural: Blocul cultural Baden-Coțofeni. Vulpe, Al. 2001 (1), p. 227-232; Vulpe Al. 2020, p. 65-68; Ciugudea, H., 2000, p. 15; Pătroi.C, 2019, p. 11-14; Motzoi-Chicideanu, I., 2011, p. 55-56. Sunt multe păreri contrare în ceea ce privește încadrarea culturii Coțofeni într-o epocă preistorică sau alta. Pentru Alexandru Vulpe cultura Coțofeni a reprezentat începutul epocii bronzului în spațiul carpato-danubian (Vulpe Al. 2001, Vulpe Al., 2020, p. 65-72), teoria acestuia fiind împărtășită ulterior și de alții. O altă teorie adoptată de arheologii români este aceea că primele două faze ale culturii Coțofeni aparțin eneoliticului iar ultima fază reprezintă începutul epocii bronzului, trecere determinată de contactele dintre comunitățile Coțofeni și cele aparținând culturilor Glina și Yamnaia. Alte păreri definesc intervalul cronologic în care sunt situate comunitățile Coțofeni drept „perioada de tranziție de la eneolitic la epoca bronzului” (Tuțulescu I. 2016, p.139-141). În fine, alte teorii plasează comunitățile Coțofeni în eneoliticul târziu sau neo-eneolitic (Ciugudean H., 2000, p. 15; Pătroi N, 2019 p. 11). Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

A late Copper Age to earliest Bronze Age culture of the southwestern Carpathians and Danube valley, known for hundreds of small, often defensively placed hilltop and cave settlements and for pottery covered in dense incised and stabbed ornament. The shift to upland sites and a stock-raising economy reflects the wider transformation of the Balkans after the collapse of the great tell-building farming societies.

Baden (Bihor County, 3699 BC–2999 BC).label: Baden
Baden (Bihor County, 3699 BC–2999 BC).prose:
[Campia Tisei, Crisana, nord-vestul Banatului, 3699 BC–2999 BC] Baden. Spatial coverage: Alba County, Arad County, Bihor County, Cluj County, Hunedoara County, Sălaj County, Timiș County. Bloc Cultural: Baden-Coțofeni. Vulpe, Al. 2001 (2),  p. 227-231. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

A Late Copper Age horizon spread across the Carpathian Basin and beyond, marked by channelled dark pottery, jugs and dippers, and cemeteries with both inhumation and cremation. Its people relied heavily on cattle, and its sites yield some of Europe's earliest evidence for wheeled vehicles and paired-ox traction, including clay wagon models and ox burials. The shift towards mobile stock-keeping and long-distance contacts foreshadows the Bronze Age societies that followed.

Cultura Amforelor Sferice (Iași County,.node: Cultura Amforelor Sferice (Iași County, 3499 BC–2399 BC)
Cultura Amforelor Sferice (Iași County,.label: Cultura Amforelor Sferice
Cultura Amforelor Sferice (Iași County,.prose:
[Nordul și Centrul Moldovei, concentrare mai mare în zona Câmpiei Siretului, 3499 BC–2399 BC] Cultura Amforelor Sferice. Spatial coverage: Bacău County, Botoșani County, Iași County, Neamț County, Vaslui County. Mihăilescu-Bîrliba, V.,Szmyt,  M., 2003, p. 82-112; Motzoi-Chicideanu I. 2011 p. 213-219. Cultura Amforelor Globulare ocupa un vas spațiu care se întindea din din Schleswig-Hollstein, cuprinzând zona de litoral a Mării Baltice din Brandenburg, de acolo în Mecklenburg, Vorpommern  și regiunea Elba mijlocie-Saale, apoi în cea mai mare parte a Poloniei inclusiv, din nou, litoralul baltic, pentru a pătrunde   apoi dinspre Podolia și Volynia către est până  la cursul mijlociu al Niprului. Urmele acestei culturi sunt datate între 3500 a. Chr și 2400 a. Chr. (I Motzoi-Chicideanu). Arheologii români au identificat un subgrup din cadrul acestei culturi în Câmpia Moldovei (V. Mihăilescu-Bîrliba, M. Smyzt 2003). Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

Named for the round, richly decorated pots buried with its dead, this was a mobile herding society spread across the plains between the Elbe and the Dniester. Its people built stone-slab graves and sacrificed cattle alongside human burials, and their expansion east brought them into contact with the steppe world on the eve of the Corded Ware and Yamnaya migrations that reshaped Europe's population.

Epoca antică (Constanța County, 649 BC–A.label: Epoca antică
Epoca antică (Constanța County, 649 BC–A.prose:
[Coasta de Vest a Mării Negre (Dobrogea), 649 BC–AD 620] Epoca antică. Spatial coverage: Constanța County, Tulcea County. Pana la cucerirea romana a Daciei doar Dobrogea o consideram ca fiind inclusa in epoca antica cand teritoriile nord-dunarene se afla in plina epoca a fierului. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

Greek colonists from Miletus and Megara founded Histria, Tomis and Callatis on this coast, trading wine, oil and pottery inland to the Getae for grain and slaves. Rome absorbed the region as part of Moesia, exiled the poet Ovid to Tomis, and built the roads, forts and monuments that culminated in the Tropaeum Traiani; the cities survived as Byzantine strongholds until Avar and Slav attacks broke them in the early seventh century.

Epoca moderna (Romania, AD 1821–AD 1919).label: Epoca moderna
Epoca moderna (Romania, AD 1821–AD 1919).prose:
[Romania, AD 1821–AD 1919] Epoca moderna. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

Tudor Vladimirescu's 1821 uprising opened a century in which the Romanian principalities moved from Ottoman suzerainty to an independent kingdom. The union of Moldavia and Wallachia in 1859, the reforms of Alexandru Ioan Cuza, independence won on the battlefield in 1877 and the entry of a German dynasty transformed a peasant society into a modernising state with railways, universities and a French-facing elite. It closed with the union of 1918 and the creation of Greater Romania.

Epoca contemporana (Romania, AD 1919–AD.label: Epoca contemporana
Epoca contemporana (Romania, AD 1919–AD.prose:
[Romania, AD 1919–AD 2024] Epoca contemporana. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

Romania emerged from the First World War roughly doubled in size, uniting Transylvania, Bessarabia and Bukovina with the Old Kingdom. What followed was a turbulent century: interwar cultural flowering and political extremism, territorial losses and dictatorship in the Second World War, four decades of communist rule culminating in Ceaușescu's execution in 1989, and then a halting transition to democracy, NATO and the European Union.

Dridu (Romania, AD 700–AD 1050).label: Dridu
Dridu (Romania, AD 700–AD 1050).prose:
[Romania, AD 700–AD 1050] Dridu. Madgearu, Al., 1997. Conform cu Tratatul de Istorie a Românilor, vol. III, Şt. Olteanu, R. Popa, M. Rusu, p. 97-102 cultura Dridu are faza principala intre secolele IX-XI si o rima faza de formare intre secolele VII-IX. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

An early medieval culture of the lower Danube plain, known from villages of sunken-floor huts, hand-made and wheel-made pottery with combed wavy decoration, and cremation then inhumation cemeteries. It represents the settled population living under Bulgar and later Byzantine influence after the Slavic settlement of the Balkans. Romanian and Bulgarian archaeologists have argued fiercely over whose ancestors made it, which is why the material is so intensively studied.

voievodatul Transilvaniei (Hunedoara Cou.label: voievodatul Transilvaniei
voievodatul Transilvaniei (Hunedoara Cou.prose:
[Transilvania, AD 1111–AD 1541] voievodatul Transilvaniei. Spatial coverage: Alba County, Arad County, Bihor County, Bistrița-Năsăud County, Brașov County, Caraș-Severin County, Cluj County, Covasna County. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

Transylvania was governed as a voivodeship within the Hungarian kingdom, its ruler appointed by the king and its politics shaped by the Hungarian nobility, the Székelys and the German-speaking Saxon towns. Fortified churches, mining settlements and stone castles spread across the region, along with defences against Tatar and later Ottoman raids. Hungary's collapse at Mohács ended the arrangement, and Transylvania emerged as a semi-independent principality between Habsburg and Ottoman power.

Țara românească (Gorj County, AD 1310–AD.label: Țara românească
Țara românească (Gorj County, AD 1310–AD.prose:
[ Muntenia and Oltenia, AD 1310–AD 1859] Țara românească. Spatial coverage: Argeș County, Brăila County, Bucharest, Buzău County, Călărași County, Dolj County, Dâmbovița County, Giurgiu County. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

Wallachia emerged as an independent principality when Basarab I threw off Hungarian overlordship, and it governed the plains between the Carpathians and the Danube for five centuries. Its princes, among them Mircea the Elder, Vlad the Impaler and Michael the Brave, manoeuvred between Hungary, Poland and the Ottomans, eventually paying tribute while keeping their own church, boyar assemblies and law. Union with Moldavia in 1859 created the modern Romanian state.

Dobrogea (Tulcea County, AD 1346–AD 1388.label: Dobrogea
Dobrogea (Tulcea County, AD 1346–AD 1388.prose:
[Dobrogea, AD 1346–AD 1388] Dobrogea. Spatial coverage: Constanța County, Tulcea County. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

The lands between the lower Danube and the Black Sea broke away from Bulgarian control under a line of local rulers, most notably Dobrotitsa, who gave the region its name. They played Genoa, Venice, Byzantium and Wallachia against one another, ran a fleet, and profited from the grain and fish trade of the Danube delta ports. Ottoman expansion swallowed the small state at the end of the century.

Moldova (Hunedoara County, AD 1352–AD 18.label: Moldova
Moldova (Hunedoara County, AD 1352–AD 18.prose:
[Muntenia, Oltenia, Transilvania, Moldova, AD 1352–AD 1859] Moldova. Spatial coverage: Alba County, Arad County, Argeș County, Bacău County, Bihor County, Bistrița-Năsăud County, Brașov County, Brăila County. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

The principality of Moldavia took shape east of the Carpathians in the mid-fourteenth century and reached its height under Stephen the Great, who held off Ottoman, Hungarian and Polish armies and founded the painted monasteries of Bukovina. From the sixteenth century it paid tribute to the Sultan while keeping its own princes, later Greek Phanariot appointees from Constantinople. Its union with Wallachia in 1859 created the state that became Romania.

principatul Transilvaniei (Cluj County,.label: principatul Transilvaniei
principatul Transilvaniei (Cluj County,.prose:
[Transilvania, AD 1541–AD 1821] principatul Transilvaniei. Spatial coverage: Alba County, Arad County, Bihor County, Bistrița-Năsăud County, Brașov County, Caraș-Severin County, Cluj County, Covasna County. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

After the Ottomans destroyed the medieval Hungarian kingdom, Transylvania survived as a self-governing principality paying tribute to the sultan while playing the Habsburgs off against him. Its diet, dominated by Hungarian nobles, Székelys and Saxons, issued the Edict of Turda in 1568 recognising several Protestant confessions alongside Catholicism, an unusually broad toleration for the age, while the Orthodox Romanian majority remained without political rights. Habsburg armies took control at the end of the seventeenth century, after which the principality kept its name and institutions but lost its independence.

Epoca greaca arhaica (Constanța County,.node: Epoca greaca arhaica (Constanța County, 649 BC–479 BC)
Epoca greaca arhaica (Constanța County,.label: Epoca greaca arhaica
Epoca greaca arhaica (Constanța County,.prose:
[Coasta de Vest a Mării Negre (Dobrogea), 649 BC–479 BC] Epoca greaca arhaica. Spatial coverage: Constanța County, Tulcea County. Avram, A. 2001, p. 538; Avram, A. 2010, p. 563; Iliescu, V. 1970, p. 91; Lungu, V. 2019, p. 123; Alexandrescu 1962, p. 69.(se suprapune in linii mari cu Hallstatt tarziu)                                                                                                                                                       În preajma momentului fondării Histriei, pe cea mai mare parte a teritoriului dobrogean înflorea civilizația Babadag (Alexandrescu, P. 1971, p. 44-45). În aceeași linie de idei, Alexandru Avram: În ajunul colonizării greceşti Dobrogea era locuită de purtătorii unei civilizaţii tipice pentru Hallstatt C şi definite, după aşezarea eponimă, drept cultura Babadag (faza a III-a) (Avram, A. 2010, p. 563). În urmă cu mai mult timp, Alexandru Avram vedea o relație directă între finalul culturii Babadag III și stabilirea primelor apoikia grecești în această regiune (Avram, A. 1991, p. 19-30, citat în Smaranda Andrews, 2010, p. 32). În 2010, același autor susține opusul („Cert este că dispariţia aşezărilor de tip Babadag nu are nimic a face cu fenomenul colonizării greceşti.” Avram, A. 2010, p. 565). Pe de altă parte, Petre Alexandrescu presupune că dizolvarea culturilor Babadag și Basarabi, pe parcursul secolului al VII-lea a. Chr., a fost determinată sub presiunea sciților veniți din stepele nord-pontice și din Nordul Caucazului (Alexandrescu, P. 1971, p. 45).
Se presupune că cel puţin de pe la sfârşitul secolului al VIII-lea, unii navigatori greci s-au aventurat în Marea Neagră, având loc astfel contacte precoloniale ale grecilor în Pont (Alexandrescu 1999, p. 1 și passim; Avram 2010, p. 562).Cu toate acestea, dincolo de chestiunea de a şti dacă grecii au frecventat sau nu Marea Neagră încă de pe la sfârşitul secolului al VIII-lea - în funcţie de creditul acordat, fie surselor literare, fie evidenţei arheologice - este cert că fondarea primelor aşezări durabile nu a avut loc decât începând de pe la mijlocul secolului al VII-iea (Avram 2010, p. 562). Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

Colonists from Miletus planted Histria on a lagoon of the Black Sea coast around 657 BC, followed by Tomis and, later, Dorian Callatis — the first cities on what is now Romanian soil. They came for grain, fish and slaves from the interior, and brought with them coinage, writing, temples and painted Ionian pottery. The encounter between these Greek towns and the Thracian and Scythian peoples of the hinterland shaped the region for the next thousand years.

Epoca greaca clasica (Constanța County,.node: Epoca greaca clasica (Constanța County, 479 BC–322 BC)
Epoca greaca clasica (Constanța County,.label: Epoca greaca clasica
Epoca greaca clasica (Constanța County,.prose:
[Coasta de Vest a Mării Negre (Dobrogea), 479 BC–322 BC] Epoca greaca clasica. Spatial coverage: Constanța County, Tulcea County. Epoca greaca clasica (se suprapune in linii mari cu inceputurile Latene). Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

The Black Sea colonies grew rich shipping grain and salt fish to the Aegean, minting their own silver and building stone temples to Apollo and Aphrodite. They negotiated constantly with Getic and Scythian rulers inland, sometimes paying tribute, sometimes trading, and were briefly drawn into Athenian naval politics. Excavations at Histria show a fortified Greek town with sacred precinct, houses and cemeteries that flourished throughout these centuries.

Epoca elenistică (Tulcea County, 322 BC–.label: Epoca elenistică
Epoca elenistică (Tulcea County, 322 BC–.prose:
[Coasta de Vest a Mării Negre (Dobrogea), 322 BC–27 BC] Epoca elenistică. Spatial coverage: Constanța County, Tulcea County. Ștefan, A. 1971, p. 29-44; Aricescu, A. 1977, p. 24; Nawotka, K. D,  1991, p. 79; Vulpe, Al. 2001, p. 645; Rădulescu, A. 2001, p. 657. În studiul său din 1971, Alexandru Suceveanu tratează subiectul general al anexării Dobrogei de către Romani (Suceveanu, A. 1971, p. 113). Mai târziu, în volumul din 1977 (Viața economică în Dobrogea Romană), Suceveanu discută separat problematica includerii în sfera de influență romană a fiecărui oraș grecesc vest-pontic în parte, considerând că după campania lui Lucullus (72 a. Chr.), orașele grecești din Dobrogea sunt anexate ca stipendiariae. Deși este de acord că după campania lui M. Licinius Crassus din anii 29-28 a. Chr. cetățile grecești intră într-o dependență definitivă față de imperiu, autorul consideră că scrisorile guvernatorilor dintre anii 46-68 p. Chr. sunt o dovadă a faptului că în această perioadă orașele grecești încă nu beneficiau de un foedus. Dupa Lambrino 1933, 287; Petre, A. 1971, p. 98 finalul epocii elenistice este dat de campania lui Lucullus din 72-71 a.Chr in urma careia cetatile grecesti de pe malul de vest al Pontului Euxin intra in subordinea Romei. Ștefan, A. 1971, p. 29-44 a fost combătută de Avram 1998. Rădulescu, A. 2010, p. 689; Avram, A. 1998, p. 115-129; Avram, A. 2001, p. 616; Avram, A. 2010, p. 642-644; Ruscu, L. 2013, p. 12 considera epoca elenistica se considera ca se incheie in 3/2 a.Chr. D. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

After Alexander's death his general Lysimachus took control of the Black Sea coast, and the Greek ports of the Danube mouth — Histria, Orgame, Aegyssus — were drawn into the wider Hellenistic world of Macedonian kings, mercenaries and long-distance trade. Local Getic chieftains grew powerful enough to extract tribute from the cities, and Scythian rulers minted their own coins in the region. Wine amphorae from Rhodes, Thasos and Sinope found in the delta show just how far these small towns reached.

Epoca Romană (Romania, AD 46–AD 620).label: Epoca Romană
Epoca Romană (Romania, AD 46–AD 620).prose:
[Romania, AD 46–AD 620] Epoca Romană. Provinciile romane Moesia, Moesia Inferior si Scythia. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

Trajan's two wars destroyed the Dacian kingdom and turned it into a province settled with colonists from across the empire, whose Latin speech is the ancestor of Romanian. Gold from the Apuseni mines, salt, roads, forts and cities such as Ulpia Traiana Sarmizegetusa and Apulum made Dacia prosperous, though its exposed position beyond the Danube led Rome to abandon it after some 165 years.

Chilia Militari (Teleorman County, AD 11.label: Chilia Militari
Chilia Militari (Teleorman County, AD 11.prose:
[Muntenia centrala si de vest, AD 118–AD 275] Chilia Militari. Spatial coverage: Argeș County, Bucharest, Dâmbovița County, Giurgiu County, Ilfov County, Prahova County, Teleorman County. Bichir, Gh., 1974, p. 28-29; Ionita, I 2001, p. 404-422; Zahariade, M., Lichiardopol, D., 2006, p. 1; Macrea, M., 1968, p. 192. Data de început bazată pe descoperirea ultimelor monede de la Drajna și Mălăiești. Intervalul cand romanii s--au retras din castrele de la Targsor, Drajna și Mălăiești este in intervalul 117-119. Data de final este considerata a doua jumatate a secoluli al III-lea p.Chr. Am considerat necesara sa impingem aceasta data inspre finalul acestui secol daca nu chiar post 320 p.Chr. deoarece extinderea purtatorilor culturii Santana de Mures-Cerneahov  In Muntenia trebuie sa se fi produs dupa extinderea acestei culturi in Moldova. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

An archaeological grouping in the plains of Wallachia, north of the Roman Danube frontier, known from settlements and cemeteries of communities usually identified as free Dacians. Their wheel-made pottery, brooches and coins show constant trade and cultural exchange with the neighbouring Roman province, illustrating how porous the imperial border really was.

Poienesti-Vartescoi (Bacău County, AD 10.label: Poienesti-Vartescoi
Poienesti-Vartescoi (Bacău County, AD 10.prose: [Moldova Centrală, AD 106–AD 320] Poienesti-Vartescoi. Spatial coverage: Bacău County, Vaslui County. Bichir, Gh. 1974, p. 26; Ioniță, I., 1982, p. 14. Dupa Gh Bichir aceasta este data de început pentru Moldova Centrală. Arheologic se constată că în timpul celui de-al doilea război dacic (105—106), aşezările La Tène din Moldova au fost distruse (Bîtca Doamnei, Piatra Şoimului (Calu). Răcătău, Brad, Poiana-Dulceşti (La Broşteanu) etc.). Aşezarea din punctul "Broşteanu" încetează în pragul sec. al II-lea (anii 105—106), iar primul nivel de locuire al aşezărilor de pe Silişte şi Varniţa, datat cu monede de bronz şi argint de la Traian (AR, anii 112—117). După 319 are loc o conviețuire între carpi și goți); Dupa Sanie, S., 1981, p. 19 inceputul acestei culturi este pe la 170 p.Chr. in Moldova de nord, după invazia costobocilor. In Bichir, Gh., 1973, p. 154. se considera ca gotii se aseaza in Moldova dupa 319 p.Chr.. Dupa Ignat, M. 1999, p. 136 anul de final este plasat prin 315 p.Chr. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

Santana de Mureș - Cerneahov (Cluj Count.node: Santana de Mureș - Cerneahov (Cluj County, AD 300–AD 425)
Santana de Mureș - Cerneahov (Cluj Count.label: Santana de Mureș - Cerneahov
Santana de Mureș - Cerneahov (Cluj Count.prose:
[Transilvania, Muntenia, Moldova, Ucraina de nord si centrala, AD 300–AD 425] Santana de Mureș - Cerneahov. Spatial coverage: Alba County, Argeș County, Bacău County, Bistrița-Năsăud County, Brașov County, Brăila County, Bucharest, Buzău County. Bichir, Gh., 1973, p. 154; Kazanski 1991, 11; Palade 1992, 206; Mitrea 2005, 138; Constantinescu 2007, 59;  Harhoiu 2008, 66;  Ioniță I. 2010, 484, 809; Stanciu I. 2010, 822-823; Kazanski 2015, 111-124; Lazarescu, V.A., Ciuperca, B., Anton, A.  2015, p. 223-227. Anul 300 pentru inceperea acestei culturi reprezinta o medie intre cei care pun inceputurile acesteia in a doua jumatate a secolului al III-lea si cei care sustin ca data de inceput prima jumatate a secolului al IV-lea. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

A material culture spread across a vast belt from Transylvania to the Dnieper, generally linked with the Goths and the mixed populations living alongside them beyond the Roman frontier. Its villages produced wheel-made grey tableware in quantity, used Roman coins and amphorae, and buried their dead in large flat cemeteries. Its disappearance in the late fourth and early fifth centuries tracks the arrival of the Huns and the migrations that followed.

Lăpuș (Satu Mare County, 1299 BC–1049 BC.label: Lăpuș
Lăpuș (Satu Mare County, 1299 BC–1049 BC.prose:
[Maramures si nordul Transilvaniei, 1299 BC–1049 BC] Lăpuș. Spatial coverage: Bistrița-Năsăud County, Cluj County, Maramureș County, Satu Mare County, Sălaj County. Laszlo, A. 2001, p. 300. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

A Late Bronze Age group of the northwestern Carpathians known chiefly from its cemetery of earthen burial mounds, where the cremated dead were placed with quantities of finely made, dark burnished pottery. Excavation of a large mound-covered structure interpreted as a cult building points to communities capable of organised, monumental effort. The group's channelled and knobbed pottery styles feed directly into the later Gáva tradition of the eastern Carpathian Basin.

Lăpuș I (Satu Mare County, 1299 BC–1099.node: Lăpuș I (Satu Mare County, 1299 BC–1099 BC)
Lăpuș I (Satu Mare County, 1299 BC–1099.label: Lăpuș I
Lăpuș I (Satu Mare County, 1299 BC–1099.prose:
[Maramures si nordul Transilvaniei, 1299 BC–1099 BC] Lăpuș I. Spatial coverage: Bistrița-Năsăud County, Cluj County, Maramureș County, Satu Mare County, Sălaj County. Laszlo, A. 2001, p. 300. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

The earlier phase of the mound cemetery, with cremation burials under tumuli accompanied by richly decorated dark pottery and bronze ornaments, set within the wider Carpathian tumulus burial world.

Lăpuș II (Satu Mare County, 1099 BC–1049.node: Lăpuș II (Satu Mare County, 1099 BC–1049 BC)
Lăpuș II (Satu Mare County, 1099 BC–1049.label: Lăpuș II
Lăpuș II (Satu Mare County, 1099 BC–1049.prose:
[Maramures si nordul Transilvaniei, 1099 BC–1049 BC] Lăpuș II. Spatial coverage: Bistrița-Năsăud County, Cluj County, Maramureș County, Satu Mare County, Sălaj County. Laszlo, A. 2001, p. 300. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

The later phase of the mound-burial tradition, when pottery shifts towards the channelled and knobbed styles that anticipate the Gáva ceramics of the following centuries, and monumental built structures appear beneath the mounds.

Igrita (Arad County, 1299 BC–1049 BC).label: Igrita
Igrita (Arad County, 1299 BC–1049 BC).prose:
[Crișana, 1299 BC–1049 BC] Igrita. Spatial coverage: Arad County, Bihor County. Laszlo, A. 2001, p. 300. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

A Late Bronze Age group of the Crișana region in north-western Romania, named after a cave used as a burial place. It is known chiefly from cremation deposits and fine dark pottery placed in caves and rock shelters rather than from large open settlements.

Cruceni (Romania, 1299 BC–1099 BC).label: Cruceni
Cruceni (Romania, 1299 BC–1099 BC).prose:
[Romania, 1299 BC–1099 BC] Cruceni. Laszlo, A. 2001,  p. 300. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

A late Bronze Age urnfield community of the Banat plain, known chiefly from cemeteries where the dead were cremated and their ashes placed in decorated pottery urns. It belongs with the Belegiš group of the middle Danube, part of the broad shift across central Europe from burial mounds to flat cremation cemeteries.

Cruceni I (Romania, 1299 BC–1199 BC).label: Cruceni I
Cruceni I (Romania, 1299 BC–1199 BC).prose:
[Romania, 1299 BC–1199 BC] Cruceni I. Laszlo, A. 2001,  p. 300. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

The earlier stage of the Banat urnfield group, marked by dark burnished urns with incised and encrusted ornament covering the cremated remains. Grave goods are modest, and the uniformity of the rite points to settled farming communities sharing burial customs with neighbours across the middle Danube.

Cruceni II (Romania, 1199 BC–1099 BC).label: Cruceni II
Cruceni II (Romania, 1199 BC–1099 BC).prose:
[Romania, 1199 BC–1099 BC] Cruceni II. Laszlo, A. 2001,  p. 300. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

The later stage of the Banat urnfield group, in which channelled and fluted decoration replaces the earlier incised and encrusted ornament on cremation urns. The change ties these cemeteries to the wider fluted-ware horizon that spread across the Carpathian Basin at the close of the Bronze Age.

Verbicioara (Mehedinți County, 1199 BC–1.label: Verbicioara
Verbicioara (Mehedinți County, 1199 BC–1.prose:
[Muntenia, Oltenia, 1199 BC–1099 BC] Verbicioara. Spatial coverage: Argeș County, Brăila County, Bucharest, Buzău County, Călărași County, Dolj County, Dâmbovița County, Giurgiu County. Laszlo, A. 2001,  p. 300. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

A Bronze Age culture of Oltenia and the Danube valley in south-western Romania, known chiefly from its settlements and its dark, highly burnished pottery decorated with incised spirals and meanders, often filled with white paste. Its people farmed and herded in small tell-like and open villages, and their bronze- and goldwork shows links running down the Danube to the Balkans and the Aegean world.

Radovanu (Teleorman County, 1199 BC–1099.label: Radovanu
Radovanu (Teleorman County, 1199 BC–1099.prose: [Muntenia de sud, 1199 BC–1099 BC] Radovanu. Coslogeni (Constanța County, 1299 BC–109.prose:
[Muntenia de est, Dobrogea, 1299 BC–1099 BC] Coslogeni. Spatial coverage: Brăila County, Buzău County, Constanța County, Călărași County, Ialomița County, Tulcea County. Laszlo, A. 2001, p. 300. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

A Late Bronze Age herding culture of the lower Danube and Dobrudja, part of the wider Noua-Sabatinovka-Coslogeni complex that stretched east across the steppe. Its most recognisable sites are the so-called ash mounds, low heaps of grey settlement debris packed with cattle and sheep bone, that mark seasonal camps of a heavily pastoral economy.

Medias (Cluj County, 1099 BC–799 BC).prose: [Transilvania, 1099 BC–799 BC] Medias. Bobda-Susani (Timiș County, 1099 BC–999.prose:
[Banat, 1099 BC–999 BC] Bobda-Susani. Spatial coverage: Caraș-Severin County, Timiș County. Laszlo, A. 2001, p. 300. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

A late Bronze Age horizon on the Banat plain, known above all from cremation cemeteries whose ashes were buried in urns beneath low mounds. The great tumulus at Susani covered a monumental timber-and-earth structure with a rich funeral pyre, hinting at a warrior elite able to command large-scale labour. Its metalwork and pottery link the region to the wider Urnfield world spreading across the middle Danube at the time.

Insula Banului (Bucharest, 999 BC–799 BC.prose: [Muntenia, Oltenia, 999 BC–799 BC] Insula Banului. Babadag (Tulcea County, 1049 BC–649 BC).prose:
[Dobrogea, 1049 BC–649 BC] Babadag. Spatial coverage: Constanța County, Tulcea County. Babadag I, Babadag II, Babadag III. Laszlo, A. 2001, p. 300. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

An Early Iron Age culture of the Dobruja and lower Danube, known from fortified hilltop settlements and thick refuse layers rather than rich graves. Its hallmark is dark burnished pottery decorated with channelling and, later, stamped concentric circles and spirals. The communities farmed and herded on the Black Sea steppe fringe and traded with Thracian and Aegean worlds before disruption around the time steppe horsemen appeared in the region.

Mezocsat (Bihor County, 899 BC–699 BC).label: Mezocsat
Mezocsat (Bihor County, 899 BC–699 BC).prose:
[Crisana, 899 BC–699 BC] Mezocsat. Spatial coverage: Arad County, Bihor County. Laszlo, A. 2001, p. 300. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

An Early Iron Age group of the eastern Carpathian Basin known mainly from its cemeteries, where inhumation burials replaced the cremation rite of the preceding Urnfield world. Graves contain horse harness, bronze and iron weapons and steppe-style ornaments, and the shift is usually read as evidence of eastern horse-riding populations, often linked to the Cimmerians, moving into the Tisza region. It marks the moment when steppe influence began reshaping the cultures of the middle Danube.

Kalaca (Timiș County, 999 BC–899 BC).label: Kalaca
Kalaca (Timiș County, 999 BC–899 BC).prose: [Banat, 999 BC–899 BC] Kalaca. Spatial coverage: Caraș-Severin County, Timiș County. Laszlo, A. 2001, p. 300. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

Gornea (Timiș County, 899 BC–799 BC).prose:
[Banat, 899 BC–799 BC] Gornea. Spatial coverage: Caraș-Severin County, Timiș County. Laszlo, A. 2001, p. 300. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

A settlement horizon of the Danube gorges in the Banat, associated with the Gornea–Kalakača group that marks the transition from the Late Bronze Age to the earliest Iron Age in the middle Danube. Its dark burnished pottery with fluted and channelled decoration replaced older Bronze Age styles and spread widely along the river, signalling the reorganisation of communities that preceded the Hallstatt world.

Teleac (Sălaj County, 1049 BC–799 BC).label: Teleac
Teleac (Sălaj County, 1049 BC–799 BC).prose:
[Transilvania, 1049 BC–799 BC] Teleac. Spatial coverage: Alba County, Bistrița-Năsăud County, Brașov County, Cluj County, Covasna County, Harghita County, Hunedoara County, Mureș County. Teleac I, Teleac II, Teleac III.  Laszlo, A. 2001, p. 300. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

Named after a vast fortified hilltop settlement in Transylvania, enclosed by earthen ramparts and ditches on a scale unmatched in the region. Belonging to the transition from the Late Bronze Age to the Early Iron Age, it shows large-scale communal labour, metalworking and the channelled black pottery of the Gáva tradition, and appears to have been destroyed by fire.

Hallstatt timpuriu cu ceramica canelata.node: Hallstatt timpuriu cu ceramica canelata (Mehedinți County, 999 BC–699 BC)
Hallstatt timpuriu cu ceramica canelata.label: Hallstatt timpuriu cu ceramica canelata
Hallstatt timpuriu cu ceramica canelata.prose:
[Muntenia, Oltenia, Moldova, 999 BC–699 BC] Hallstatt timpuriu cu ceramica canelata. Spatial coverage: Argeș County, Bacău County, Brăila County, Bucharest, Buzău County, Călărași County, Dolj County, Dâmbovița County. Laszlo, A. 2001, p. 300. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

The opening stage of the Iron Age along the lower Danube, recognised above all by its pottery: dark, highly burnished bowls and urns decorated with broad fluted grooves and bosses instead of paint. Cremation in urnfields was the normal burial rite, and bronze remained common while iron slowly spread. The uniformity of this channelled ware over a huge area from the Tisza to the Danube gorges points to shared workshops, tastes and exchange networks.

Stoicani (Bacău County, 799 BC–749 BC).prose: [Moldova centrala si de sud, Estul Munteniei, Dobrogea, 799 BC–749 BC] Stoicani. Soldanesti (Bacău County, 799 BC–699 BC).prose: [Moldova centrala si de sud, Estul Munteniei, 799 BC–699 BC] Soldanesti. Basarabi (Sălaj County, 799 BC–649 BC).prose:

Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

An Early Iron Age culture of the middle and lower Danube, instantly recognisable from its pottery: burnished dark surfaces covered with stamped and incised spirals, meanders and channelled fluting, the lines filled with white paste. Its remarkably uniform style spread across a wide swathe of the Balkans and Carpathian basin, marking a period of shared taste and exchange among the communities usually identified with the early Thracians.

Gulmenița (Argeș County, 4499 BC–3699 BC.label: Gulmenița
Gulmenița (Argeș County, 4499 BC–3699 BC.prose:
[Muntenia, Nord-estul Olteniei, Sudul Moldovei, Bugeac, Dobrogea, 4499 BC–3699 BC] Gulmenița. Farming communities of the lower Danube and its tributaries who lived on tells - mounds built up from generations of mud-brick houses on the same spot. They produced graphite-painted pottery, fired clay figurines and some of the earliest large-scale copper and gold work in Europe, part of the same world that produced the astonishingly rich Varna cemetery. The culture collapsed toward the end of the fourth millennium as settlements were abandoned across the region.

Sălcuța (Caraș-Severin County, 4499 BC–3.label: Sălcuța
Sălcuța (Caraș-Severin County, 4499 BC–3.prose:
[Estul Banatului, Oltenia, Vestul Munteniei, 4499 BC–3999 BC] Sălcuța. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

A Copper Age culture of the lower Danube in what is now Oltenia and neighbouring Serbia and Bulgaria, part of the wider Balkan world that produced Europe's earliest large-scale copper metallurgy. Its people lived in tell-like settlements, made dark burnished and graphite-painted pottery, and cast heavy copper hammer-axes. Its later phases coincide with the disruption and collapse of the old Balkan tell societies.

Petresti (Mureș County, 4999 BC–4499 BC).label: Petresti
Petresti (Mureș County, 4999 BC–4499 BC).prose:
[Centrul si sud-vestul Transilvaniei, Banat, 4999 BC–4499 BC] Petresti. Spatial coverage: Alba County, Caraș-Severin County, Hunedoara County, Mureș County, Sibiu County, Timiș County. Petrescu-Dambovita, M. 2001 (2), p.161-162. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

A Copper Age culture of the Transylvanian uplands, known above all for finely made pottery painted before firing in bold bichrome and trichrome designs, among the most accomplished ceramics of prehistoric southeastern Europe. Its communities lived in settled villages, farmed and herded, and worked the copper that was becoming widely available across the Balkans. It grew out of the Vinča tradition and stands alongside the better-known Cucuteni-Tripolye world to the east.

Cucuteni (Moldova, 4599 BC–3699 BC).label: Cucuteni
Cucuteni (Moldova, 4599 BC–3699 BC).prose:
[Moldova, Sud-estul Transilkvaniei, 4599 BC–3699 BC] Cucuteni. Spatial coverage: Bacău County, Brașov County, Covasna County, Galați County, Iași County, Moldova, Neamț County, Vaslui County. Cucuteni A. Cucuteni A-B. Cucuteni B. Cucuteni-Ariusd-Tripolie/Ariusd-Cucuteni-Tripolje. Petrescu-Dambovita, M. 2001 (2), p.162-166. Epoca de final poate sa fie pe la 3000 a.Chr. si intra in Epoca timpurie a bronzului. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

Farming communities of the forest-steppe famous for their painted pottery—spirals and bands in red, white and black on vessels of remarkable size and precision—and for clay figurines and house models. Villages could be very large, laid out in concentric rings of houses, and many were deliberately burned at intervals and rebuilt, a practice still argued over. Together with Trypillia to the east this was one of the densest concentrations of population in Neolithic Europe.

Schneckerberg (Covasna County, 2699 BC–2.label: Schneckerberg
Schneckerberg (Covasna County, 2699 BC–2.prose: [Sud-estul Transilvaniei, nord-estul Munteniei, 2699 BC–2399 BC] Schneckerberg. Glina (Argeș County, 2699 BC–2399 BC).prose:
[Muntenia, Oltenia, Sudul si sud-estul Transilvanieei, 2699 BC–2399 BC] Glina. An Early Bronze Age culture of the lower Danube and Wallachian plain, known for coarse handmade pottery with knobbed and fingertip-impressed decoration and for small settlements on terraces and hilltops. Its people herded cattle and sheep, buried some of their dead under low tumuli, and belonged to the wider network of communities through which metalwork and steppe influences spread into southeastern Europe.

Yamnaya (Neamț County, 3399 BC–2499 BC).label: Yamnaya
Yamnaya (Neamț County, 3399 BC–2499 BC).prose:
[Moldova, Muntenia, Dobrogea, Banat, Crișana, Câmpia de Vest, Depresiunea Transilvaniei, 3399 BC–2499 BC] Yamnaya. Spatial coverage: Alba County, Arad County, Argeș County, Bacău County, Bihor County, Brașov County, Brăila County, Bucharest. Gogâltan, F., 2015, p. 63; Frânculeasa, A., 2019, p. 129-168. Pentru spațiul cuprins între Banat, bazinul inferior al Mureșului, Crișana și valea Someșului Mic, Gogâltan datează structuri Yamna între 2800 - 2500 a. Chr. (Gogâltan 2015 p. 63). Cele mai timpurii urme Yamnaya datate C14 au fost descoperite la Galați (3400 cal BC)) și Baia Hamangia (3380-3010 cal BC) (A. Frânculeasa 2013, p. 43). Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

Pastoralists from the Pontic-Caspian steppe, known from the pit graves under low earth mounds that they scattered across the grasslands, the dead laid on their backs with knees raised and dusted with red ochre. Wagons, cattle and horses let them exploit open country that farmers had largely ignored, and burials in the lower Danube region mark their westward push. Ancient DNA has tied this expansion to a massive movement of steppe ancestry into Europe and to the spread of Indo-European languages.

grupul Gornea-Foeni (Timiș County, 2199.label: grupul Gornea-Foeni
grupul Gornea-Foeni (Timiș County, 2199.prose:
[Banat, 2199 BC–1949 BC] grupul Gornea-Foeni. Spatial coverage: Caraș-Severin County, Timiș County. Gogâltan, F., 2015, p. 63. Period definition from Institutul Național al Patrimoniului periodizare — Bogdan Șandric, 2023.

An Early Bronze Age community of the Banat plain and Danube gorges, known mainly from settlement pottery with channelled and incised decoration. Its sites document the local reworking of older Copper Age traditions as new metal-using networks spread up the Danube.

grupul Sănislău (Satu Mare County, 2899.node: grupul Sănislău (Satu Mare County, 2899 BC–2299 BC)
grupul Sănislău (Satu Mare County, 2899.label: grupul Sănislău
