Formativo temprano-medio (Tucumán, 350 B.label: Formativo temprano-medio
Formativo temprano-medio (Tucumán, 350 B.prose:
[Quebrada de Los Corrales, Tucumán, 350 BC–AD 750] Formativo temprano-medio. Period definition from Los geoespacios arqueológicos durante el Holoceno Superior en la Quebrada del río de Los Corrales (El Infiernillo, Tucumán, Argentina) — Caria Mario Alejandro, 2009.

Early village life in the valleys and eastern slopes of Tucumán, best known from the Tafí valley with its circular stone house compounds, terraced fields and carved stone menhirs set in ceremonial spaces. Households farmed maize and kept llamas, ground their food with stone mortars, and buried their dead in cists near the home. In the humid piedmont to the east, related communities produced the modelled funerary urns of the Candelaria tradition.
Formativo temprano-medio (Tucumán, 350 B.source: Los geoespacios arqueológicos durante el Holoceno Superior en la Quebrada del río de Los Corrales (El Infiernillo, Tucumán, Argentina)

Candelaria II (Tucumán, AD 200–AD 400).label: Candelaria II
Candelaria II (Tucumán, AD 200–AD 400).prose:
[Piedemonte Oriental - Tierras Bajas, Tucumán, AD 200–AD 400] Candelaria II. Period definition from Investigaciones Arqueológicas en el sector meridional de las Selvas Occidentales — Heredia Osvaldo R., 1974.

In the humid wooded eastern slopes of northwest Argentina, farming communities lived in dispersed hamlets and buried their dead in large ceramic urns. Their grey-black pottery, often modelled with human and animal faces, links them to neighbouring valley cultures and shows how maize agriculture and settled village life spread down from the highlands into the yungas forest.
Candelaria II (Tucumán, AD 200–AD 400).source: Investigaciones Arqueológicas en el sector meridional de las Selvas Occidentales

Candelaria III (Tucumán, AD 400–AD 700).label: Candelaria III
Candelaria III (Tucumán, AD 400–AD 700).prose:
[Piedemonte Oriental - Tierras Bajas, Tucumán, AD 400–AD 700] Candelaria III. Period definition from Investigaciones Arqueológicas en el sector meridional de las Selvas Occidentales — Heredia Osvaldo R., 1974.

The later centuries of the urn-burial tradition in the forested eastern ranges, with continuing village agriculture and modelled grey pottery. Contact with the valleys to the west is visible in the ceramics, and the population that emerged from these communities occupied the region until the Inca and then the Spanish arrived.
Candelaria III (Tucumán, AD 400–AD 700).source: Investigaciones Arqueológicas en el sector meridional de las Selvas Occidentales

Candelaria IV (Tucumán, AD 700–AD 1000).label: Candelaria IV
Candelaria IV (Tucumán, AD 700–AD 1000).prose:
[Piedemonte Oriental - Tierras Bajas, Tucumán, AD 700–AD 1000] Candelaria IV. Period definition from Investigaciones Arqueológicas en el sector meridional de las Selvas Occidentales — Heredia Osvaldo R., 1974.

The final stretch of the Candelaria ceramic tradition in the wooded eastern foothills of the Andes, made by farming communities who grew maize, kept llamas and lived in scattered hamlets. They are best known for their dark burnished pottery and modelled human faces and figures, including large burial urns used for the dead. Their world was eventually absorbed into the denser, more fortified settlement patterns of the late pre-Inca centuries.
Candelaria IV (Tucumán, AD 700–AD 1000).source: Investigaciones Arqueológicas en el sector meridional de las Selvas Occidentales

Formativo (Tucumán, 550 BC–AD 750).prose: [Piedemonte Oriental - Tierras Bajas, Tucumán, 550 BC–AD 750] Formativo. Desarrollos Regionales (Tucumán, AD 750–.label: Desarrollos Regionales
Desarrollos Regionales (Tucumán, AD 750–.prose:
[Piedemonte Oriental - Tierras Bajas, Tucumán, AD 750–AD 1500] Desarrollos Regionales. Period definition from Geoarqueología del sector septentrional de las tierras bajas de la provincia de Tucumán (Argentina): patrones en el uso del espacio durante la época prehispánica — Caria Mario Alejandro, 2019-05-30.

After the Tiwanaku-influenced horizon faded, the valleys and highlands of northwest Argentina broke into a mosaic of local polities, best known through the Santa María and related groups. Communities clustered in dense, walled hilltop settlements — pukaras — with terraced fields below, buried their dead in painted urns, and worked copper and bronze. Warfare and competition between chiefdoms shaped the landscape until Inca armies absorbed the region in the late fifteenth century.
Desarrollos Regionales (Tucumán, AD 750–.source: Geoarqueología del sector septentrional de las tierras bajas de la provincia de Tucumán (Argentina): patrones en el uso del espacio durante la época prehispánica

Estilo Candelaria (Tucumán, 999 BC–AD 10.label: Estilo Candelaria
Estilo Candelaria (Tucumán, 999 BC–AD 10.prose:
[Piedemonte Oriental - Tierras Bajas, Tucumán, 999 BC–AD 1000] Estilo Candelaria. Period definition from Vida y muerte de los instrumentos musicales prehispánicos de las tierras bajas del Noroeste Argentino — Caria Mario Alejandro, 2021-07-21.

The Candelaria peoples farmed the humid eastern slopes and valleys below the Andes, growing maize in forest clearings and living in scattered hamlets rather than towns. They are best known for their pottery: grey and blackish vessels with modelled human faces and animal forms, and large urns in which the dead were buried in a crouched position. Their material culture links the highland Andean world with the tropical lowlands to the east.
Estilo Candelaria (Tucumán, 999 BC–AD 10.source: Vida y muerte de los instrumentos musicales prehispánicos de las tierras bajas del Noroeste Argentino

2° milenio d.C. (Tucumán, AD 1001–AD 200.label: 2° milenio d.C.
2° milenio d.C. (Tucumán, AD 1001–AD 200.prose:
[Piedemonte Oriental - Tierras Bajas, Tucumán, AD 1001–AD 2000] 2° milenio d.C.. Period definition from La alimentación prehispánica en las tierras bajas de Tucumán (Argentina): una primera aproximación a su análisis — Caria Mario Alejandro , 2020-12-23.

In the valleys of northwestern Argentina, farming communities of the Santa María and related traditions built dense stone settlements, terraced fields and painted funerary urns before the Inca absorbed the region into Collasuyu in the late 1400s. Spanish colonisation from the 1550s brought encomiendas and the long Calchaquí wars, ending with the forced removal of whole populations in the 1660s. Later centuries saw Tucumán become a sugar-growing province and the site of Argentina's declaration of independence in 1816.
2° milenio d.C. (Tucumán, AD 1001–AD 200.source: La alimentación prehispánica en las tierras bajas de Tucumán (Argentina): una primera aproximación a su análisis

Período de expansión incaica-Inca Imperi.node: Período de expansión incaica-Inca Imperial (Santiago del Estero, AD 1475–AD 1532)
Período de expansión incaica-Inca Imperi.label: Período de expansión incaica-Inca Imperial
Período de expansión incaica-Inca Imperi.prose:
[Santiago del Estero, AD 1475–AD 1532] Período de expansión incaica-Inca Imperial. Period definition from Posibles influencias incaicas en Santiago del Estero — Gramajo de Martínez Moreno Amalia Josefina, 1982.

The Inca state absorbed the southern Andes into Collasuyu, its southeastern quarter, extending roads, way stations and administrative centres far beyond the Cuzco heartland. Local populations were counted, taxed in labour and sometimes resettled as mitmaqkuna colonists, and Cuzco-style pottery and architecture appear at provincial sites. In the eastern lowlands the imperial presence was thinner, an indirect frontier zone rather than a fully governed province — and it lasted barely two generations before the Spanish arrival.
Período de expansión incaica-Inca Imperi.source: Posibles influencias incaicas en Santiago del Estero

Late pottery-making and farming (Santiag.node: Late pottery-making and farming (Santiago del Estero, AD 1150–AD 1550)
Late pottery-making and farming (Santiag.label: Late pottery-making and farming
Late pottery-making and farming (Santiag.prose: [Santiago del Estero, AD 1150–AD 1550] Late pottery-making and farming. Period definition from First Approach to Study the Presence of Domesticated Camelids (Lama glama) in the Chaco‐Santiago Region, a Marginal Zone of the South Central Andes — del Papa Luis Manuel , 2012-08-15. Farming communities of the Dulce and Salado floodplains grew maize, squash and beans on seasonally flooded land, living in villages built on low mounds above the water. They made the distinctive incised and painted wares of the Sunchituyoj and Averías traditions, including modelled zoomorphic vessels and urn burials. The sequence ends with the arrival of Spanish expeditions, who found dense riverine populations here before disease and encomienda broke them up.

Formativo Inferior (Salta, 599 BC–AD 400.label: Formativo Inferior
Formativo Inferior (Salta, 599 BC–AD 400.prose:
[Valles Calchaquíes Medios, Salta, 599 BC–AD 400] Formativo Inferior. Period definition from Sitios arqueológicos del Valle Calchaquí Medio (Departamentos de Molinos y San Carlos) — Raffino Rodolfo Adelio, 1983.

Settled agricultural life in the valleys and eastern piedmont of the Argentine Northwest, based on maize, quinoa and camelid herding. Communities lived in small dispersed hamlets with round stone-walled houses and cultivation plots, made incised and painted pottery, and worked copper and gold. Regional exchange networks carried pottery styles, obsidian and Amazonian and Pacific goods across the Andes.
Formativo Inferior (Salta, 599 BC–AD 400.source: Sitios arqueológicos del Valle Calchaquí Medio (Departamentos de Molinos y San Carlos)

Formativo Superior (Salta, AD 400–AD 900.label: Formativo Superior
Formativo Superior (Salta, AD 400–AD 900.prose:
[Valles Calchaquíes Medios, Salta, AD 400–AD 900] Formativo Superior. Period definition from Sitios arqueológicos del Valle Calchaquí Medio (Departamentos de Molinos y San Carlos) — Raffino Rodolfo Adelio, 1983.

The later stage of village farming society in the Argentine Northwest, when settlements grew larger and more clustered, agricultural terraces and irrigation spread, and craft production in ceramics and metal became more specialised. Distinct regional pottery styles emerged, and differences in burial goods hint at growing inequality. These communities are the direct ancestors of the fortified towns and chiefdoms of the following Regional Development period.
Formativo Superior (Salta, AD 400–AD 900.source: Sitios arqueológicos del Valle Calchaquí Medio (Departamentos de Molinos y San Carlos)

Período de Desarrollos Regionales (Salta.label: Período de Desarrollos Regionales
Período de Desarrollos Regionales (Salta.prose:
[Valles Calchaquíes Medios, Salta, 899 BC–AD 1470] Período de Desarrollos Regionales. Period definition from Sitios arqueológicos del Valle Calchaquí Medio (Departamentos de Molinos y San Carlos) — Raffino Rodolfo Adelio, 1983.

Sharply distinct local traditions emerged across the valleys, each with its own pottery, architecture and territory. Settlements grew into agglomerated stone towns with terraced fields and defensive walls, and the dead were interred with painted urns and bronze goods. Interpretation of the period turns on whether these were warring chiefdoms or looser village confederations.
Período de Desarrollos Regionales (Salta.source: Sitios arqueológicos del Valle Calchaquí Medio (Departamentos de Molinos y San Carlos)

Período Inka (Salta, AD 1470–AD 1535).label: Período Inka
Período Inka (Salta, AD 1470–AD 1535).prose:
[Valles Calchaquíes Medios, Salta, AD 1470–AD 1535] Período Inka. Period definition from Sitios arqueológicos del Valle Calchaquí Medio (Departamentos de Molinos y San Carlos) — Raffino Rodolfo Adelio, 1983.

Salta's valleys and high puna became part of Collasuyu, crossed by the Qhapaq Ñan and dotted with tambos, agricultural terraces and administrative sites. The most spectacular legacy is high-altitude ceremonial architecture, including the summit sanctuaries where children were sacrificed and preserved by the cold. Local communities supplied labour and were sometimes uprooted and resettled to serve the state.
Período Inka (Salta, AD 1470–AD 1535).source: Sitios arqueológicos del Valle Calchaquí Medio (Departamentos de Molinos y San Carlos)

Período Hispano-Indigena (Salta, AD 1535.label: Período Hispano-Indigena
Período Hispano-Indigena (Salta, AD 1535.prose:
[Valles Calchaquíes Medios, Salta, AD 1535–AD 1660] Período Hispano-Indigena. Period definition from Sitios arqueológicos del Valle Calchaquí Medio (Departamentos de Molinos y San Carlos) — Raffino Rodolfo Adelio, 1983.

Spanish entradas into the valleys of the Northwest collided with Diaguita-Calchaquí communities, producing a century of encomienda demands, refounded towns and repeated uprisings. Archaeologically it shows as indigenous villages with European glass beads, iron tools, horse and cattle bone and majolica alongside traditional urn burials and painted wares. It ends with the crushing of the last Calchaquí resistance and the forced relocation of whole communities far from their homelands.
Período Hispano-Indigena (Salta, AD 1535.source: Sitios arqueológicos del Valle Calchaquí Medio (Departamentos de Molinos y San Carlos)

Período Medio (Salta, AD 600–AD 1000).label: Período Medio
Período Medio (Salta, AD 600–AD 1000).prose:
[Valles Calchaquíes Medios, Salta, AD 600–AD 1000] Período Medio. Period definition from Nuevos aportes a la prehistoria del valle Calchaquí. Noroeste argentino — Pollard Gordon, 1983.

The centuries when the Aguada tradition dominated the Northwest, famous for its dark polished ceramics engraved with feline, serpent and sacrificer imagery. Metallurgy flourished, with cast bronze plaques and axes, and shared iconography suggests ritual specialists and networks of exchange linking widely separated valleys. Contacts with the Bolivian altiplano and Tiwanaku world brought hallucinogenic snuff kits and camelid caravan goods.
Período Medio (Salta, AD 600–AD 1000).source: Nuevos aportes a la prehistoria del valle Calchaquí. Noroeste argentino

Formativo de las sociedades agrícolas en.label: Formativo de las sociedades agrícolas en el Sur del Valle Calchaquí
Formativo de las sociedades agrícolas en.prose:
[Valles Calchaquíes Sur, Salta, 899 BC–AD 1000] Formativo de las sociedades agrícolas en el Sur del Valle Calchaquí. Period definition from El Alisar y El Divisadero. Dos Sitios Arqueológicos con Pinturas Rupestres en Cafayate, Salta. — Ledesma Rossana Elizabeth, 2004.

Agricultural communities settled the southern Calchaquí valley, farming maize and squash on terraced and irrigated plots and pasturing llama herds on the surrounding slopes. Their villages of stone-walled compounds, with grinding stones, storage cists and painted pottery, show a way of life that lasted well over a millennium. Later in the sequence settlements grew and clustered, foreshadowing the dense fortified towns of the Calchaquí chiefdoms.

Período Formativo (Salta, AD 1–AD 1000).label: Período Formativo
Período Formativo (Salta, AD 1–AD 1000).prose:
[Valles Calchaquíes Sur, Salta, AD 1–AD 1000] Período Formativo. Period definition from La figura humana en el arte rupestre en el sur del valle Calchaquí (Salta, Argentina) — Ledesma Rossana , 2015.

Permanent farming villages spread through the valleys: houses and patios enclosed by stone walls, terraced fields, llama corrals and communal cemeteries. The Tafí tradition of this era left carved stone menhirs and stone-lined house compounds, while snuff trays, metal ornaments and exotic materials show ties reaching to the puna, the Pacific coast and the forested lowlands.
Período Formativo (Salta, AD 1–AD 1000).source: La figura humana en el arte rupestre en el sur del valle Calchaquí (Salta, Argentina)

Período de Desarrollos Regionales o Tard.node: Período de Desarrollos Regionales o Tardío (Salta, AD 900–AD 1400)
Período de Desarrollos Regionales o Tard.label: Período de Desarrollos Regionales o Tardío
Período de Desarrollos Regionales o Tard.prose:
[Valles Calchaquíes Medios, Salta, AD 900–AD 1400] Período de Desarrollos Regionales o Tardío. Period definition from El Valle Calchaquí Medio (Salta, Argentina) durante los siglos XV-XVII: aportes desde el registro arqueológico y las fuentes documentales — Castellanos María Cecilia, 2016-03.

Local polities in the Calchaquí and neighbouring valleys built agglomerated stone settlements, some heavily fortified, and farmed terraced slopes with irrigation. Each group developed its own ceramic style, and bronze ornaments and weapons became widespread. Population growth and visible defence works point to sustained competition before Inca rule imposed a new order.

Período Tardío o de Desarrollos Regional.prose:
[Valles Calchaquíes Medios, Salta, AD 900–AD 1500] Período Tardío o de Desarrollos Regionales e Inca. El caso de Tacuil, valle Calchaquí medio, Salta, Argentina. — Castellanos María Cecilia, 2020-12-28.

Centuries of independent valley polities, with terraced agriculture, nucleated settlements and defensive pukaras, followed by their absorption into the Inca empire. Local painted wares and urn burials continued while imperial roads, tambos and administrative sites were grafted onto the landscape. The sequence ends on the eve of European contact.

Período previo a la conquista inka (Salt.node: Período previo a la conquista inka (Salta, AD 1000–AD 1430)
Período previo a la conquista inka (Salt.label: Período previo a la conquista inka
Período previo a la conquista inka (Salt.prose:
[Valles Calchaquíes Sur, Salta, AD 1000–AD 1430] Período previo a la conquista inka. Period definition from Nuevos datos sobre la prehistoria local en la quebrada de Tolombón. Pcia. De Salta. Argentina — Williams Verónica Isabel, 2003.

Valley communities lived in large stone-built settlements, many of them perched on defensible heights with encircling walls, farming terraced slopes and herding llamas. Distinctive urn burials and painted funerary ceramics mark the period, and warfare between neighbouring groups appears to have been frequent. These independent polities retained strong local identities right up to their absorption by the Inca state.

[Valles Calchaquíes Sur, Salta, AD 1000–AD 1536] Período de Desarrollos Regionales e Inca. Period definition from El uso del espacio a nivel estatal en el sur del Tawantinsuyu — Williams Verónica Isabel, 2010.

Independent valley societies with their own ceramic styles and fortified settlements were drawn, in the final century, into the Inca empire. Imperial roads, tambos and mountaintop shrines were built across the region, and high-altitude ritual sites here have preserved some of the most remarkable Inca offerings known. The sequence closes with Spanish entry into the Calchaquí valleys.
Período de Desarrollos Regionales e Inca.source: El uso del espacio a nivel estatal en el sur del Tawantinsuyu

Período Medio (Salta, AD 1000–AD 1450).label: Período Medio
Período Medio (Salta, AD 1000–AD 1450).prose:
[Valles Calchaquíes Norte, Salta, AD 1000–AD 1450] Período Medio. Period definition from Experiencia de la muerte y la representación de las personas en las prácticas funerarias del valle Calchaquí Norte — Acuto Felix, 2011-06-01.

The centuries when the Aguada tradition dominated the Northwest, famous for its dark polished ceramics engraved with feline, serpent and sacrificer imagery. Metallurgy flourished, with cast bronze plaques and axes, and shared iconography suggests ritual specialists and networks of exchange linking widely separated valleys. Contacts with the Bolivian altiplano and Tiwanaku world brought hallucinogenic snuff kits and camelid caravan goods.
Período Medio (Salta, AD 1000–AD 1450).source: Experiencia de la muerte y la representación de las personas en las prácticas funerarias del valle Calchaquí Norte

Late Intermediate period (Salta, AD 1000.label: Late Intermediate period
Late Intermediate period (Salta, AD 1000.prose:
[Valles Calchaquíes Norte, Salta, AD 1000–AD 1450] Late Intermediate period. Period definition from Recognising strategies for conquered territories: a case study from the Inka North Calchaquí Valley — Acuto Felix Alejandro, 2012-12.

Following the collapse of Tiwanaku-linked influence, valley populations grew and reorganised into competing local chiefdoms, farming irrigated terraces and herding llamas. Settlements shifted onto defensible heights, and elaborately painted funerary urns for infants are among the most distinctive finds. The sequence ends with Inca conquest, which overlaid an imperial administration on these local polities.
Late Intermediate period (Salta, AD 1000.source: Recognising strategies for conquered territories: a case study from the Inka North Calchaquí Valley

Inka occupation (Salta, AD 1450–AD 1536).label: Inka occupation
Inka occupation (Salta, AD 1450–AD 1536).prose:
[Valles Calchaquíes Norte, Salta, AD 1450–AD 1536] Inka occupation. Period definition from Recognising strategies for conquered territories: a case study from the Inka North Calchaquí Valley — Acuto Felix Alejandro, 2012-12.

Inca administrators extended the royal road and a network of tambos and fortified centres through the Calchaquí and Lerma valleys, drawing local communities into imperial tribute and mining. Mountaintop sanctuaries, including some of the highest sacrificial sites known, mark the state's presence on the peaks. Spanish entradas found these arrangements still in place, and the valleys' peoples resisted them for well over a century.
Inka occupation (Salta, AD 1450–AD 1536).source: Recognising strategies for conquered territories: a case study from the Inka North Calchaquí Valley

Late Intermediate Period (Salta, AD 1250.label: Late Intermediate Period
Late Intermediate Period (Salta, AD 1250.prose:
[Valles Calchaquíes Norte, Salta, AD 1250–AD 1450] Late Intermediate Period. Period definition from Death, personhood, and relatedness in the South Andes a thousand years ago — Acuto Felix Alejandro, 2014-07-08.

With no overarching state, communities in the northwestern Andean valleys built dense hilltop settlements and defensive pukaras, a sign of chronic conflict over land and water. Santa María painted urns, irrigated terracing and llama caravan trade tie the valleys into a wide exchange network. Inca armies absorbed the whole region at the close of the period, imposing roads, garrisons and forced resettlement.
Late Intermediate Period (Salta, AD 1250.source: Death, personhood, and relatedness in the South Andes a thousand years ago

Período Tardío (Salta, AD 900–AD 1470).label: Período Tardío
Período Tardío (Salta, AD 900–AD 1470).prose:
[Valles Calchaquíes Norte, Salta, AD 900–AD 1470] Período Tardío. Period definition from El sitio Mariscal (SSalCac5): Investigaciones sobre la vida cotidiana en una aldea prehispánica del valle Calchaquí Norte — Kergaravat Marisa, 2014.

Following the end of the Middle Period, the Northwest fragmented into competing local polities with their own painted ceramics, cemeteries and territories. Agriculture intensified on terraces and irrigated land, populations concentrated in large villages, and fortified pukaras multiplied on ridges and hilltops. These chiefdoms were still expanding when the Inca arrived.
Período Tardío (Salta, AD 900–AD 1470).source: El sitio Mariscal (SSalCac5): Investigaciones sobre la vida cotidiana en una aldea prehispánica del valle Calchaquí Norte

Período Intermedio Tardío (Salta, AD 900.label: Período Intermedio Tardío
Período Intermedio Tardío (Salta, AD 900.prose:
[Valles Calchaquíes Norte, Salta, AD 900–AD 1460] Período Intermedio Tardío. Period definition from Las vasijas y su potencial como sujetos estabilizadores de seres incompletos: Prácticas mortuorias de infantes durante el período Tardío en el Valle Calchaquí Norte — Amuedo Claudia, 2015-06.

After the collapse of the Middle Period order, populations in the valleys built dense settlements, extensive terraced fields and irrigation systems, and increasingly clustered in defensible hilltop pukaras. Regional identities are visible in distinct painted pottery styles and in urn burials of infants beneath house floors. The rising evidence for warfare and territorial competition sets the stage for Inca conquest.

Período de contacto hispano-indígena (Sa.label: Período de contacto hispano-indígena
Período de contacto hispano-indígena (Sa.prose:
[Valles Calchaquíes Norte, Salta, AD 1535–AD 1664] Período de contacto hispano-indígena. Period definition from ¿Qué, cómo y quiénes comen a través de un ushnu? Historias de comensalidad en el ushnu de Guitián (Salta, Argentina) — Amuedo Claudia, 2020-12-19.

Spanish expeditions pushing down from Peru and across from Chile met the fortified valley communities of the northwest, and the encounter lasted more than a century. Encomienda labour demands, missionaries and epidemic disease reshaped indigenous life, while repeated uprisings — the Calchaquí wars — kept whole valleys outside colonial control until the 1660s, when the defeated populations were deported wholesale to distant settlements. Archaeologically the period shows up as mixed assemblages: European glass, glazed ware and iron alongside traditional pottery.
Período de contacto hispano-indígena (Sa.source: ¿Qué, cómo y quiénes comen a través de un ushnu? Historias de comensalidad en el ushnu de Guitián (Salta, Argentina)

Período Inka (Salta, AD 1430–AD 1535).label: Período Inka
Período Inka (Salta, AD 1430–AD 1535).prose:
[Valles Calchaquíes Norte, Salta, AD 1430–AD 1535] Período Inka. Period definition from Recrear el cosmos en la cocina: cocción y comensalidad en el sitio Guitián (Salta, Argentina) — Amuedo Claudia, 2022-08-06.

Salta's valleys and high puna became part of Collasuyu, crossed by the Qhapaq Ñan and dotted with tambos, agricultural terraces and administrative sites. The most spectacular legacy is high-altitude ceremonial architecture, including the summit sanctuaries where children were sacrificed and preserved by the cold. Local communities supplied labour and were sometimes uprooted and resettled to serve the state.
Período Inka (Salta, AD 1430–AD 1535).source: Recrear el cosmos en la cocina: cocción y comensalidad en el sitio Guitián (Salta, Argentina)

Período Formativo en el Valle Calchaquí.node: Período Formativo en el Valle Calchaquí Norte (Salta, 750 BC–AD 450)
Período Formativo en el Valle Calchaquí.label: Período Formativo en el Valle Calchaquí Norte
Período Formativo en el Valle Calchaquí.prose:
[Valles Calchaquíes Norte, Salta, 750 BC–AD 450] Período Formativo en el Valle Calchaquí Norte. Period definition from Primeros entierros y primeros cultivos en el Valle Calchaquí: Los inicios del Holoceno y del primer milenio en el sitio Puente del Diablo (SSalLap20) — Lema Verónica Soledad , 2022-05-19.

Farming settlements filled the northern Calchaquí valley, building stone-walled house compounds and vast fields bounded by rock alignments and terraces along the river terraces and alluvial fans. Residents cultivated maize, quinoa and beans, herded llamas and traded obsidian and other goods across the puna, creating the agrarian landscape that later towns would inherit.
Período Formativo en el Valle Calchaquí.source: Primeros entierros y primeros cultivos en el Valle Calchaquí: Los inicios del Holoceno y del primer milenio en el sitio Puente del Diablo (SSalLap20)

Formativo Temprano (Salta, 1550 BC–450 B.label: Formativo Temprano
Formativo Temprano (Salta, 1550 BC–450 B.prose:
[Valles Calchaquíes Norte, Salta, 1550 BC–450 BC] Formativo Temprano. Period definition from El espacio doméstico en las ocupaciones aldeanas del valle Calchaquí Norte (Salta, Argentina) — Rivolta María Clara, 2017.

The transition from mobile hunting and gathering to settled life in the valleys of the Argentine Northwest. People began cultivating maize, beans and quinoa, herding llamas, storing crops in pits and cists, and making the region's first pottery, while continuing to hunt guanaco and vicuña. Small, widely spaced hamlets of round houses replaced the earlier rock-shelter camps.
Formativo Temprano (Salta, 1550 BC–450 B.source: El espacio doméstico en las ocupaciones aldeanas del valle Calchaquí Norte (Salta, Argentina)

Desarrollos Regionales (Salta, AD 900–AD.label: Desarrollos Regionales
Desarrollos Regionales (Salta, AD 900–AD.prose:
[Valles Calchaquíes Norte, Salta, AD 900–AD 1480] Desarrollos Regionales. Period definition from Paisaje y Materialidad en el Formativo del Valle Calchaquí Norte — Rivolta María Clara, 2020-12-19.

After the Tiwanaku-influenced horizon faded, the valleys and highlands of northwest Argentina broke into a mosaic of local polities, best known through the Santa María and related groups. Communities clustered in dense, walled hilltop settlements — pukaras — with terraced fields below, buried their dead in painted urns, and worked copper and bronze. Warfare and competition between chiefdoms shaped the landscape until Inca armies absorbed the region in the late fifteenth century.
Desarrollos Regionales (Salta, AD 900–AD.source: Paisaje y Materialidad en el Formativo del Valle Calchaquí Norte

Ocupación incaica (Salta, AD 1480–AD 152.label: Ocupación incaica
Ocupación incaica (Salta, AD 1480–AD 152.prose:
[Valles Calchaquíes Norte, Salta, AD 1480–AD 1520] Ocupación incaica. Period definition from Paisaje y Materialidad en el Formativo del Valle Calchaquí Norte — Rivolta María Clara, 2020-12-19.

Inca armies extended Tawantinsuyu into the far south, incorporating the valleys and puna of the northwest Argentine Andes as part of Qollasuyu. The state built roads, waystations and administrative centres, resettled populations of mitmaqkuna, and pressed local labour into mining and farming. Mountaintop shrines from this drive include the frozen child sacrifices of Llullaillaco; the whole system lasted barely two generations before Spanish arrival.
Ocupación incaica (Salta, AD 1480–AD 152.source: Paisaje y Materialidad en el Formativo del Valle Calchaquí Norte

Late Period (Salta, AD 900–AD 1430).label: Late Period
Late Period (Salta, AD 900–AD 1430).prose:
[Valles Calchaquíes Norte, Salta, AD 900–AD 1430] Late Period. Period definition from Irrigation canals from the Calchaqui valley (province of Salta, Argentina) — Páez María Cecilia, 2019-10.

Egyptian kings ruled again from Sais after the Assyrian withdrawal, reviving Old Kingdom art and burial customs in a deliberate archaising style, while Greek and Carian mercenaries and traders settled in the Delta at Naukratis. Persian conquest in 525 BC made Egypt a satrapy, interrupted by brief native dynasties, until Alexander took the country in 332 BC. The period is where Egypt becomes fully entangled with the Mediterranean world that would later record its history.
Late Period (Salta, AD 900–AD 1430).source: Irrigation canals from the Calchaqui valley (province of Salta, Argentina)

Inca Period (Salta, AD 1430–AD 1530).label: Inca Period
Inca Period (Salta, AD 1430–AD 1530).prose:
[Valles Calchaquíes Norte, Salta, AD 1430–AD 1530] Inca Period. Period definition from Irrigation canals from the Calchaqui valley (province of Salta, Argentina) — Páez María Cecilia, 2019-10.

Cusco's armies incorporated the valleys of the Calchaquí and the Andean south into Qollasuyu, installing garrisons, administrative sites and roads linked to the great highland highway. Local communities kept their own pottery and burial customs while paying labour tribute and, in places, being moved wholesale as mitmaqkuna colonists. Mining and metalworking in the region were of particular interest to the state.
Inca Period (Salta, AD 1430–AD 1530).source: Irrigation canals from the Calchaqui valley (province of Salta, Argentina)

Formativo Superior (La Rioja, 599 BC–AD.label: Formativo Superior
Formativo Superior (La Rioja, 599 BC–AD.prose:
[La Rioja, Argentina, 599 BC–AD 900] Formativo Superior. Period definition from Un tipo de estratégia de localización en el oeste riojano (Villa Castelli) — Callegari Adriana , 1991.

The later stage of village farming society in the Argentine Northwest, when settlements grew larger and more clustered, agricultural terraces and irrigation spread, and craft production in ceramics and metal became more specialised. Distinct regional pottery styles emerged, and differences in burial goods hint at growing inequality. These communities are the direct ancestors of the fortified towns and chiefdoms of the following Regional Development period.
Formativo Superior (La Rioja, 599 BC–AD.source: Un tipo de estratégia de localización en el oeste riojano (Villa Castelli)

Periodo Medio (La Rioja, AD 550–AD 900).label: Periodo Medio
Periodo Medio (La Rioja, AD 550–AD 900).prose:
[La Rioja, Argentina, AD 550–AD 900] Periodo Medio. Period definition from Materialización de la Ideología, Ceremonialismo y Complejidad Social. Un Caso de Estudio: La Cuestecilla (Famatina, La Rioja) — Callegari Adriana , 2000.

The time of the Aguada tradition in the Argentine Northwest, when scattered farming villages shared a strikingly uniform art style: black incised and polychrome pottery, cast bronze plaques and discs, and repeated images of felines, shamans and trophy heads. Craft specialisation and metallurgy reached new heights, and the imagery suggests ritual leaders and a widely shared belief system linking valleys across the region.
Periodo Medio (La Rioja, AD 550–AD 900).source: Materialización de la Ideología, Ceremonialismo y Complejidad Social. Un Caso de Estudio: La Cuestecilla (Famatina, La Rioja)

Período Temprano o Formativo (La Rioja,.label: Período Temprano o Formativo
Período Temprano o Formativo (La Rioja,.prose:
[La Rioja, Argentina, 599 BC–AD 550] Período Temprano o Formativo. Period definition from Los Recursos Arqueológicos de Villa Castelli. Dto. General La Madrid, La Rioja — Callegari Adriana , 2007.

Mobile hunting gave way to settled village farming, with irrigation, maize and camelid herding supporting permanent hamlets. Pottery, weaving and early copper metallurgy appear, alongside elaborate burials and long-distance trade in shell, obsidian and hallucinogenic snuff paraphernalia. Everything that later valley societies built on - fields, herds, kin-based villages - takes shape in these centuries.

Periodo Medio o de Integración Regional.node: Periodo Medio o de Integración Regional (La Rioja, AD 550–AD 1100)
Periodo Medio o de Integración Regional.label: Periodo Medio o de Integración Regional
Periodo Medio o de Integración Regional.prose:
[La Rioja, Argentina, AD 550–AD 1100] Periodo Medio o de Integración Regional. Period definition from Los Recursos Arqueológicos de Villa Castelli. Dto. General La Madrid, La Rioja — Callegari Adriana , 2007.

Named for the way distant valley communities came to share one visual language – the feline and shaman imagery of the Aguada style – on pottery, bronze and rock walls. Farming villages grew, irrigation and llama herding expanded, and metalworkers produced fine cast plaques and axes. The unity dissolved towards the end of the period, giving way to more localised, competitive societies.
Periodo Medio o de Integración Regional.source: Los Recursos Arqueológicos de Villa Castelli. Dto. General La Madrid, La Rioja

Período Tardío o de los Desarrollos Regi.node: Período Tardío o de los Desarrollos Regionales (La Rioja, AD 1100–AD 1450)
Período Tardío o de los Desarrollos Regi.label: Período Tardío o de los Desarrollos Regionales
Período Tardío o de los Desarrollos Regi.prose:
[La Rioja, Argentina, AD 1100–AD 1450] Período Tardío o de los Desarrollos Regionales. Period definition from Los Recursos Arqueológicos de Villa Castelli. Dto. General La Madrid, La Rioja — Callegari Adriana , 2007.

After the collapse of the earlier Aguada-style unity, the western valleys broke into competing local chiefdoms with their own pottery styles, among them the Sanagasta and Angualasto traditions. Villages of stone-walled compounds spread across irrigated valley floors, some perched on defensible heights, and dead children were buried in painted ceramic urns beneath house floors. These were the societies the Inca armies later absorbed, and whose descendants the Spanish met as the Diaguita.
Período Tardío o de los Desarrollos Regi.source: Los Recursos Arqueológicos de Villa Castelli. Dto. General La Madrid, La Rioja

Período Hispano Indígena (La Rioja, AD 1.prose:
[La Rioja, Argentina, AD 1535–AD 1700] Período Hispano Indígena. Period definition from Los Recursos Arqueológicos de Villa Castelli. Dto. General La Madrid, La Rioja — Callegari Adriana , 2007.

The contact era, when indigenous communities of the western valleys encountered Spanish settlers, encomenderos and priests. Sites from this time mix local hand-made pottery with glazed European wares, glass beads and iron, and record the resistance, forced resettlement and demographic collapse that ended independent indigenous polities in the region.

Período Temprano (La Rioja, 99 BC–AD 600.prose:
[La Rioja, Argentina, 99 BC–AD 600] Período Temprano. Period definition from Estrellas Riojanas. Geoglifos del norte de la provincia de La Rioja, Argentina — Callegari Adriana , 2019-06.

Farming villages became the normal way of life: people settled in one place, grew maize, beans and squash, herded llamas, made pottery and began working copper and gold. Small clusters of round or rectangular houses spread through the valleys, with grinding stones, carved stone menhirs and the first metal ornaments. The social groundwork for the later valley chiefdoms was laid here.

Tardío 0 o de transición (La Rioja, AD 8.node: Tardío 0 o de transición (La Rioja, AD 800–AD 1350)
Tardío 0 o de transición (La Rioja, AD 8.label: Tardío 0 o de transición
Tardío 0 o de transición (La Rioja, AD 8.prose:
[La Rioja, Argentina, AD 800–AD 1350] Tardío 0 o de transición. Period definition from Arquitectura y asentamiento de las sociedades tardías del sector centro-norte del Valle de Vinchina, La Rioja. — Spengler Gisela , 2017.

A transitional stage in the northwest Argentine sequence, between the collapse of the Aguada-style ceremonial tradition and the emergence of the densely settled Late Period communities. Villages became more dispersed and agricultural, decorated pottery styles simplified and diversified regionally, and the political landscape fragmented into local groups.
Tardío 0 o de transición (La Rioja, AD 8.source: Arquitectura y asentamiento de las sociedades tardías del sector centro-norte del Valle de Vinchina, La Rioja.

Tardío I (La Rioja, AD 1350–AD 1430).label: Tardío I
Tardío I (La Rioja, AD 1350–AD 1430).prose:
[La Rioja, Argentina, AD 1350–AD 1430] Tardío I. Period definition from Arquitectura y asentamiento de las sociedades tardías del sector centro-norte del Valle de Vinchina, La Rioja. — Spengler Gisela , 2017.

The first full Late Period stage in the western valleys, when farming communities clustered into larger nucleated settlements, often on defensible ground, and irrigated fields and terraces were extended across the valley floors. Regional ceramic styles and local chiefly leadership crystallised in the generations just before Inca armies reached the region.
Tardío I (La Rioja, AD 1350–AD 1430).source: Arquitectura y asentamiento de las sociedades tardías del sector centro-norte del Valle de Vinchina, La Rioja.

Tardío II (La Rioja, AD 1430–AD 1636).label: Tardío II
Tardío II (La Rioja, AD 1430–AD 1636).prose:
[La Rioja, Argentina, AD 1430–AD 1636] Tardío II. Period definition from Arquitectura y asentamiento de las sociedades tardías del sector centro-norte del Valle de Vinchina, La Rioja. — Spengler Gisela , 2017.

Covers the incorporation of these valley communities into the Inca empire's southern province and then their violent absorption into the Spanish colonial world. Inca roads, tambos and administrative sites overlay existing settlements, and after the 1530s came encomienda, forced resettlement and the long indigenous resistance in the Calchaquí valleys.
Tardío II (La Rioja, AD 1430–AD 1636).source: Arquitectura y asentamiento de las sociedades tardías del sector centro-norte del Valle de Vinchina, La Rioja.

Período Precerámico (La Rioja, 9999 BC–A.label: Período Precerámico
Período Precerámico (La Rioja, 9999 BC–A.prose:
[La Rioja, Argentina, 9999 BC–AD 600] Período Precerámico. Period definition from Mapa arqueológico de la provincia de La Rioja — Raviña María Gabriela , 1988.

Millennia of hunting and gathering before pottery, from the first peopling of the region through Holocene camelid hunters using caves, rockshelters and open camps. Stone projectile points, grinding tools and vivid rock art record shifting prey and expanding social networks. Towards its end, the taming of llamas and cultivation of highland crops began the slow move to settled village life.
Período Precerámico (La Rioja, 9999 BC–A.source: Mapa arqueológico de la provincia de La Rioja

Formativo Inferior (La Rioja, 599 BC–AD.label: Formativo Inferior
Formativo Inferior (La Rioja, 599 BC–AD.prose:
[La Rioja, Argentina, 599 BC–AD 1000] Formativo Inferior. Period definition from Mapa arqueológico de la provincia de La Rioja — Raviña María Gabriela , 1988.

Settled agricultural life in the valleys and eastern piedmont of the Argentine Northwest, based on maize, quinoa and camelid herding. Communities lived in small dispersed hamlets with round stone-walled houses and cultivation plots, made incised and painted pottery, and worked copper and gold. Regional exchange networks carried pottery styles, obsidian and Amazonian and Pacific goods across the Andes.
Formativo Inferior (La Rioja, 599 BC–AD.source: Mapa arqueológico de la provincia de La Rioja

Formativo Superior (La Rioja, AD 600–AD.label: Formativo Superior
Formativo Superior (La Rioja, AD 600–AD.prose:
[La Rioja, Argentina, AD 600–AD 1000] Formativo Superior. Period definition from Mapa arqueológico de la provincia de La Rioja — Raviña María Gabriela , 1988.

The later stage of village farming society in the Argentine Northwest, when settlements grew larger and more clustered, agricultural terraces and irrigation spread, and craft production in ceramics and metal became more specialised. Distinct regional pottery styles emerged, and differences in burial goods hint at growing inequality. These communities are the direct ancestors of the fortified towns and chiefdoms of the following Regional Development period.
Formativo Superior (La Rioja, AD 600–AD.source: Mapa arqueológico de la provincia de La Rioja

Desarrollos Regionales (La Rioja, AD 100.label: Desarrollos Regionales
Desarrollos Regionales (La Rioja, AD 100.prose:
[La Rioja, Argentina, AD 1000–AD 1470] Desarrollos Regionales. Period definition from Mapa arqueológico de la provincia de La Rioja — Raviña María Gabriela , 1988.

After the Tiwanaku-influenced horizon faded, the valleys and highlands of northwest Argentina broke into a mosaic of local polities, best known through the Santa María and related groups. Communities clustered in dense, walled hilltop settlements — pukaras — with terraced fields below, buried their dead in painted urns, and worked copper and bronze. Warfare and competition between chiefdoms shaped the landscape until Inca armies absorbed the region in the late fifteenth century.
Desarrollos Regionales (La Rioja, AD 100.source: Mapa arqueológico de la provincia de La Rioja

Período Inka (La Rioja, AD 1470–AD 1535).label: Período Inka
Período Inka (La Rioja, AD 1470–AD 1535).prose:
[La Rioja, Argentina, AD 1470–AD 1535] Período Inka. Period definition from Mapa arqueológico de la provincia de La Rioja — Raviña María Gabriela , 1988.

Salta's valleys and high puna became part of Collasuyu, crossed by the Qhapaq Ñan and dotted with tambos, agricultural terraces and administrative sites. The most spectacular legacy is high-altitude ceremonial architecture, including the summit sanctuaries where children were sacrificed and preserved by the cold. Local communities supplied labour and were sometimes uprooted and resettled to serve the state.
Período Inka (La Rioja, AD 1470–AD 1535).source: Mapa arqueológico de la provincia de La Rioja

Período Hispano Indígena (La Rioja, AD 1.label: Período Hispano Indígena
Período Hispano Indígena (La Rioja, AD 1.prose:
[La Rioja, Argentina, AD 1535–AD 1660] Período Hispano Indígena. Period definition from Mapa arqueológico de la provincia de La Rioja — Raviña María Gabriela , 1988.

The contact era, when indigenous communities of the western valleys encountered Spanish settlers, encomenderos and priests. Sites from this time mix local hand-made pottery with glazed European wares, glass beads and iron, and record the resistance, forced resettlement and demographic collapse that ended independent indigenous polities in the region.
Período Hispano Indígena (La Rioja, AD 1.source: Mapa arqueológico de la provincia de La Rioja

Período Tardío o de Desarrollos Regional.node: Período Tardío o de Desarrollos Regionales (La Rioja, AD 1000–AD 1480)
Período Tardío o de Desarrollos Regional.label: Período Tardío o de Desarrollos Regionales
Período Tardío o de Desarrollos Regional.prose:
[La Rioja, Argentina, AD 1000–AD 1480] Período Tardío o de Desarrollos Regionales. Period definition from Arte rupestre entre las sierras y Los Llanos riojanos: localidad arqueológica Palancho — Falchi María Pía , 2011-12-01.

Local chiefdoms in the valleys built dense villages, extensive field systems and hilltop refuges, each with recognisable pottery and burial customs. Long-distance caravan traffic kept them supplied with obsidian, metals and altiplano goods, while competition over land and water drove fortification. Their leaders were the intermediaries through whom the Inca later governed.
Período Tardío o de Desarrollos Regional.source: Arte rupestre entre las sierras y Los Llanos riojanos: localidad arqueológica Palancho

Período de Integración Regional (La Rioj.node: Período de Integración Regional (La Rioja, AD 550–AD 1000)
Período de Integración Regional (La Rioj.label: Período de Integración Regional
Período de Integración Regional (La Rioj.prose:
[La Rioja, Argentina, AD 550–AD 1000] Período de Integración Regional. Period definition from Arte rupestre en la localidad arqueológica El Chiflón- Punta de la Greda (Parque Natural Provincial El Chiflón, La Rioja) en su contexto regional. — Falchi María Pía , 2017.

Farming villages across the western valleys grew denser and more organised, tied together by shared styles of decorated pottery, textiles and cast bronze. This is the horizon of the Aguada tradition, whose black incised vessels carry stylised feline and warrior imagery that suggests shamanic ritual and an emerging elite. Metallurgy, llama herding and irrigation agriculture all became firmly established, setting the economic base for the later chiefdoms of the region.
Período de Integración Regional (La Rioj.source: Arte rupestre en la localidad arqueológica El Chiflón- Punta de la Greda (Parque Natural Provincial El Chiflón, La Rioja) en su contexto regional.

Período de Desarrollos Regionales (La Ri.node: Período de Desarrollos Regionales (La Rioja, AD 1000–AD 1450)
Período de Desarrollos Regionales (La Ri.label: Período de Desarrollos Regionales
Período de Desarrollos Regionales (La Ri.prose:
[La Rioja, Argentina, AD 1000–AD 1450] Período de Desarrollos Regionales. Period definition from Arte rupestre en la localidad arqueológica El Chiflón- Punta de la Greda (Parque Natural Provincial El Chiflón, La Rioja) en su contexto regional. — Falchi María Pía , 2017.

Sharply distinct local traditions emerged across the valleys, each with its own pottery, architecture and territory. Settlements grew into agglomerated stone towns with terraced fields and defensive walls, and the dead were interred with painted urns and bronze goods. Interpretation of the period turns on whether these were warring chiefdoms or looser village confederations.
Período de Desarrollos Regionales (La Ri.source: Arte rupestre en la localidad arqueológica El Chiflón- Punta de la Greda (Parque Natural Provincial El Chiflón, La Rioja) en su contexto regional.

Late Period (La Rioja, AD 900–AD 1470).label: Late Period
Late Period (La Rioja, AD 900–AD 1470).prose:
[La Rioja, Argentina, AD 900–AD 1470] Late Period. Period definition from Temporal dynamics of La Rioja village landscapes, Argentina — Cahiza Pablo , 2021-10.

Egyptian kings ruled again from Sais after the Assyrian withdrawal, reviving Old Kingdom art and burial customs in a deliberate archaising style, while Greek and Carian mercenaries and traders settled in the Delta at Naukratis. Persian conquest in 525 BC made Egypt a satrapy, interrupted by brief native dynasties, until Alexander took the country in 332 BC. The period is where Egypt becomes fully entangled with the Mediterranean world that would later record its history.
Late Period (La Rioja, AD 900–AD 1470).source: Temporal dynamics of La Rioja village landscapes, Argentina

Período de Desarrollos Regionales o Agro.node: Período de Desarrollos Regionales o Agroalfarero Tardío (La Rioja, AD 1000–AD 1470)
Período de Desarrollos Regionales o Agro.label: Período de Desarrollos Regionales o Agroalfarero Tardío
Período de Desarrollos Regionales o Agro.prose:
[La Rioja, Argentina, AD 1000–AD 1470] Período de Desarrollos Regionales o Agroalfarero Tardío. Period definition from Análisis ceramológicos de la Tambería de Guandacol (dpto. Felipe Varela, provincia de La Rioja). Avances para el conocimiento de las prácticas de manufactura. — Carosio Sebastián , 2011.

Farming communities in the western valleys reached their greatest extent, irrigating fields, terracing slopes and living in dense stone-built settlements. Distinct regional ceramic traditions and infant urn burials mark the period, along with widespread copper-bronze metallurgy. Growing evidence of conflict - walls, lookouts, weapons - accompanies the rise of local chiefly authority.
Período de Desarrollos Regionales o Agro.source: Análisis ceramológicos de la Tambería de Guandacol (dpto. Felipe Varela, provincia de La Rioja). Avances para el conocimiento de las prácticas de manufactura.

Desarrollos Regionales (La Rioja, AD 120.prose:
[La Rioja, Argentina, AD 1200–AD 1470] Desarrollos Regionales. Period definition from Cadena operativa y tradición tecnológica cerámica durante Desarrollos Regionales en el extremo sur del Noroeste Argentino (ca. 1200-1470 AD). Un aporte desde el estilo tecnológico Sanagasta/Angualasto del sitio Tambería de Guandacol (Provincia de La Rioja). — Carosio Sebastián , 2017.

Communities clustered in dense, walled hilltop settlements — pukaras — with terraced fields below, buried their dead in painted urns, and worked copper and bronze. Warfare and competition between chiefdoms shaped the landscape until Inca armies absorbed the region in the late fifteenth century.

Período de Dominio Incaico Regional (La.node: Período de Dominio Incaico Regional (La Rioja, AD 1470–AD 1533)
Período de Dominio Incaico Regional (La.label: Período de Dominio Incaico Regional
Período de Dominio Incaico Regional (La.prose:
[La Rioja, Argentina, AD 1470–AD 1533] Período de Dominio Incaico Regional. Period definition from Estudios preliminares de Pigmentos en Cerámicas Arqueológicas Tardías Mediante Microscopio de Barrido Electrónico (MEB-EDS). Aportes para el Conocimiento Tecnológico Alfarero de las Sociedades de la Tambería de Guandacol (Oeste de la Provincial de La Rioja). — Carosio Sebastián , 2017.

Imperial administration reached the western valleys, imposing tribute in labour, redirecting agriculture and mining, and tying local settlements into the Andean road network. Local pottery continued but adopted imperial shapes and motifs, evidence of negotiated rather than total control. The arrangement lasted only decades before Spanish forces arrived.
Período de Dominio Incaico Regional (La.source: Estudios preliminares de Pigmentos en Cerámicas Arqueológicas Tardías Mediante Microscopio de Barrido Electrónico (MEB-EDS). Aportes para el Conocimiento Tecnológico Alfarero de las Sociedades de la Tambería de Guandacol (Oeste de la Provincial de La Rioja).

Período de Desarrollos Regionales (La Ri.prose:

Sharply distinct local traditions emerged across the valleys, each with its own pottery, architecture and territory. Settlements grew into agglomerated stone towns with terraced fields and defensive walls, and the dead were interred with painted urns and bronze goods. Interpretation of the period turns on whether these were warring chiefdoms or looser village confederations.

Período del Dominio Inca (La Rioja, AD 1.node: Período del Dominio Inca (La Rioja, AD 1480–AD 1535)
Período del Dominio Inca (La Rioja, AD 1.label: Período del Dominio Inca
Período del Dominio Inca (La Rioja, AD 1.prose:
[La Rioja, Argentina, AD 1480–AD 1535] Período del Dominio Inca. Period definition from Patrimonio arqueológico en el Valle de Guandacol (provincia de La Rioja, Argentina): Estudios exploratorios de los procesos de alteración natural y cultural.  — Carosio Sebastián , 2017.

Inca officials incorporated the valleys into the empire, taking control of mineral sources, imposing labour tribute and installing garrisons and storage facilities along the road system. Imperial pottery and architecture appear alongside continuing local traditions, and high-altitude mountain shrines in the region attest to state-sponsored ritual. The arrangement collapsed with the Spanish invasion, though Inca administrative geography shaped how the colonisers first understood the area.
Período del Dominio Inca (La Rioja, AD 1.source: Patrimonio arqueológico en el Valle de Guandacol (provincia de La Rioja, Argentina): Estudios exploratorios de los procesos de alteración natural y cultural.

Periodo Agroalfarero Tardío (La Rioja, A.label: Periodo Agroalfarero Tardío
Periodo Agroalfarero Tardío (La Rioja, A.prose: [La Rioja, Argentina, AD 1200–AD 1470] Periodo Agroalfarero Tardío. Period definition from Una aproximación a las trayectorias estilísticas cerámicas del valle de Guandacol (Provincia de La Rioja): Continuidades y rupturas entre los siglos XIII y XVIII. — Carosio Sebastián , 2017.
Periodo Agroalfarero Tardío (La Rioja, A.source: Una aproximación a las trayectorias estilísticas cerámicas del valle de Guandacol (Provincia de La Rioja): Continuidades y rupturas entre los siglos XIII y XVIII.

Dominación Inca (La Rioja, AD 1470–AD 15.label: Dominación Inca
Dominación Inca (La Rioja, AD 1470–AD 15.prose:
[La Rioja, Argentina, AD 1470–AD 1535] Dominación Inca. Period definition from Una aproximación a las trayectorias estilísticas cerámicas del valle de Guandacol (Provincia de La Rioja): Continuidades y rupturas entre los siglos XIII y XVIII. — Carosio Sebastián , 2017.

Inca armies pushed south into the valleys of northwest Argentina, folding them into Collasuyu, the empire's southern quarter. The state built roads, waystations and administrative centres, moved populations of resettled colonists (mitmaqkuna) to work fields and mines, and imposed labour tribute on local chiefdoms. Traces survive as hilltop sanctuaries, stretches of the Qhapaq Ñan and imperial-style pottery mixed into local wares. It lasted only a few decades before Spanish forces arrived.
Dominación Inca (La Rioja, AD 1470–AD 15.source: Una aproximación a las trayectorias estilísticas cerámicas del valle de Guandacol (Provincia de La Rioja): Continuidades y rupturas entre los siglos XIII y XVIII.

fase transicional del Formativo a los De.node: fase transicional del Formativo a los Desarrollos Regionales (La Rioja, AD 600–AD 1200)
fase transicional del Formativo a los De.label: fase transicional del Formativo a los Desarrollos Regionales
fase transicional del Formativo a los De.prose:
[La Rioja, Argentina, AD 600–AD 1200] fase transicional del Formativo a los Desarrollos Regionales. Period definition from Una aproximación a las trayectorias estilísticas cerámicas del valle de Guandacol (Provincia de La Rioja): Continuidades y rupturas entre los siglos XIII y XVIII. — Carosio Sebastián , 2017.

Farming villages of the Argentine Northwest, long organised around small irrigated plots and llama herding, gave way to denser and more hierarchical settlement, with distinctive regional ceramic styles and, in this stretch of the Andes, the spread of Aguada iconography of felines and warriors. Metallurgy in copper and bronze became a marker of status, and communities began fortifying and clustering in defensible spots. The pattern of competing local polities set here is what the Inca later found and absorbed.
fase transicional del Formativo a los De.source: Una aproximación a las trayectorias estilísticas cerámicas del valle de Guandacol (Provincia de La Rioja): Continuidades y rupturas entre los siglos XIII y XVIII.

Período Intermedio Tardío o Período de l.node: Período Intermedio Tardío o Período de los Desarrollos Regionales (La Rioja, AD 1000–AD 1430)
Período Intermedio Tardío o Período de l.label: Período Intermedio Tardío o Período de los Desarrollos Regionales
Período Intermedio Tardío o Período de l.prose:
[La Rioja, Argentina, AD 1000–AD 1430] Período Intermedio Tardío o Período de los Desarrollos Regionales. Period definition from Primeros resultados del estudio bioarqueológico de restos óseos humanos de La Rioja (Argentina). — Gheggi María Soledad , 2019.

With no unifying horizon style, communities in the western valleys developed their own pottery traditions, settlement layouts and leadership. Farming spread across terraced slopes and irrigated valley floors, supporting larger, more nucleated villages, while fortified sites and weapon-related finds point to conflict between groups. These local polities were the societies the Inca later absorbed.
Período Intermedio Tardío o Período de l.source: Primeros resultados del estudio bioarqueológico de restos óseos humanos de La Rioja (Argentina).

Período de los Desarrollos Regionales (L.node: Período de los Desarrollos Regionales (La Rioja, AD 1100–AD 1470)
Período de los Desarrollos Regionales (L.label: Período de los Desarrollos Regionales
Período de los Desarrollos Regionales (L.prose:
[La Rioja, Argentina, AD 1100–AD 1470] Período de los Desarrollos Regionales. Period definition from Prospecciones arqueológicas en el valle de Guandacol, depto. Felipe Varela, La Rioja. — Iniesta María Lourdes , 2013.

With the collapse of the earlier integrative traditions, communities fragmented into distinct local groups, each with its own pottery styles and territory. Settlements moved to defensible spurs and hilltops, walls and lookouts multiplied, and skeletal trauma points to endemic raiding over land and water. These were the densely populated valley chiefdoms that the Inca armies would later conquer and reorganise.
Período de los Desarrollos Regionales (L.source: Prospecciones arqueológicas en el valle de Guandacol, depto. Felipe Varela, La Rioja.

Período de Dominación Inca (La Rioja, AD.node: Período de Dominación Inca (La Rioja, AD 1470–AD 1536)
Período de Dominación Inca (La Rioja, AD.label: Período de Dominación Inca
Período de Dominación Inca (La Rioja, AD.prose:
[La Rioja, Argentina, AD 1470–AD 1536] Período de Dominación Inca. Period definition from Prospecciones arqueológicas en el valle de Guandacol, depto. Felipe Varela, La Rioja. — Iniesta María Lourdes , 2013.

Inca armies and administrators extended Tawantinsuyu into the western valleys, linking them by road to Cuzco and reorganising labour for mining and farming. Storehouses, waystations and high-altitude shrines appear alongside existing local settlements, and communities were sometimes resettled as mitmaqkuna. Imperial control lasted barely two generations before Spanish invasion dismantled it.
Período de Dominación Inca (La Rioja, AD.source: Prospecciones arqueológicas en el valle de Guandacol, depto. Felipe Varela, La Rioja.

Período de los Desarrollos Regionales o.node: Período de los Desarrollos Regionales o Agroalfarero Tardío (La Rioja, AD 1000–AD 1480)
Período de los Desarrollos Regionales o.label: Período de los Desarrollos Regionales o Agroalfarero Tardío
Período de los Desarrollos Regionales o.prose:
[La Rioja, Argentina, AD 1000–AD 1480] Período de los Desarrollos Regionales o Agroalfarero Tardío. Period definition from Investigaciones arqueológicas sobre las sociedades tardías del Valle de Guandacol (Departamento Felipe Varela, oeste de La Rioja): Espacio, estilos tecnológicos cerámicos y cronología — Iniesta María Lourdes , 2014.

Populations grew and clustered into large agglomerated villages surrounded by terraced fields and irrigation canals, each region developing its own recognisable ceramic style. Fortified hilltop sites and evidence of violence suggest competition between neighbouring polities, while long-distance exchange in metal and hallucinogenic plants continued. This mosaic of independent valley societies was the political landscape the Inca encountered.
Período de los Desarrollos Regionales o.source: Investigaciones arqueológicas sobre las sociedades tardías del Valle de Guandacol (Departamento Felipe Varela, oeste de La Rioja): Espacio, estilos tecnológicos cerámicos y cronología

Período Tardío (La Rioja, AD 1300–AD 144.label: Período Tardío
Período Tardío (La Rioja, AD 1300–AD 144.prose:
[La Rioja, Argentina, AD 1300–AD 1440] Período Tardío. Period definition from Configuración del paisaje tardío (ca. 1300-1440 d.c.) en el Valle de Guandacol (Felipe Varela, oeste de la provincia de La Rioja) — Iniesta María Lourdes , 2016.

Following the end of the Middle Period, the Northwest fragmented into competing local polities with their own painted ceramics, cemeteries and territories. Agriculture intensified on terraces and irrigated land, populations concentrated in large villages, and fortified pukaras multiplied on ridges and hilltops. These chiefdoms were still expanding when the Inca arrived.

Agriculture intensified on terraces and irrigated land, populations concentrated in large villages, and fortified pukaras multiplied on ridges and hilltops. These chiefdoms were still expanding when the Inca arrived.

Período de Dominación Incaica (La Rioja,.node: Período de Dominación Incaica (La Rioja, AD 1475–AD 1536)
Período de Dominación Incaica (La Rioja,.label: Período de Dominación Incaica
Período de Dominación Incaica (La Rioja,.prose:
[La Rioja, Argentina, AD 1475–AD 1536] Período de Dominación Incaica. Period definition from Investigaciones arqueológicas en la sierra de Famatina (Prov. de La Rioja) — Schobinger Juan , 1966.

The southern reach of Tawantinsuyu, administered through the road system, provincial centres and the resettlement of labourers far from their homelands. The Inca were drawn by metals - copper, silver, gold - and by the region's farmland, and left mountaintop sanctuaries at extraordinary altitudes. Their rule collapsed with the Spanish capture of Atahualpa, leaving local groups to face a new conqueror.
Período de Dominación Incaica (La Rioja,.source: Investigaciones arqueológicas en la sierra de Famatina (Prov. de La Rioja)

Cultura de Los Morrillos (San Juan, 5899.node: Cultura de Los Morrillos (San Juan, 5899 BC–2199 BC)
Cultura de Los Morrillos (San Juan, 5899.label: Cultura de Los Morrillos
Cultura de Los Morrillos (San Juan, 5899.prose:
[San Juan, Argentina, 5899 BC–2199 BC] Cultura de Los Morrillos. Period definition from Textilería incaica en la provincia de San Juan: Los ajuares de los cerros Mercedario, Toro y Tambillos — Catalina Teresa Michieli, 1990.

Hunter-gatherers of the high Andean valleys who camped in rock shelters, hunted guanaco and vicuña, and left painted and engraved rock art on the cliffs around their sites. The exceptionally dry conditions preserved wooden tools, cordage and burials, making these caves one of the fullest records of archaic life in the southern Andes.
Cultura de Los Morrillos (San Juan, 5899.source: Textilería incaica en la provincia de San Juan: Los ajuares de los cerros Mercedario, Toro y Tambillos

Cultura de Ansilta (San Juan, 1799 BC–AD.label: Cultura de Ansilta
Cultura de Ansilta (San Juan, 1799 BC–AD.prose:
[San Juan, Argentina, 1799 BC–AD 550] Cultura de Ansilta. Period definition from Textilería incaica en la provincia de San Juan: Los ajuares de los cerros Mercedario, Toro y Tambillos — Catalina Teresa Michieli, 1990.

Early cultivators of the high western Andes who combined hunting guanaco with small-scale gardening of maize and squash, living in caves and rock shelters. Their dry burial sites have preserved extraordinary twined textiles and netted bags, giving an unusually detailed picture of clothing and craft in a period that otherwise leaves little behind.
Cultura de Ansilta (San Juan, 1799 BC–AD.source: Textilería incaica en la provincia de San Juan: Los ajuares de los cerros Mercedario, Toro y Tambillos

Fase Cultural Punta del Barro (San Juan,.label: Fase Cultural Punta del Barro
Fase Cultural Punta del Barro (San Juan,.prose: [San Juan, Argentina, AD 50–AD 550] Fase Cultural Punta del Barro. Period definition from Textilería incaica en la provincia de San Juan: Los ajuares de los cerros Mercedario, Toro y Tambillos — Catalina Teresa Michieli, 1990.

Cultura Angualasto (San Juan, AD 1200–AD.label: Cultura Angualasto
Cultura Angualasto (San Juan, AD 1200–AD.prose:
[San Juan, Argentina, AD 1200–AD 1450] Cultura Angualasto. Period definition from Nuevas evidencias textiles del período tardío en el valle fronterizo de Iglesia (San Juan, Argentina) y sus relaciones con el norte de Chile y noroeste argentino — Catalina Teresa Michieli, 2001.

Farmers of the arid Andean valleys who irrigated maize and beans, stored grain in stone silos, and buried their dead in dry caves where textiles and basketry survive remarkably well. Their distinctive plain and incised pottery marks the last centuries of local independence before Inca armies absorbed the region.
Cultura Angualasto (San Juan, AD 1200–AD.source: Nuevas evidencias textiles del período tardío en el valle fronterizo de Iglesia (San Juan, Argentina) y sus relaciones con el norte de Chile y noroeste argentino

Cultura de la Aguada (San Juan, AD 650–A.node: Cultura de la Aguada (San Juan, AD 650–AD 1050)
Cultura de la Aguada (San Juan, AD 650–A.label: Cultura de la Aguada
Cultura de la Aguada (San Juan, AD 650–A.prose:
[San Juan, Argentina, AD 650–AD 1050] Cultura de la Aguada. Period definition from Textilería Aguada en el Valle de Iglesia, provincia de San Juan — Catalina Teresa Michieli, 2001.

Known for dark, polished pottery and bronze plaques covered in feline and jaguar-man imagery, this was the great artistic tradition of northwest Argentina. Its craftsmen mastered metallurgy, its iconography suggests shamanic ritual and human sacrifice, and its motifs echo those of Tiwanaku far to the north, hinting at long-distance religious connections across the Andes.
Cultura de la Aguada (San Juan, AD 650–A.source: Textilería Aguada en el Valle de Iglesia, provincia de San Juan

Período Tardío (Catamarca, AD 900–AD 120.label: Período Tardío
Período Tardío (Catamarca, AD 900–AD 120.prose:
[Valle de Abaucán, Catamarca, Argentina, AD 900–AD 1200] Período Tardío. Period definition from  Identificacion y Analisis de Pigmentos y Pinturas en Ceramicas Arqueológicas Sanagasta (ca. 900 1200 AD) e Inka (ca. 1480 1532 AD) a traves de MEB-EDS y Microespectroscopia de Raman (Abaucan, Tinogasta, Catamarca, Argentina). — de La Fuente Guillermo Adrián, 2010.

Following the end of the Middle Period, the Northwest fragmented into competing local polities with their own painted ceramics, cemeteries and territories. Agriculture intensified on terraces and irrigated land, populations concentrated in large villages, and fortified pukaras multiplied on ridges and hilltops. These chiefdoms were still expanding when the Inca arrived.
Período Tardío (Catamarca, AD 900–AD 120.source: Identificacion y Analisis de Pigmentos y Pinturas en Ceramicas Arqueológicas Sanagasta (ca. 900 1200 AD) e Inka (ca. 1480 1532 AD) a traves de MEB-EDS y Microespectroscopia de Raman (Abaucan, Tinogasta, Catamarca, Argentina).

Período Agroalfarero Tardío (Catamarca,.label: Período Agroalfarero Tardío
Período Agroalfarero Tardío (Catamarca,.prose:
[Valle de Abaucán, Catamarca, Argentina, AD 900–AD 1450] Período Agroalfarero Tardío. Period definition from  Identificacion y Analisis de Pigmentos y Pinturas en Ceramicas Arqueológicas Sanagasta (ca. 900 1200 AD) e Inka (ca. 1480 1532 AD) a traves de MEB-EDS y Microespectroscopia de Raman (Abaucan, Tinogasta, Catamarca, Argentina). — de La Fuente Guillermo Adrián, 2010.

After the collapse of the Aguada tradition, the valleys of the northwest filled with sizeable, densely packed settlements built of stone, many of them fortified hilltop pukaras overlooking terraced fields. Distinct regional styles emerged, such as the Santa María funerary urns painted with staring anthropomorphic faces and the Belén ceramics, and bronze working reached its peak. Warfare between valley polities was common, and the era closed with their incorporation into the Inca empire.
Período Agroalfarero Tardío (Catamarca,.source: Identificacion y Analisis de Pigmentos y Pinturas en Ceramicas Arqueológicas Sanagasta (ca. 900 1200 AD) e Inka (ca. 1480 1532 AD) a traves de MEB-EDS y Microespectroscopia de Raman (Abaucan, Tinogasta, Catamarca, Argentina).

Período Inka (Catamarca, AD 1480–AD 1532.label: Período Inka
Período Inka (Catamarca, AD 1480–AD 1532.prose:
[Valle de Abaucán, Catamarca, Argentina, AD 1480–AD 1532] Período Inka. Period definition from Cronología por Termoluminiscencia (TL) de Cerámicas pertenecientes al Horizonte Inka (ca. AD 1480-AD 1532) y el Período Tardío (ca. AD 900-AD 1450) en el sur del Valle de Abaucán: Análisis Comparativos y Resultados Preliminares (Tinogasta, Catamarca). — de La Fuente Guillermo Adrián, 2010.

Salta's valleys and high puna became part of Collasuyu, crossed by the Qhapaq Ñan and dotted with tambos, agricultural terraces and administrative sites. The most spectacular legacy is high-altitude ceremonial architecture, including the summit sanctuaries where children were sacrificed and preserved by the cold. Local communities supplied labour and were sometimes uprooted and resettled to serve the state.
Período Inka (Catamarca, AD 1480–AD 1532.source: Cronología por Termoluminiscencia (TL) de Cerámicas pertenecientes al Horizonte Inka (ca. AD 1480-AD 1532) y el Período Tardío (ca. AD 900-AD 1450) en el sur del Valle de Abaucán: Análisis Comparativos y Resultados Preliminares (Tinogasta, Catamarca).

Late Period (Catamarca, AD 900–AD 1450).label: Late Period
Late Period (Catamarca, AD 900–AD 1450).prose:
[Valle de Abaucán, Catamarca, Argentina, AD 900–AD 1450] Late Period. Period definition from Urns, Bowls, and Ollas: Pottery-Making Practices and Technical Identity in the Southern Andes During the Late Period (ca. A.D. 900—A.D. 1450) (Catamarca, Northwestern Argentine Region, Argentina) — Guillermo A. De La Fuente, 2011-06.

Egyptian kings ruled again from Sais after the Assyrian withdrawal, reviving Old Kingdom art and burial customs in a deliberate archaising style, while Greek and Carian mercenaries and traders settled in the Delta at Naukratis. Persian conquest in 525 BC made Egypt a satrapy, interrupted by brief native dynasties, until Alexander took the country in 332 BC. The period is where Egypt becomes fully entangled with the Mediterranean world that would later record its history.
Late Period (Catamarca, AD 900–AD 1450).source: Urns, Bowls, and Ollas: Pottery-Making Practices and Technical Identity in the Southern Andes During the Late Period (ca. A.D. 900—A.D. 1450) (Catamarca, Northwestern Argentine Region, Argentina)

Inca Period (Catamarca, AD 1480–AD 1530).label: Inca Period
Inca Period (Catamarca, AD 1480–AD 1530).prose:
[Valle de Abaucán, Catamarca, Argentina, AD 1480–AD 1530] Inca Period. Period definition from Chemical and Petrographic Analysis of Pre-Hispanic Pottery from the Southern Abaucán Valley, Catamarca, Argentina — de La Fuente Guillermo Adrián, 2014-02-16.

Cusco's armies incorporated the valleys of the Calchaquí and the Andean south into Qollasuyu, installing garrisons, administrative sites and roads linked to the great highland highway. Local communities kept their own pottery and burial customs while paying labour tribute and, in places, being moved wholesale as mitmaqkuna colonists. Mining and metalworking in the region were of particular interest to the state.
Inca Period (Catamarca, AD 1480–AD 1530).source: Chemical and Petrographic Analysis of Pre-Hispanic Pottery from the Southern Abaucán Valley, Catamarca, Argentina

Período Tardío Inicial (Catamarca, AD 90.label: Período Tardío Inicial
Período Tardío Inicial (Catamarca, AD 90.prose:
[Valle de Abaucán, Catamarca, Argentina, AD 900–AD 1300] Período Tardío Inicial. Period definition from Prácticas alfareras, tecnología y cronología durante los períodos Tardío e Inca en el sector meridional del Valle de Abaucán. Tradiciones y rupturas: el caso de Costa de Reyes N°5 (Tinogasta, Catamarca, Argentina) — Vera Sergio David, 2019-03.

The opening phase of the late sequence, when Aguada-era patterns gave way to new regional communities in the Catamarca valleys. Settlements grew more nucleated, agricultural terracing and irrigation expanded, and distinctive local pottery traditions such as early Belén wares took shape. Signs of defence and conflict begin to appear in settlement locations.
Período Tardío Inicial (Catamarca, AD 90.source: Prácticas alfareras, tecnología y cronología durante los períodos Tardío e Inca en el sector meridional del Valle de Abaucán. Tradiciones y rupturas: el caso de Costa de Reyes N°5 (Tinogasta, Catamarca, Argentina)

Período Intermedio Tardío (Catamarca, AD.label: Período Intermedio Tardío
Período Intermedio Tardío (Catamarca, AD.prose:
[Valle de Abaucán, Catamarca, Argentina, AD 1300–AD 1480] Período Intermedio Tardío. Period definition from Prácticas alfareras, tecnología y cronología durante los períodos Tardío e Inca en el sector meridional del Valle de Abaucán. Tradiciones y rupturas: el caso de Costa de Reyes N°5 (Tinogasta, Catamarca, Argentina) — Vera Sergio David, 2019-03.

After the collapse of the Middle Period order, populations in the valleys built dense settlements, extensive terraced fields and irrigation systems, and increasingly clustered in defensible hilltop pukaras. Regional identities are visible in distinct painted pottery styles and in urn burials of infants beneath house floors. The rising evidence for warfare and territorial competition sets the stage for Inca conquest.
Período Intermedio Tardío (Catamarca, AD.source: Prácticas alfareras, tecnología y cronología durante los períodos Tardío e Inca en el sector meridional del Valle de Abaucán. Tradiciones y rupturas: el caso de Costa de Reyes N°5 (Tinogasta, Catamarca, Argentina)

Período Tardío-Inca (Catamarca, AD 1480–.label: Período Tardío-Inca
Período Tardío-Inca (Catamarca, AD 1480–.prose:
[Valle de Abaucán, Catamarca, Argentina, AD 1480–AD 1600] Período Tardío-Inca. Period definition from Prácticas alfareras, tecnología y cronología durante los períodos Tardío e Inca en el sector meridional del Valle de Abaucán. Tradiciones y rupturas: el caso de Costa de Reyes N°5 (Tinogasta, Catamarca, Argentina) — Vera Sergio David, 2019-03.

The last stretch of independent valley life overlapped with, and was overtaken by, imperial rule and then Spanish invasion. Inca administrative sites, road segments and storehouses were grafted onto existing Belén and Santa María settlements, and local potters began mixing imperial shapes and designs into their own work. The sequence ends in the long indigenous resistance of the Calchaquí Wars.
Período Tardío-Inca (Catamarca, AD 1480–.source: Prácticas alfareras, tecnología y cronología durante los períodos Tardío e Inca en el sector meridional del Valle de Abaucán. Tradiciones y rupturas: el caso de Costa de Reyes N°5 (Tinogasta, Catamarca, Argentina)

Período Agroalfarero Tardío (Catamarca,.prose:
[Valle de Abaucán, Catamarca, Argentina, AD 900–AD 1450] Período Agroalfarero Tardío. Period definition from Prácticas alfareras, tecnología y cronología durante los períodos Tardío e Inca en el sector meridional del Valle de Abaucán. Tradiciones y rupturas: el caso de Costa de Reyes N°5 (Tinogasta, Catamarca, Argentina) — Vera Sergio David, 2019-03.

After the collapse of the Aguada tradition, the valleys of the northwest filled with sizeable, densely packed settlements built of stone, many of them fortified hilltop pukaras overlooking terraced fields. Distinct regional styles emerged, such as the Santa María funerary urns painted with staring anthropomorphic faces and the Belén ceramics, and bronze working reached its peak. Warfare between valley polities was common, and the era closed with their incorporation into the Inca empire.

Período Agroalfarero Temprano (Catamarca.label: Período Agroalfarero Temprano
Período Agroalfarero Temprano (Catamarca.prose:
[Valle de Abaucán, Catamarca, Argentina, 199 BC–AD 600] Período Agroalfarero Temprano. Period definition from Aproximación a los estudios de traza. El caso de las urnas funerarias estilo Saujil (Catamarca, noroeste argentino). — Vera Sergio David, 2018.

The first settled farming villages of northwest Argentina, when maize agriculture, llama herding and pottery making took hold across valleys and puna. Communities such as those at Tafí built circular stone house compounds around patios, carved standing stone monoliths, and produced modelled and painted ceramics, while early copper and gold work appears in graves. Populations remained small and dispersed, without the fortifications and towns of later centuries.
Período Agroalfarero Temprano (Catamarca.source: Aproximación a los estudios de traza. El caso de las urnas funerarias estilo Saujil (Catamarca, noroeste argentino).

Período Hispano Indígena (Catamarca, AD.label: Período Hispano Indígena
Período Hispano Indígena (Catamarca, AD.prose:
[Valle de Abaucán, Catamarca, Argentina, AD 1535–AD 1690] Período Hispano Indígena. Period definition from Ultimas etapas del desarrollo cultural indigena (1480-1690) en el valle de Abaucan, Tinogasta, Provincia de Catamarca — Sempé de Gómez Llanes María Carlota, 1973.

The contact era, when indigenous communities of the western valleys encountered Spanish settlers, encomenderos and priests. Sites from this time mix local hand-made pottery with glazed European wares, glass beads and iron, and record the resistance, forced resettlement and demographic collapse that ended independent indigenous polities in the region.
Período Hispano Indígena (Catamarca, AD.source: Ultimas etapas del desarrollo cultural indigena (1480-1690) en el valle de Abaucan, Tinogasta, Provincia de Catamarca
